τε τῇ Ῥώμῃ καὶ παρ᾽ ἄλλοις τισὶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[138]</tei-num> ἀνετίθει δὲ καὶ τοῦτον τὸν ἀγῶνα Καίσαρι κατὰ πενταετηρίδα παρεσκευασμένος ἄγειν αὐτόν: ὁ δ᾽ αὐτῷ πᾶσαν τὴν εἰς τὰ τοιαῦτα παρασκευὴν ἀπὸ τῶν οἰκείων διεπέμπετο τὴν φιλοτιμίαν ἐπικοσμῶν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[139]</tei-num> ἰδίᾳ δὲ καὶ ἡ γυνὴ Καίσαρος Ἰουλία πολλὰ τῶν ἐκεῖ πολυτελεστάτων ἀπέστειλεν, ὡς μηδὲν ὑστερεῖν τὰ πάντα συντιμώμενα ταλάντων πεντακοσίων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[140]</tei-num> συνελθόντος δ᾽ εἰς τὴν πόλιν ὄχλου πλείονος κατὰ θεωρίαν καὶ πρεσβείας, ἃς ἔπεμπον οἱ δῆμοι δι᾽ ἃς ἐπεπόνθεισαν εὐεργεσίας, ἅπαντας ἐξεδέξατο καὶ καταγωγαῖς καὶ τραπέζαις καὶ διηνεκέσιν ἑορταῖς, τῆς πανηγύρεως ἐν μὲν ταῖς ἡμέραις ἐχούσης τὰς ἀπὸ τῶν θεαμάτων ψυχαγωγίας, ἐν δὲ ταῖς νυξὶ τὰς εὐφροσύνας καὶ τὴν εἰς τοῦτο πολυτέλειαν, ὡς ἐπίσημον γενέσθαι τὴν μεγαλοψυχίαν αὐτοῦ: <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[141]</tei-num> εἰς πάντα γὰρ ἅπερ ἂν ἐπιτηδεύσειεν ἐφιλονείκει τὴν τῶν ἤδη γεγενημένων ἐπίδειξιν ὑπερβαλέσθαι, καί φασιν αὐτόν τε Καίσαρα καὶ Ἀγρίππαν πολλάκις εἰπεῖν, ὡς ἀποδέοι τὰ τῆς ἀρχῆς Ἡρώδῃ τῆς οὔσης ἐν αὐτῷ μεγαλοψυχίας: ἄξιον γὰρ εἶναι καὶ Συρίας ἁπάσης καὶ Αἰγύπτου τὴν βασιλείαν ἔχειν.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num142" xml:id="greek-book16-num142" id="greek-book16-num142" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[142]</tei-num> Μετὰ δὲ τὴν πανήγυριν ταύτην καὶ τὰς ἑορτὰς πόλιν ἄλλην ἀνήγειρεν ἐν τῷ πεδίῳ τῷ λεγομένῳ Καφαρσαβᾶ τόπον ἔνυδρον καὶ χώραν ἀρίστην φυτοῖς ἐκλέξας, ποταμοῦ τε περιρρέοντος τὴν πόλιν αὐτὴν καὶ καλλίστου κατὰ μέγεθος τῶν φυτῶν περιειληφότος ἄλσους. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[143]</tei-num> ταύτην ἀπὸ Ἀντιπάτρου τοῦ πατρὸς Ἀντιπατρίδα προσηγόρευσεν. ἐπώνυμον δὲ καὶ τῇ μητρὶ χωρίον ὑπὲρ Ἱεριχοῦν οἰκοδομήσας ἀσφαλείᾳ τε διάφορον καὶ καταγωγαῖς ἥδιστον ἐκάλεσεν Κύπρον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[144]</tei-num> Φασαήλῳ τε τῷ ἀδελφῷ μνημεῖα διὰ τὴν γεγενημένην εἰς αὐτὸν φιλοστοργίαν ἀνετίθει τὰ κάλλιστα, πύργον ἐπ᾽ αὐτῆς τῆς πόλεως ἀναστήσας οὐδὲν ἐλάττω τοῦ κατὰ τὴν Φάρον, ὃν προσηγόρευσεν Φασάηλον, ἀσφαλείας τε τῇ πόλει μέρος ὄντα καὶ μνήμης τῷ τετελευτηκότι διὰ τὴν προσηγορίαν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[145]</tei-num> ὁμώνυμον δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ πόλιν περὶ τὸν αὐλῶνα τῆς Ἱεριχοῦντος ἔκτισεν ἀπιόντων κατὰ βορρᾶν ἄνεμον, δι᾽ ἧς καὶ τὴν πέριξ χώραν ἔρημον οὖσαν ἐνεργοτέραν ἐποίησεν ταῖς ἐπιμελείαις τῶν οἰκητόρων. Φασαηλίδα καὶ ταύτην ἐκάλει.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num146" xml:id="greek-book16-num146" id="greek-book16-num146" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[146]</tei-num> Τὰς δὲ ἄλλας εὐεργεσίας ἄπορον εἰπεῖν ὅσας ἀπέδωκεν ταῖς πόλεσιν ἔν τε Συρίᾳ καὶ κατὰ τὴν Ἑλλάδα καὶ παρ᾽ οἷς ποτ᾽ ἂν ἀποδημήσας τύχοι: καὶ γὰρ πλείους λειτουργίας καὶ δημοσίων ἔργων κατασκευὰς καὶ χρήματα τοῖς δεομένοις ἔργοις εἰς ἐπιμέλειαν τῶν προτέρων ἔργων ἐκλελοιπότων ἄφθονα χαρίσασθαι δοκεῖ. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[147]</tei-num> τὰ δὲ μέγιστα καὶ διασημότατα τῶν πεπραγμένων αὐτῷ Ῥοδίοις μὲν τό τε Πύθιον ἀνέστησεν οἰκείοις ἀναλώμασιν καὶ παρέσχεν ἀργυρίου πολλὰ τάλαντα πρὸς ναυπηγίαν. Νικοπολίταις δὲ τοῖς ἐπ᾽ Ἀκτίῳ κτισθεῖσιν ὑπὸ Καίσαρος τὰ πλεῖστα τῶν δημοσίων συγκατεσκεύασεν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[148]</tei-num> Ἀντιοχεῦσι δὲ τοῖς ἐν Συρίᾳ μεγίστην πόλιν οἰκοῦσιν, ἣν κατὰ μῆκος τέμνει πλατεῖα, ταύτην αὐτὴν στοαῖς παρ᾽ ἑκάτερα καὶ λίθῳ τὴν ὕπαιθρον ὁδὸν ξεστῷ καταστορέσας πλεῖστον εἰς κόσμον καὶ τὴν τῶν οἰκούντων εὐχρηστίαν ὠφέλησεν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[149]</tei-num> τόν γε μὴν Ὀλυμπίασιν ἀγῶνα πολὺ τῆς προσηγορίας ἀδοξότερον ὑπ᾽ ἀχρηματίας διατεθειμένον τιμιώτερον ἐποίει χρημάτων προσόδους καταστήσας καὶ πρὸς θυσίας καὶ τὸν ἄλλον κόσμον ἐσεμνοποίησεν τὴν πανήγυριν. διὰ δὴ ταύτην τὴν φιλοτιμίαν διηνεκὴς ἀγωνοθέτης παρὰ τοῖς Ἠλείοις ἀνεγράφη.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num150" xml:id="greek-book16-num150" id="greek-book16-num150" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[150]</tei-num> Τοῖς μὲν οὖν ἄλλοις ἐπέρχεται θαυμάζειν τὸ διεστὸς τῆς ἐν τῇ φύσει προαιρέσεως: ὅταν μὲν γὰρ εἰς τὰς φιλοτιμίας καὶ τὰς εὐεργεσίας ἀπίδωμεν, αἷς ἐκέχρητο πρὸς ἅπαντας ἀνθρώπους, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως οὐκ ἄν τις αὐτὸν καὶ τῶν ἔλαττον τετιμημένων ἠρνήθη μὴ συνομολογεῖν εὐεργετικωτάτῃ κεχρῆσθαι τῇ φύσει. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[151]</tei-num> ὅταν δὲ εἰς τὰς τιμωρίας καὶ ἀδικίας, ἃς εἰς τοὺς ἀρχομένους καὶ τοὺς οἰκειοτάτους ἐπεδείξατο βλέψῃ καὶ καταμάθῃ τὸ σκληρὸν καὶ τὸ δυσπαράκλητον τοῦ τρόπου, νικηθήσεται θηριώδη δοκεῖν καὶ πάσης μετριότητος ἀλλότριον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[152]</tei-num> ἔνθεν καὶ διάφορόν τινα καὶ μαχομένην ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ νομίζουσιν γενέσθαι τὴν προαίρεσιν. ἐγὼ δ᾽ οὐχ οὕτως ἔχων μίαν αἰτίαν ἀμφοτέρων τούτων ὑπολαμβάνω: <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[153]</tei-num> φιλότιμος γὰρ ὢν καὶ τούτου τοῦ πάθους ἡττημένος ἰσχυρῶς, προήγετο μὲν εἰς μεγαλοψυχίαν, εἴ που μνήμης εἰς αὖθις ἢ κατὰ τὸ παρὸν εὐφημίας ἐλπὶς ἐμπέσοι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[154]</tei-num> ταῖς δὲ δαπάναις ὑπὲρ δύναμιν χρώμενος ἠναγκάζετο χαλεπὸς εἶναι τοῖς ὑποτεταγμένοις: τὰ γὰρ εἰς οὓς ἐδαπάνα πολλὰ γενόμενα κακῶν ποριστὴν ἐξ ὧν ἐλάμβανεν ἐποίει. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[155]</tei-num> καὶ συνειδὼς ἐφ᾽ οἷς ἠδίκει τοὺς ὑποτεταγμένους μισούμενον ἑαυτὸν τὸ μὲν ἐπανορθοῦσθαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας οὐ ῥᾴδιον ἐνόμιζεν: οὐδὲ γὰρ εἰς τὰς προσόδους λυσιτελὲς ἦν. ἀντεφιλονείκει δὲ τὴν δύσνοιαν αὐτὴν εὐπορίας ἀφορμὴν ποιούμενος. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[156]</tei-num> περί γε μὴν τοὺς οἰκείους, εἴ τις ἢ λόγῳ μὴ θεραπεύοι τὸ δοῦλον ἐξομολογούμενος ἢ δόξειεν εἰς τὴν ἀρχήν τι παρακινεῖν, οὐχ ἱκανὸς ἑαυτοῦ κρατεῖν ἐγίνετο καὶ διεξῆλθεν ὁμοῦ συγγενεῖς καὶ φίλους ἴσα πολεμίοις τιμωρούμενος ἐκ τοῦ μόνος ἐθέλειν τετιμῆσθαι τὰς τοιαύτας ἁμαρτίας ἀναλαμβάνων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[157]</tei-num> μαρτύριον δέ μοι τούτου τοῦ πάθους, ὅτι μέγιστον περὶ αὐτὸν ἦν, καὶ τὰ γινόμενα κατὰ τὰς Καίσαρος καὶ Ἀγρίππα καὶ τῶν ἄλλων φίλων τιμάς: οἷς γὰρ ἐθεράπευεν τοὺς κρείττονας, τούτοις καὶ αὐτὸς ἠξίου θεραπεύεσθαι καὶ τὸ κάλλιστον ὧν ᾤετο παρέχων ἐν τῷ διδόναι τὴν τοῦ τυχεῖν τῶν ὁμοίων ἐπιθυμίαν ἐδήλου. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[158]</tei-num> τό γε μὴν Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος ἠλλοτρίωται νόμῳ πρὸς πάντα τὰ τοιαῦτα καὶ συνείθισται τὸ δίκαιον ἀντὶ τοῦ πρὸς δόξαν ἠγαπηκέναι. διόπερ οὐκ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχαρισμένον, ὅτι μὴ δυνατὸν εἰκόσιν ἢ ναοῖς ἢ τοιούτοις ἐπιτηδεύμασιν κολακεύειν τοῦ βασιλέως τὸ φιλότιμον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[159]</tei-num> αἰτία μὲν αὕτη μοι δοκεῖ τῆς Ἡρώδου περὶ μὲν τοὺς οἰκείους καὶ συμβούλους ἁμαρτίας, περὶ δὲ τοὺς ἔξω καὶ μὴ προσήκοντας εὐεργεσίας.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num160" xml:id="greek-book16-num160" id="greek-book16-num160" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[160]</tei-num> Τοὺς δὲ κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν Ἰουδαίους καὶ ὅσους ἡ πρὸς Κυρήνῃ Λιβύη κατέσχεν ἐκάκουν αἱ πόλεις, τῶν μὲν πρότερον βασιλέων ἰσονομίαν αὐτοῖς παρεσχημένων, ἐν δὲ τῷ τότε δι᾽ ἐπηρείας ἐχόντων τῶν Ἑλλήνων αὐτούς, ὡς καὶ χρημάτων ἱερῶν ἀφαίρεσιν ποιεῖσθαι καὶ καταβλάπτειν ἐν τοῖς ἐπὶ μέρους. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[161]</tei-num> πάσχοντες δὲ κακῶς καὶ πέρας οὐδὲν εὑρίσκοντες τῆς τῶν Ἑλλήνων ἀπανθρωπίας ἐπρεσβεύσαντο παρὰ Καίσαρα καὶ περὶ τούτων. ὁ δ᾽ αὐτοῖς τὴν αὐτὴν ἰσοτέλειαν ἔδωκεν γράψας τοῖς κατὰ τὰς ἐπαρχίας, ὧν ὑπετάξαμεν τὰ ἀντίγραφα μαρτύρια τῆς διαθέσεως, ἣν ἔσχον ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἄνωθεν οἱ κρατοῦντες.</tei-p></tei-div2>

[149] τόν γε μὴν Ὀλυμπίασιν ἀγῶνα πολὺ τῆς προσηγορίας ἀδοξότερον ὑπ᾽ ἀχρηματίας διατεθειμένον τιμιώτερον ἐποίει χρημάτων προσόδους καταστήσας καὶ πρὸς θυσίας καὶ τὸν ἄλλον κόσμον ἐσεμνοποίησεν τὴν πανήγυριν. διὰ δὴ ταύτην τὴν φιλοτιμίαν διηνεκὴς ἀγωνοθέτης παρὰ τοῖς Ἠλείοις ἀνεγράφη.[150] Τοῖς μὲν οὖν ἄλλοις ἐπέρχεται θαυμάζειν τὸ διεστὸς τῆς ἐν τῇ φύσει προαιρέσεως: ὅταν μὲν γὰρ εἰς τὰς φιλοτιμίας καὶ τὰς εὐεργεσίας ἀπίδωμεν, αἷς ἐκέχρητο πρὸς ἅπαντας ἀνθρώπους, οὐκ ἔστιν ὅπως οὐκ ἄν τις αὐτὸν καὶ τῶν ἔλαττον τετιμημένων ἠρνήθη μὴ συνομολογεῖν εὐεργετικωτάτῃ κεχρῆσθαι τῇ φύσει. [151] ὅταν δὲ εἰς τὰς τιμωρίας καὶ ἀδικίας, ἃς εἰς τοὺς ἀρχομένους καὶ τοὺς οἰκειοτάτους ἐπεδείξατο βλέψῃ καὶ καταμάθῃ τὸ σκληρὸν καὶ τὸ δυσπαράκλητον τοῦ τρόπου, νικηθήσεται θηριώδη δοκεῖν καὶ πάσης μετριότητος ἀλλότριον. [152] ἔνθεν καὶ διάφορόν τινα καὶ μαχομένην ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ νομίζουσιν γενέσθαι τὴν προαίρεσιν. ἐγὼ δ᾽ οὐχ οὕτως ἔχων μίαν αἰτίαν ἀμφοτέρων τούτων ὑπολαμβάνω: [153] φιλότιμος γὰρ ὢν καὶ τούτου τοῦ πάθους ἡττημένος ἰσχυρῶς, προήγετο μὲν εἰς μεγαλοψυχίαν, εἴ που μνήμης εἰς αὖθις ἢ κατὰ τὸ παρὸν εὐφημίας ἐλπὶς ἐμπέσοι. [154] ταῖς δὲ δαπάναις ὑπὲρ δύναμιν χρώμενος ἠναγκάζετο χαλεπὸς εἶναι τοῖς ὑποτεταγμένοις: τὰ γὰρ εἰς οὓς ἐδαπάνα πολλὰ γενόμενα κακῶν ποριστὴν ἐξ ὧν ἐλάμβανεν ἐποίει. [155] καὶ συνειδὼς ἐφ᾽ οἷς ἠδίκει τοὺς ὑποτεταγμένους μισούμενον ἑαυτὸν τὸ μὲν ἐπανορθοῦσθαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας οὐ ῥᾴδιον ἐνόμιζεν: οὐδὲ γὰρ εἰς τὰς προσόδους λυσιτελὲς ἦν. ἀντεφιλονείκει δὲ τὴν δύσνοιαν αὐτὴν εὐπορίας ἀφορμὴν ποιούμενος. [156] περί γε μὴν τοὺς οἰκείους, εἴ τις ἢ λόγῳ μὴ θεραπεύοι τὸ δοῦλον ἐξομολογούμενος ἢ δόξειεν εἰς τὴν ἀρχήν τι παρακινεῖν, οὐχ ἱκανὸς ἑαυτοῦ κρατεῖν ἐγίνετο καὶ διεξῆλθεν ὁμοῦ συγγενεῖς καὶ φίλους ἴσα πολεμίοις τιμωρούμενος ἐκ τοῦ μόνος ἐθέλειν τετιμῆσθαι τὰς τοιαύτας ἁμαρτίας ἀναλαμβάνων. [157] μαρτύριον δέ μοι τούτου τοῦ πάθους, ὅτι μέγιστον περὶ αὐτὸν ἦν, καὶ τὰ γινόμενα κατὰ τὰς Καίσαρος καὶ Ἀγρίππα καὶ τῶν ἄλλων φίλων τιμάς: οἷς γὰρ ἐθεράπευεν τοὺς κρείττονας, τούτοις καὶ αὐτὸς ἠξίου θεραπεύεσθαι καὶ τὸ κάλλιστον ὧν ᾤετο παρέχων ἐν τῷ διδόναι τὴν τοῦ τυχεῖν τῶν ὁμοίων ἐπιθυμίαν ἐδήλου. [158] τό γε μὴν Ἰουδαίων ἔθνος ἠλλοτρίωται νόμῳ πρὸς πάντα τὰ τοιαῦτα καὶ συνείθισται τὸ δίκαιον ἀντὶ τοῦ πρὸς δόξαν ἠγαπηκέναι. διόπερ οὐκ ἦν αὐτῷ κεχαρισμένον, ὅτι μὴ δυνατὸν εἰκόσιν ἢ ναοῖς ἢ τοιούτοις ἐπιτηδεύμασιν κολακεύειν τοῦ βασιλέως τὸ φιλότιμον. [159] αἰτία μὲν αὕτη μοι δοκεῖ τῆς Ἡρώδου περὶ μὲν τοὺς οἰκείους καὶ συμβούλους ἁμαρτίας, περὶ δὲ τοὺς ἔξω καὶ μὴ προσήκοντας εὐεργεσίας.[160] Τοὺς δὲ κατὰ τὴν Ἀσίαν Ἰουδαίους καὶ ὅσους ἡ πρὸς Κυρήνῃ Λιβύη κατέσχεν ἐκάκουν αἱ πόλεις, τῶν μὲν πρότερον βασιλέων ἰσονομίαν αὐτοῖς παρεσχημένων, ἐν δὲ τῷ τότε δι᾽ ἐπηρείας ἐχόντων τῶν Ἑλλήνων αὐτούς, ὡς καὶ χρημάτων ἱερῶν ἀφαίρεσιν ποιεῖσθαι καὶ καταβλάπτειν ἐν τοῖς ἐπὶ μέρους. [161] πάσχοντες δὲ κακῶς καὶ πέρας οὐδὲν εὑρίσκοντες τῆς τῶν Ἑλλήνων ἀπανθρωπίας ἐπρεσβεύσαντο παρὰ Καίσαρα καὶ περὶ τούτων. ὁ δ᾽ αὐτοῖς τὴν αὐτὴν ἰσοτέλειαν ἔδωκεν γράψας τοῖς κατὰ τὰς ἐπαρχίας, ὧν ὑπετάξαμεν τὰ ἀντίγραφα μαρτύρια τῆς διαθέσεως, ἣν ἔσχον ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν ἄνωθεν οἱ κρατοῦντες.

English.html: <tei-div2 type="chapter" n="10" data-synthetic-chapter="alignment-derived"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num136" xml:id="english-book16-num136" id="english-book16-num136" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="10" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[136]</tei-num> ABOUT this time it was that Cesarea Sebaste, which he had built, was finished. The entire building being accomplished: in the tenth year, the solemnity of it fell into the twenty-eighth year of Herod's reign, and into the hundred and ninety-second olympiad. There was accordingly a great festival and most sumptuous preparations made presently, in order to its dedication; for he had appointed a contention in music, and games to be performed naked. He had also gotten ready a great number of those that fight single combats, and of beasts for the like purpose; horse races also, and the most chargeable of such sports and shows as used to be exhibited at Rome, and in other places. He consecrated this combat to Caesar, and ordered it to be celebrated every fifth year. He also sent all sorts of ornaments for it out of his own furniture, that it might want nothing to make it decent; nay, Julia, Caesar's wife, sent a great part of her most valuable furniture [from Rome], insomuch that he had no want of any thing. The sum of them all was estimated at five hundred talents. Now when a great multitude was come to that city to see the shows, as well as the ambassadors whom other people sent, on account of the benefits they had received from Herod, he entertained them all in the public inns, and at public tables, and with perpetual feasts; this solemnity having in the day time the diversions of the fights, and in the night time such merry meetings as cost vast sums of money, and publicly demonstrated the generosity of his soul; for in all his undertakings he was ambitious to exhibit what exceeded whatsoever had been done before of the same kind. And it is related that Caesar and Agrippa often said, that the dominions of Herod were too little for the greatness of his soul; for that he deserved to have both all the kingdom of Syria, and that of Egypt also.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num142" xml:id="english-book16-num142" id="english-book16-num142" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[142]</tei-num> After this solemnity and these festivals were over, Herod erected another city in the plain called Capharsaba, where he chose out a fit place, both for plenty of water and goodness of soil, and proper for the production of what was there planted, where a river encompassed the city itself, and a grove of the best trees for magnitude was round about it: this he named Antipatris, from his father Antipater. He also built upon another spot of ground above Jericho, of the same name with his mother, a place of great security and very pleasant for habitation, and called it Cypros. He also dedicated the finest monuments to his brother Phasaelus, on account of the great natural affection there had been between them, by erecting a tower in the city itself, not less than the tower of Pharos, which he named Phasaelus, which was at once a part of the strong defenses of the city, and a memorial for him that was deceased, because it bare his name. He also built a city of the same name in the valley of Jericho, as you go from it northward, whereby he rendered the neighboring country more fruitful by the cultivation its inhabitants introduced; and this also he called Phasaelus.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num146" xml:id="english-book16-num146" id="english-book16-num146" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[146]</tei-num> But as for his other benefits, it is impossible to reckon them up, those which he bestowed on cities, both in Syria and in Greece, and in all the places he came to in his voyages; for he seems to have conferred, and that after a most plentiful manner, what would minister to many necessities, and the building of public works, and gave them the money that was necessary to such works as wanted it, to support them upon the failure of their other revenues: but what was the greatest and most illustrious of all his works, he erected Apollo's temple at Rhodes, at his own expenses, and gave them a great number of talents of silver for the repair of their fleet. He also built the greatest part of the public edifices for the inhabitants of Nicopolis, at Actium; and for the Antiochinus, the inhabitants of the principal city of Syria, where a broad street cuts through the place lengthways, he built cloisters along it on both sides, and laid the open road with polished stone, and was of very great advantage to the inhabitants. And as to the olympic games, which were in a very low condition, by reason of the failure of their revenues, he recovered their reputation, and appointed revenues for heir maintenance, and made that solemn meeting more venerable, as to the sacrifices and other ornaments; and by reason of this vast liberality, he was generally declared in their inscriptions to be one of the perpetual managers of those games.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num150" xml:id="english-book16-num150" id="english-book16-num150" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[150]</tei-num> Now some there are who stand amazed at the diversity of Herod's nature and purposes; for when we have respect to his magnificence, and the benefits which he bestowed on all mankind, there is no possibility for even those that had the least respect for him to deny, or not openly to confess, that he had a nature vastly beneficent; but when any one looks upon the punishments he inflicted, and the injuries he did, not only to his subjects, but to his nearest relations, and takes notice of his severe and unrelenting disposition there, he will be forced to allow that he was brutish, and a stranger to all humanity; insomuch that these men suppose his nature to be different, and sometimes at contradiction with itself; but I am myself of another opinion, and imagine that the occasion of both these sort of actions was one and the same; for being a man ambitious of honor, and quite overcome by that passion, he was induced to be magnificent, wherever there appeared any hopes of a future memorial, or of reputation at present; and as his expenses were beyond his abilities, he was necessitated to be harsh to his subjects; for the persons on whom he expended his money were so many, that they made him a very bad procurer of it; and because he was conscious that he was hated by those under him, for the injuries he did them, he thought it not an easy thing to amend his offenses, for that it was inconvenient for his revenue; he therefore strove on the other side to make their ill-will an occasion of his gains. As to his own court, therefore, if any one was not very obsequious to him in his language, and would not confess himself to be his slave, or but seemed to think of any innovation in his government, he was not able to contain himself, but prosecuted his very kindred and friends, and punished them as if they were enemies and this wickedness he undertook out of a desire that he might be himself alone honored. Now for this, my assertion about that passion of his, we have the greatest evidence, by what he did to honor Caesar and Agrippa, and his other friends; for with what honors he paid his respects to them who were his superiors, the same did he desire to be paid to himself; and what he thought the most excellent present he could make another, he discovered an inclination to have the like presented to himself. But now the Jewish nation is by their law a stranger to all such things, and accustomed to prefer righteousness to glory; for which reason that nation was not agreeable to him, because it was out of their power to flatter the king's ambition with statues or temples, or any other such performances; And this seems to me to have been at once the occasion of Herod's crimes as to his own courtiers and counselors, and of his benefactions as to foreigners and those that had no relation to him.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num160" xml:id="english-book16-num160" id="english-book16-num160" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[160]</tei-num> Now the cities ill-treated the Jews in Asia, and all those also of the same nation which lived ill Libya, which joins to Cyrene, while the former kings had given them equal privileges with the other citizens; but the Greeks affronted them at this time, and that so far as to take away their sacred money, and to do them mischief on other particular occasions. When therefore they were thus afflicted, and found no end of their barbarous treatment they met with among the Greeks, they sent ambassadors to Caesar on those accounts, who gave them the same privileges as they had before, and sent letters to the same purpose to the governors of the provinces, copies of which I subjoin here, as testimonials of the ancient favorable disposition the Roman emperors had towards us.</tei-p></tei-div2>

Latin.html:
<tei-div2 type="chapter" n="11" data-synthetic-chapter="milestone-derived"><tei-div2 n="11" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed=""><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num162" id="latin-book16-num162" data-origname="p" data-processed="">XI Caesar augustus pontifex tribunciae potestatis dicit. Quoniam gens iudeaorum fidelis non solum presenti tempore, sed etiam priori et magis patri meo dictatori caesari populoque romano et princeps eorum hyrcanus apparuit Placuit mihi et senatui cum sententia populi romani iudaeos suis legibus et patrio iure frui permittere. Sicut sub hyrcano <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00397.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="197r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> principe sacerdotum altissimi dei et secra ria eorum inuiolata permarere, et pecunias ab eis ab hierosolimam transmissas reddi custodibus pecuniarum. Neque uadimonia sabbato uel sexto die ab hora non exigi. Siquis autem inuentus fuerit auferent sacros sanctos eorum codices aut pecunias a synagogis huiusmodi sacrilegio teneatur et substantia eius publico romae deputetur. Suggestionem uero eorum pro piaetate mea quam habeo super omnes homines per gaium martium censorinum mihi porrectam, et hoc decretum praecipio proponi in nobilissimo loco quem omnis asiam eo numini dedicauit. Siquis autem transgressus fuerit hanc constitutionem non mediocrem paenam exsoluet. Scriptum est in caesaris templo,</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num166" id="latin-book16-num166" data-origname="p" data-processed="">caesar norbano flacco salutem, iudaei qui antiquam consuetudinem solent pecunias sacras ad hierosolimam transmittere sine inpedimento hoc faciant, haec quidem caesar.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num167" id="latin-book16-num167" data-origname="p" data-processed="">agrippa uero scripsit per iudaeis hoc modo. Agrippe magistratibus senatui populoque phesiorum salutem. Pecuniarum sacrarumque in hierosolimorum templum transmittuntur, diligentiam et custodiam in asya iudaeos habere praecipio secundum patrium morem. Hos autem qui sacras pecunias iudaeorum auferunt et ad asilium confugiunt, iubeo de trai iudeisque tradi quod iure etiam sacrilegii detrahuntur. Scripsi uero silano magistratum gerenti ne sabbato iudaei conpellantur uadimonia prebere.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num169" id="latin-book16-num169" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Marcus agrippa quirinensium magistratibus senatui et populo salutem. Iudaei qui per cirenen quibus iam augustus scriptis in libia fabio magistratum gerenti aliisque ibi prouintiae procuratoribus quatenus sine inpedimento paecuniae hierosolimis secundum morem suum transmittantur. Nunc me interpellauerunt qui ab aliquibus<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> calumpniatoribus affliguntur ocasione tributorum quae nequaquam debent et prohibentur solemnia sua per agere quo<tei-gap data-origname="gap" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-gap> nullo modo impediri admoneo. Sed et in quas sacras pecunias ciues ab eis abstulerunt has ipsis reddi praetio et in reliquo corrigi net alia committantur.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num171" id="latin-book16-num171" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Gaius norbanus flaccus proconsul sardiniensium magistratibus et senatui salutem. Caesar scripsit mihi praecipiens nequaquam iudaeos prohiberi patria consuetudine pecunias colligentes ad hierosolimam transmittere. Scripsi ergo uobis ut sciatis quem caesar et ego sic uolumus</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num172" id="latin-book16-num172" data-origname="p" data-processed="">nihilominus et iulius proconsul scripsit ita ephesiorum magistratibus senatui et populo salutem. Per asiam iudaei habitantes idibus <tei-expan data-origname="expan" data-processed="">februaris</tei-expan> ephesi mihi iudicanti demonstrauerunt caesarem augustum et agrippam concessisse eis propriis uti legibus immo et pri micias quas singuli eorum si uoluntate piaetatis causa quam in deo habent solent transmittere, habeant licentiam sine inpedimento hoc agere. Petierunt autem ut ego similiter cum decretis a caesare uel agrippa meam sententiam confirmarem. Volo igitur uos cognoscere quoniam decretis augustu et agrippae parens, praecipi eos uti et seruare sine inpedimento sua solemnia.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num174" id="latin-book16-num174" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Haec ideo explanauimus quoniam conscripta nostra amplius apud graecos uenturas ut demonstrem eis quia cunctum honorem ab initio impetrantes nihil ex patriis legibus prohibiti sumus a magistratibus agere sed et defendebamur religionem et honores in deo seruantes, quorum facio sepius mentionem ut mutatis <tei-expan data-origname="expan" data-processed="">saeculi</tei-expan> odiis causae quae nobis ob hoc uel illis inracionabiliter insertae sunt euellantur. Nam legibus hisdem nulla gens semper utitur dum et per ciuitates multa religionis differentia seruetur. Latin.text:
XI Caesar augustus pontifex tribunciae potestatis dicit. Quoniam gens iudeaorum fidelis non solum presenti tempore, sed etiam priori et magis patri meo dictatori caesari populoque romano et princeps eorum hyrcanus apparuit Placuit mihi et senatui cum sententia populi romani iudaeos suis legibus et patrio iure frui permittere. Sicut sub hyrcano  principe sacerdotum altissimi dei et secra ria eorum inuiolata permarere, et pecunias ab eis ab hierosolimam transmissas reddi custodibus pecuniarum. Neque uadimonia sabbato uel sexto die ab hora non exigi. Siquis autem inuentus fuerit auferent sacros sanctos eorum codices aut pecunias a synagogis huiusmodi sacrilegio teneatur et substantia eius publico romae deputetur. Suggestionem uero eorum pro piaetate mea quam habeo super omnes homines per gaium martium censorinum mihi porrectam, et hoc decretum praecipio proponi in nobilissimo loco quem omnis asiam eo numini dedicauit. Siquis autem transgressus fuerit hanc constitutionem non mediocrem paenam exsoluet. Scriptum est in caesaris templo,
					caesar norbano flacco salutem, iudaei qui antiquam consuetudinem solent pecunias sacras ad hierosolimam transmittere sine inpedimento hoc faciant, haec quidem caesar.
					agrippa uero scripsit per iudaeis hoc modo. Agrippe magistratibus senatui populoque phesiorum salutem. Pecuniarum sacrarumque in hierosolimorum templum transmittuntur, diligentiam et custodiam in asya iudaeos habere praecipio secundum patrium morem. Hos autem qui sacras pecunias iudaeorum auferunt et ad asilium confugiunt, iubeo de trai iudeisque tradi quod iure etiam sacrilegii detrahuntur. Scripsi uero silano magistratum gerenti ne sabbato iudaei conpellantur uadimonia prebere.
					Marcus agrippa quirinensium magistratibus senatui et populo salutem. Iudaei qui per cirenen quibus iam augustus scriptis in libia fabio magistratum gerenti aliisque ibi prouintiae procuratoribus quatenus sine inpedimento paecuniae hierosolimis secundum morem suum transmittantur. Nunc me interpellauerunt qui ab aliquibus calumpniatoribus affliguntur ocasione tributorum quae nequaquam debent et prohibentur solemnia sua per agere quo nullo modo impediri admoneo. Sed et in quas sacras pecunias ciues ab eis abstulerunt has ipsis reddi praetio et in reliquo corrigi net alia committantur.
					Gaius norbanus flaccus proconsul sardiniensium magistratibus et senatui salutem. Caesar scripsit mihi praecipiens nequaquam iudaeos prohiberi patria consuetudine pecunias colligentes ad hierosolimam transmittere. Scripsi ergo uobis ut sciatis quem caesar et ego sic uolumus
					nihilominus et iulius proconsul scripsit ita ephesiorum magistratibus senatui et populo salutem. Per asiam iudaei habitantes idibus februaris ephesi mihi iudicanti demonstrauerunt caesarem augustum et agrippam concessisse eis propriis uti legibus immo et pri micias quas singuli eorum si uoluntate piaetatis causa quam in deo habent solent transmittere, habeant licentiam sine inpedimento hoc agere. Petierunt autem ut ego similiter cum decretis a caesare uel agrippa meam sententiam confirmarem. Volo igitur uos cognoscere quoniam decretis augustu et agrippae parens, praecipi eos uti et seruare sine inpedimento sua solemnia.
					Haec ideo explanauimus quoniam conscripta nostra amplius apud graecos uenturas ut demonstrem eis quia cunctum honorem ab initio impetrantes nihil ex patriis legibus prohibiti sumus a magistratibus agere sed et defendebamur religionem et honores in deo seruantes, quorum facio sepius mentionem ut mutatis saeculi odiis causae quae nobis ob hoc uel illis inracionabiliter insertae sunt euellantur. Nam legibus hisdem nulla gens semper utitur dum et per ciuitates multa religionis differentia seruetur. Iustitia uero cunctis hominibus similiter studetur, quae commoda graecis uel barbaris existit, de qua nostrae leges multam rationem habentes omnes homines  debent nos ut amicos et hospites amplecti, nam oportet non differentia nos religionum alienos facere, sed non seruatus benignitatis affectus, quae omnium hominum communem uitam poterit custodire redeo uero ad reliquam monumem ta conscriptionis.

Greek.html: <tei-div2 type="chapter" n="11" data-synthetic-chapter="alignment-derived"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num162" xml:id="greek-book16-num162" id="greek-book16-num162" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="11" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[162]</tei-num> ‘Καῖσαρ Σεβαστὸς ἀρχιερεὺς δημαρχικῆς ἐξουσίας λέγει. ἐπειδὴ τὸ ἔθνος τὸ τῶν Ἰουδαίων εὐχάριστον εὑρέθη οὐ μόνον ἐν τῷ ἐνεστῶτι καιρῷ ἀλλὰ καὶ ἐν τῷ προγεγενημένῳ καὶ μάλιστα ἐπὶ τοῦ ἐμοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοκράτορος Καίσαρος πρὸς τὸν δῆμον τὸν Ῥωμαίων ὅ τε ἀρχιερεὺς αὐτῶν Ὑρκανός, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[163]</tei-num> ἔδοξέ μοι καὶ τῷ ἐμῷ συμβουλίῳ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας γνώμῃ δήμου Ῥωμαίων τοὺς Ἰουδαίους χρῆσθαι τοῖς ἰδίοις θεσμοῖς κατὰ τὸν πάτριον αὐτῶν νόμον, καθὼς ἐχρῶντο ἐπὶ Ὑρκανοῦ ἀρχιερέως θεοῦ ὑψίστου, τά τε ἱερὰ * εἶναι ἐν ἀσυλίᾳ καὶ ἀναπέμπεσθαι εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα καὶ ἀποδίδοσθαι τοῖς ἀποδοχεῦσιν Ἱεροσολύμων, ἐγγύας τε μὴ ὁμολογεῖν αὐτοὺς ἐν σάββασιν ἢ τῇ πρὸ αὐτῆς παρασκευῇ ἀπὸ ὥρας ἐνάτης. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[164]</tei-num> ἐὰν δέ τις φωραθῇ κλέπτων τὰς ἱερὰς βίβλους αὐτῶν ἢ τὰ ἱερὰ χρήματα ἔκ τε σαββατείου ἔκ τε ἀνδρῶνος, εἶναι αὐτὸν ἱερόσυλον καὶ τὸν βίον αὐτοῦ ἐνεχθῆναι εἰς τὸ δημόσιον τῶν Ῥωμαίων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[165]</tei-num> τό τε ψήφισμα τὸ δοθέν μοι ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν ὑπὲρ τῆς ἐμῆς εὐσεβείας ἧς ἔχω πρὸς πάντας ἀνθρώπους καὶ ὑπὲρ Γαΐου Μαρκίου Κηνσωρίνου καὶ τοῦτο τὸ διάταγμα κελεύω ἀνατεθῆναι ἐν ἐπισημοτάτῳ τόπῳ τῷ γενηθέντι μοι ὑπὸ τοῦ κοινοῦ τῆς Ἀσίας ἐν Ἀγκύρῃ. ἐὰν δέ τις παραβῇ τι τῶν προειρημένων, δώσει δίκην οὐ μετρίαν. ἐστηλογραφήθη ἐν τῷ Καίσαρος ναῷ.’</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num166" xml:id="greek-book16-num166" id="greek-book16-num166" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[166]</tei-num> ‘Καῖσαρ Νωρβανῷ Φλάκκῳ χαίρειν. Ἰουδαῖοι ὅσοι ποτ᾽ οὖν εἰσίν, οἳ δι᾽ ἀρχαίαν συνήθειαν εἰώθασιν χρήματά τε ἱερὰ φέροντες ἀναπέμπειν ἀκωλύτως τοῦτο ποιείτωσαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.’ καὶ ταῦτα μὲν Καῖσαρ.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num167" xml:id="greek-book16-num167" id="greek-book16-num167" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[167]</tei-num> Ἀγρίππας δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς ἔγραψεν ὑπὲρ τῶν Ἰουδαίων τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον: ‘Ἀγρίππας Ἐφεσίων ἄρχουσι βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. τῶν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν τὸ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀναφερομένων ἱερῶν χρημάτων τὴν ἐπιμέλειαν καὶ φυλακὴν βούλομαι τοὺς ἐν Ἀσίᾳ Ἰουδαίους ποιεῖσθαι κατὰ τὰ πάτρια. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[168]</tei-num> τούς τε κλέπτοντας ἱερὰ γράμματα τῶν Ἰουδαίων καταφεύγοντάς τε εἰς τὰς ἀσυλίας βούλομαι ἀποσπᾶσθαι καὶ παραδίδοσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, ᾧ δικαίῳ ἀποσπῶνται οἱ ἱερόσυλοι. ἔγραψα δὲ καὶ Σιλανῷ τῷ στρατηγῷ, ἵνα σάββασιν μηδεὶς ἀναγκάζῃ Ἰουδαῖον ἐγγύας ὁμολογεῖν.’</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num169" xml:id="greek-book16-num169" id="greek-book16-num169" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[169]</tei-num> ‘Μᾶρκος Ἀγρίππας Κυρηναίων ἄρχουσιν βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. οἱ ἐν Κυρήνῃ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὑπὲρ ὧν ἤδη ὁ Σεβαστὸς ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν ἐν Λιβύῃ στρατηγὸν τόντε ὄντα Φλάβιον καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἄλλους τοὺς τῆς ἐπαρχίας ἐπιμελουμένους, ἵνα ἀνεπικωλύτως ἀναπέμπηται τὰ ἱερὰ χρήματα εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὡς ἔστιν αὐτοῖς πάτριον, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[170]</tei-num> ἐνέτυχόν μοι νῦν, ὡς ὑπό τινων συκοφαντῶν ἐπηρεαζόμενοι καὶ ὡς ἐν προφάσει τελῶν μὴ ὀφειλομένων κωλύοιντο: οἷς ἀποκαθιστάνειν κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον ἐνοχλουμένοις, καὶ εἴ τινων ἱερὰ χρήματα ἀφῄρηνται τῶν πόλεων τοὺς εἰς ταῦτα ἀποκεκριμένους καὶ ταῦτα διορθώσασθαι τοῖς ἐκεῖ Ἰουδαίοις κελεύω.’</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num171" xml:id="greek-book16-num171" id="greek-book16-num171" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[171]</tei-num> ‘Γάιος Νωρβανὸς Φλάκκος ἀνθύπατος Σαρδιανῶν ἄρχουσι χαίρειν. Καῖσάρ μοι ἔγραψεν κελεύων μὴ κωλύεσθαι τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ὅσα ἂν ὦσιν κατὰ τὸ πάτριον αὐτοῖς ἔθος συναγαγόντες χρήματα ἀναπέμπειν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. ἔγραψα οὖν ὑμῖν, ἵν᾽ εἰδῆτε, ὅτι Καῖσαρ κἀγὼ οὕτως θέλομεν γίνεσθαι.’</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num172" xml:id="greek-book16-num172" id="greek-book16-num172" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[172]</tei-num> Οὐδὲν ἧττον καὶ Ἰούλιος Ἀντώνιος ἀνθύπατος ἔγραψεν ‘Ἐφεσίων ἄρχουσιν βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι εἰδοῖς Φεβρουαρίοις δικαιοδοτοῦντί μοι ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ὑπέδειξαν Καίσαρα τὸν Σεβαστὸν καὶ Ἀγρίππαν συγκεχωρηκέναι αὐτοῖς χρῆσθαι τοῖς ἰδίοις νόμοις καὶ ἔθεσιν, ἀπαρχάς τε, ἃς ἕκαστος αὐτῶν ἐκ τῆς ἰδίας προαιρέσεως εὐσεβείας ἕνεκα τῆς πρὸς τὸ θεῖον * ἀνακομιδῆς συμπορευομένους ποιεῖν ἀνεμποδίστως. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[173]</tei-num> ᾔτουν τε, ὅπως κἀγὼ ὁμοίως τοῖς ὑπὸ τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ καὶ Ἀγρίππα δοθεῖσιν τὴν ἐμὴν γνώμην βεβαιώσω. ὑμᾶς οὖν βούλομαι εἰδέναι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ καὶ Ἀγρίππα βουλήμασιν συνεπιτρέπειν αὐτοῖς χρῆσθαι καὶ ποιεῖν κατὰ τὰ πάτρια χωρὶς ἐμποδισμοῦ.’</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num174" xml:id="greek-book16-num174" id="greek-book16-num174" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[174]</tei-num> Ταῦτα μὲν οὖν παρεθέμην ἐξ ἀνάγκης, ἐπειδὴ μέλλουσιν αἱ τῶν ἡμετέρων πράξεων ἀναγραφαὶ τὸ πλέον εἰς τοὺς Ἕλληνας ἰέναι, δεικνὺς αὐτοῖς ὅτι πάσης τιμῆς ἄνωθεν ἐπιτυγχάνοντες οὐδὲν τῶν πατρίων ἐκωλύθημεν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχόντων πράττειν, ἀλλὰ καὶ συνεργούμεθα τὰ τῆς θρησκείας ἔχοντες καὶ τῶν εἰς τὸν θεὸν τιμῶν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[175]</tei-num> ποιοῦμαι δὲ πολλάκις αὐτῶν τὴν μνήμην ἐπιδιαλλάττων τὰ γένη καὶ τὰς ἐμπεφυκυίας τοῖς ἀλογίστοις ἡμῶν τε κἀκείνων μίσους αἰτίας ὑπεξαιρούμενος. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[176]</tei-num> ἔθεσιν μὲν γὰρ οὐδέν ἐστιν γένος ὃ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἀεὶ χρῆται καὶ κατὰ πόλεις ἔσθ᾽ ὅπη πολλῆς ἐγγιγνομένης τῆς διαφορᾶς: τὸ δίκαιον δὲ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ὁμοίως ἐπιτηδεύοντες λυσιτελέστατον ὂν Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[177]</tei-num> οὗ πλεῖστον οἱ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν νόμοι λόγον ἔχοντες ἅπασιν ἡμᾶς, εἰ καθαρῶς ἐμμένοιμεν αὐτοῖς, εὔνους καὶ φίλους ἀπεργάζονται. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[178]</tei-num> διὸ καὶ ταῦτα παρ᾽ ἐκείνων ἡμῖν ἀπαιτητέον καὶ δέον οὐκ ἐν τῇ διαφορᾷ τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων οἴεσθαι τὸ ἀλλότριον, ἀλλ᾽ ἐν τῷ πρὸς καλοκαγαθίαν ἐπιτηδείως ἔχειν: τοῦτο γὰρ κοινὸν ἅπασιν καὶ μόνον ἱκανὸν διασώζειν τὸν τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίον. ἐπάνειμι δὲ πάλιν ἐπὶ τὰ συνεχῆ τῆς ἱστορίας.</tei-p></tei-div2>

Ἰουδαῖοι ὅσοι ποτ᾽ οὖν εἰσίν, οἳ δι᾽ ἀρχαίαν συνήθειαν εἰώθασιν χρήματά τε ἱερὰ φέροντες ἀναπέμπειν ἀκωλύτως τοῦτο ποιείτωσαν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα.’ καὶ ταῦτα μὲν Καῖσαρ.[167] Ἀγρίππας δὲ καὶ αὐτὸς ἔγραψεν ὑπὲρ τῶν Ἰουδαίων τὸν τρόπον τοῦτον: ‘Ἀγρίππας Ἐφεσίων ἄρχουσι βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. τῶν εἰς τὸ ἱερὸν τὸ ἐν Ἱεροσολύμοις ἀναφερομένων ἱερῶν χρημάτων τὴν ἐπιμέλειαν καὶ φυλακὴν βούλομαι τοὺς ἐν Ἀσίᾳ Ἰουδαίους ποιεῖσθαι κατὰ τὰ πάτρια. [168] τούς τε κλέπτοντας ἱερὰ γράμματα τῶν Ἰουδαίων καταφεύγοντάς τε εἰς τὰς ἀσυλίας βούλομαι ἀποσπᾶσθαι καὶ παραδίδοσθαι τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις, ᾧ δικαίῳ ἀποσπῶνται οἱ ἱερόσυλοι. ἔγραψα δὲ καὶ Σιλανῷ τῷ στρατηγῷ, ἵνα σάββασιν μηδεὶς ἀναγκάζῃ Ἰουδαῖον ἐγγύας ὁμολογεῖν.’[169] ‘Μᾶρκος Ἀγρίππας Κυρηναίων ἄρχουσιν βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. οἱ ἐν Κυρήνῃ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὑπὲρ ὧν ἤδη ὁ Σεβαστὸς ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν ἐν Λιβύῃ στρατηγὸν τόντε ὄντα Φλάβιον καὶ πρὸς τοὺς ἄλλους τοὺς τῆς ἐπαρχίας ἐπιμελουμένους, ἵνα ἀνεπικωλύτως ἀναπέμπηται τὰ ἱερὰ χρήματα εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα, ὡς ἔστιν αὐτοῖς πάτριον, [170] ἐνέτυχόν μοι νῦν, ὡς ὑπό τινων συκοφαντῶν ἐπηρεαζόμενοι καὶ ὡς ἐν προφάσει τελῶν μὴ ὀφειλομένων κωλύοιντο: οἷς ἀποκαθιστάνειν κατὰ μηδένα τρόπον ἐνοχλουμένοις, καὶ εἴ τινων ἱερὰ χρήματα ἀφῄρηνται τῶν πόλεων τοὺς εἰς ταῦτα ἀποκεκριμένους καὶ ταῦτα διορθώσασθαι τοῖς ἐκεῖ Ἰουδαίοις κελεύω.’[171] ‘Γάιος Νωρβανὸς Φλάκκος ἀνθύπατος Σαρδιανῶν ἄρχουσι χαίρειν. Καῖσάρ μοι ἔγραψεν κελεύων μὴ κωλύεσθαι τοὺς Ἰουδαίους ὅσα ἂν ὦσιν κατὰ τὸ πάτριον αὐτοῖς ἔθος συναγαγόντες χρήματα ἀναπέμπειν εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα. ἔγραψα οὖν ὑμῖν, ἵν᾽ εἰδῆτε, ὅτι Καῖσαρ κἀγὼ οὕτως θέλομεν γίνεσθαι.’[172] Οὐδὲν ἧττον καὶ Ἰούλιος Ἀντώνιος ἀνθύπατος ἔγραψεν ‘Ἐφεσίων ἄρχουσιν βουλῇ δήμῳ χαίρειν. οἱ ἐν τῇ Ἀσίᾳ κατοικοῦντες Ἰουδαῖοι εἰδοῖς Φεβρουαρίοις δικαιοδοτοῦντί μοι ἐν Ἐφέσῳ ὑπέδειξαν Καίσαρα τὸν Σεβαστὸν καὶ Ἀγρίππαν συγκεχωρηκέναι αὐτοῖς χρῆσθαι τοῖς ἰδίοις νόμοις καὶ ἔθεσιν, ἀπαρχάς τε, ἃς ἕκαστος αὐτῶν ἐκ τῆς ἰδίας προαιρέσεως εὐσεβείας ἕνεκα τῆς πρὸς τὸ θεῖον * ἀνακομιδῆς συμπορευομένους ποιεῖν ἀνεμποδίστως. [173] ᾔτουν τε, ὅπως κἀγὼ ὁμοίως τοῖς ὑπὸ τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ καὶ Ἀγρίππα δοθεῖσιν τὴν ἐμὴν γνώμην βεβαιώσω. ὑμᾶς οὖν βούλομαι εἰδέναι ἐν τοῖς τοῦ Σεβαστοῦ καὶ Ἀγρίππα βουλήμασιν συνεπιτρέπειν αὐτοῖς χρῆσθαι καὶ ποιεῖν κατὰ τὰ πάτρια χωρὶς ἐμποδισμοῦ.’[174] Ταῦτα μὲν οὖν παρεθέμην ἐξ ἀνάγκης, ἐπειδὴ μέλλουσιν αἱ τῶν ἡμετέρων πράξεων ἀναγραφαὶ τὸ πλέον εἰς τοὺς Ἕλληνας ἰέναι, δεικνὺς αὐτοῖς ὅτι πάσης τιμῆς ἄνωθεν ἐπιτυγχάνοντες οὐδὲν τῶν πατρίων ἐκωλύθημεν ὑπὸ τῶν ἀρχόντων πράττειν, ἀλλὰ καὶ συνεργούμεθα τὰ τῆς θρησκείας ἔχοντες καὶ τῶν εἰς τὸν θεὸν τιμῶν. [175] ποιοῦμαι δὲ πολλάκις αὐτῶν τὴν μνήμην ἐπιδιαλλάττων τὰ γένη καὶ τὰς ἐμπεφυκυίας τοῖς ἀλογίστοις ἡμῶν τε κἀκείνων μίσους αἰτίας ὑπεξαιρούμενος. [176] ἔθεσιν μὲν γὰρ οὐδέν ἐστιν γένος ὃ τοῖς αὐτοῖς ἀεὶ χρῆται καὶ κατὰ πόλεις ἔσθ᾽ ὅπη πολλῆς ἐγγιγνομένης τῆς διαφορᾶς: τὸ δίκαιον δὲ πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις ὁμοίως ἐπιτηδεύοντες λυσιτελέστατον ὂν Ἕλλησίν τε καὶ βαρβάροις, [177] οὗ πλεῖστον οἱ παρ᾽ ἡμῖν νόμοι λόγον ἔχοντες ἅπασιν ἡμᾶς, εἰ καθαρῶς ἐμμένοιμεν αὐτοῖς, εὔνους καὶ φίλους ἀπεργάζονται. [178] διὸ καὶ ταῦτα παρ᾽ ἐκείνων ἡμῖν ἀπαιτητέον καὶ δέον οὐκ ἐν τῇ διαφορᾷ τῶν ἐπιτηδευμάτων οἴεσθαι τὸ ἀλλότριον, ἀλλ᾽ ἐν τῷ πρὸς καλοκαγαθίαν ἐπιτηδείως ἔχειν: τοῦτο γὰρ κοινὸν ἅπασιν καὶ μόνον ἱκανὸν διασώζειν τὸν τῶν ἀνθρώπων βίον. ἐπάνειμι δὲ πάλιν ἐπὶ τὰ συνεχῆ τῆς ἱστορίας.

English.html: <tei-div2 type="chapter" n="11" data-synthetic-chapter="alignment-derived"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num162" xml:id="english-book16-num162" id="english-book16-num162" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="11" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[162]</tei-num> "Caesar Augustus, high priest and tribune of the people, ordains thus: Since the nation of the Jews hath been found grateful to the Roman people, not only at this time, but in time past also, and chiefly Hyrcanus the high priest, under my father Caesar the emperor, it seemed good to me and my counselors, according to the sentence and oath of the people of Rome, that the Jews have liberty to make use of their own customs, according to the law of their forefathers, as they made use of them under Hyrcanus the high priest of the Almighty God; and that their sacred money be not touched, but be sent to Jerusalem, and that it be committed to the care of the receivers at Jerusalem; and that they be not obliged to go before any judge on the sabbath day, nor on the day of the preparation to it, after the ninth hour. But if any one be caught stealing their holy books, or their sacred money, whether it be out of the synagogue or public school, he shall be deemed a sacrilegious person, and his goods shall be brought into the public treasury of the Romans. And I give order that the testimonial which they have given me, on account of my regard to that piety which I exercise toward all mankind, and out of regard to Caius Marcus Censorinus, together with the present decree, be proposed in that most eminent place which hath been consecrated to me by the community of Asia at Ancyra. And if any one transgress any part of what is above decreed, he shall be severely punished." This was inscribed upon a pillar in the temple of Caesar.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num166" xml:id="english-book16-num166" id="english-book16-num166" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[166]</tei-num> "Caesar to Norbanus Flaccus, sendeth greeting. Let those Jews, how many soever they be, who have been used, according to their ancient custom, to send their sacred money to Jerusalem, do the same freely." These were the decrees of Caesar.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num167" xml:id="english-book16-num167" id="english-book16-num167" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[167]</tei-num> Agrippa also did himself write after the manner following, on behalf of the Jews: "Agrippa, to the magistrates, senate, and people of the Ephesians, sendeth greeting. I will that the care and custody of the sacred money that is carried to the temple at Jerusalem be left to the Jews of Asia, to do with it according to their ancient custom; and that such as steal that sacred money of the Jews, and fly to a sanctuary, shall be taken thence and delivered to the Jews, by the same law that sacrilegious persons are taken thence. I have also written to Sylvanus the praetor, that no one compel the Jews to come before a judge on the sabbath day."</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num169" xml:id="english-book16-num169" id="english-book16-num169" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[169]</tei-num> "Marcus Agrippa to the magistrates, senate, and people of Cyrene, sendeth greeting. The Jews of Cyrene have interceded with me for the performance of what Augustus sent orders about to Flavius, the then praetor of Libya, and to the other procurators of that province, that the sacred money may be sent to Jerusalem freely, as hath been their custom from their forefathers, they complaining that they are abused by certain informers, and under pretense of taxes which were not due, are hindered from sending them, which I command to be restored without any diminution or disturbance given to them. And if any of that sacred money in the cities be taken from their proper receivers, I further enjoin, that the same be exactly returned to the Jews in that place."</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num171" xml:id="english-book16-num171" id="english-book16-num171" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[171]</tei-num> "Caius Norbanus Flaccus, proconsul, to the magistrates of the Sardians, sendeth greeting. Caesar hath written to me, and commanded me not to forbid the Jews, how many soever they be, from assembling together according to the custom of their forefathers, nor from sending their money to Jerusalem. I have therefore written to you, that you may know that both Caesar and I would have you act accordingly."</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num172" xml:id="english-book16-num172" id="english-book16-num172" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[172]</tei-num> Nor did Julius Antonius, the proconsul, write otherwise. "To the magistrates, senate, and people of the Ephesians, sendeth greeting. As I was dispensing justice at Ephesus, on the Ides of February, the Jews that dwell in Asia demonstrated to me that Augustus and Agrippa had permitted them to use their own laws and customs, and to offer those their first-fruits, which every one of them freely offers to the Deity on account of piety, and to carry them in a company together to Jerusalem without disturbance. They also petitioned me that I also would confirm what had been granted by Augustus and Agrippa by my own sanction. I would therefore have you take notice, that according to the will of Augustus and Agrippa, I permit them to use and do according to the customs of their forefathers without disturbance."</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num174" xml:id="english-book16-num174" id="english-book16-num174" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[174]</tei-num> I have been obliged to set down these decree because the present history of our own acts will go generally among the Greeks; and I have hereby demonstrated to them that we have formerly been in great esteem, and have not been prohibited by those governors we were under from keeping any of the laws of our forefathers; nay, that we have been supported by them, while we followed our own religion, and the worship we paid to God; and I frequently make mention of these decrees, in order to reconcile other people to us, and to take away the causes of that hatred which unreasonable men bear to us. As for our customs there is no nation which always makes use of the same, and in every city almost we meet with them different from one another; but natural justice is most agreeable to the advantage of all men equally, both Greeks and barbarians, to which our laws have the greatest regard, and thereby render us, if we abide in them after a pure manner, benevolent and friendly to all men; on which account we have reason to expect the like return from others, and to inform them that they ought not to esteem difference of positive institutions a sufficient cause of alienation, but [join with us in] the pursuit of virtue and probity, for this belongs to all men in common, and of itself alone is sufficient for the preservation of human life. I now return to the thread of my history.</tei-p></tei-div2>

<tei-div2 type="chapter" n="12" data-synthetic-chapter="milestone-derived"><tei-div2 n="12" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed=""><tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num179" id="latin-book16-num179" data-origname="p" data-processed="">XII. Igitur herodes sicut predixi consumptis suis pecuniis. Audiens hyrcanum ante se regem aperuisse tumulum dauid et tria milia talenturum inuenisse multo plus credens deposita quae, ad omnes sumptus suos sufficerent tumulum aperiens ingreditur noctu, dum nequaquam uellet hoc ciuitatem sentire unde si delissimos amicos tantum ducens pecunias quidem depositas sicut hyrcanus non inuenit, ornatum uero et uasa aurea plura tulit. Dumque omne studium poneret, et inquisitionem diligentiorem faceret ac uellet interius ingredi ad urnas inquibus dauid uel salomonis corpora posita erant, duo eius satellites flammis exusti sunt ab interiore parte occurentibus. Tunc ille timore perterritus <tei-unclear reason="fading" data-origname="unclear" data-processed="">egredi</tei-unclear> egreditur et propiaculo monumentum ex lapide candido ante ianuam magnificentissimis construxit expensis Cuius et nicolaus historiografus meminit sed descensum regis obtauit dum inhonestum hoc factum cognosceret quod semper in suis egit constriptis. Nam uiuente rege et cum eo degens ad gratias eius et fauorem eius tantum modo dicebat quae ad gloriam eius pertinebant. Multas uero iniquitates eius mutabat et cum multo studio caelabat. Nam mariae filiorumque eius mortes crudeliter factas ad satisfactiones cupiens perducere ut luxuriosa millam et adulescentes patris insidiatores accusauit. Res gestas autem regis amplioribus laudibus extollens, delictis eius studiose satisfacit uenia danda est quia<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> non historia sed laudem conscripsit. Nos uero generi asamona eorum regum propinqui, et cum honore sacerdotum habentes aliquid mentiri non putauimus. Ideoque cum ueritate gestorum memoriam recensemus,</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num188" id="latin-book16-num188" data-origname="p" data-processed="">in domesticis uero malis herodes constitutus affligebatur.<tei-lb data-origname="lb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-lb> [...]</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num194" id="latin-book16-num194" data-origname="p" data-processed="">[...]<tei-lb data-origname="lb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-lb> Nam multi ex regis ira accipientes audaciam accusabant propinquos et amicos eius, quibus ita inter se dispositis nulla requies erat, siquidem salome inimica filiis mariae aristobolo suam filiam con uinctam nullatanus fidem ei seruare demittebat, dum flecteret eam ut quicquid locutus secrete fuisset nuntiare sibi. Et in altercationibus quae inter iugales saepius contingunt cogebat puellam dicere quae de marito sciebat. Illa uero dicebat quod saepius memoriam suae matris mariae faceret et quod patrem odio haberet. Frequenter autem terminaretur quia si principatum optineret filios quos herodes ab aliis uxoribus habebat, magistros litterarum in agris constitueret dum apta esset ad hoc opus quam habebant circa studia diligentia. Vxores uero si quando uiderent maternum in dui ornatum pro praesentibus ornamentis ciliciis intercludi ne solem uiderent, quae confestim per salome regi nunciata, dolorem eius inflammabant. Vrguebatur uero multo peius omnibus credens et inuicem se accusantibus tunc autem filiis interminatus satisfactionibus eorum ad praesens mollitus. In posterum atrocius exarsit.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num206" id="latin-book16-num206" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Nam ferora cum ad alexandrum uenisset et filiam archelai glafiram sicut praediximus habentem, salomem inquit dicentem audiui, quod herodes in amore glafire suae nurus incidisset et minime disiderii solatium possit inuenire. Quod ille audiens adulescentia uel emulatione commotus, quae honoris causa circa puellam ab herode fiebat, propter amorem haec eadem facere suspicabatur. Dolorem <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00399.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="198r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> ergo minus tollerans, patri nuntiauit cum lacrimis quae ferora dixisset. Herodes autem multo magis feruens, et mendacium inpudice criminationis non ferens turbatur, et saepius exclamans maliuolentiam familiarum qualis ipse erga eos fuisset, et qualis eos inuenisset. Conuocauit feroram quem huius modi adgressus pessime omnium in quo ad tam in mensam uel infandam in deuotinem peruenisti, ut alia de nobis existimes aut loquaris. Nonne uideo tuam uoluntatem quia non im meam iniuriam talia uerba producere sed insidias et uenena inmittere filio pro mea perditone festinasti. Quid enim alter nisi bonitate retentus quam hic puer in se habet portate potuisset in patrem non uindicare tam crudelem opinionem. Prius enim gladium in dextra quam hoc uerbum in animo eius debebas inmittere contra patrem. Quid autem conaris male loquendo de me nisi uteorum fauorem fraudibus tibi concilies. Nam talia dixisti, quae tuae impiaetatis fuissent cogitanda. Abscede iam pessime crica fratrem atque benefactorem, et tecum quidem haec malicia conscientiae conuiuat. Ego uero uindico sicut soleo meos, nec uindicans merito in eis sed magis beneficiis exornans quibus indigni esse nascuntur.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num213" id="latin-book16-num213" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Talia quidem rex ferora uero statim mestitia plenus. Salomi inquid haec persuasit et ab illa sermones audiui. Quem mox ut audiuit, nam presens erat exclamauit, quod nihil ab ipsa tale dictum fuisset, et quod festinarent omnes ad odium regis eam perducere. Cunctisque modis occidere propter fidem quam erga eum semper habere cosgnoscerent in praesenti uero sibi insidiari quod sola reflecteret fratrem, ne uxorem quam nunc haberet repudiaret, regisque filiam in matrimonio sibi coniungeret. Qua propter me falsis inquit accusationibus est agressus. Cum haec dixisset crines suos dilacerans et pectora manibus tundens uerisimi<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>lis ad negationem esse constabat, maliuolentiam uero morum dissimultationem redurguebat, feroras autem in modio restitit nullam habens satisfactionem Nam alexandro se dixisse confessus est audisse uero a salome minime comprobauit, unde diu confessione sermonum inter eos facta rex fratrem uel sororem auersatus filium pro constantia laudauit quod sibi sermones ferorae nuntiasset. Ac lite facta salome ut accusationis commote caput omnium odio tenebatur, quam uxorem regis ut maliuolam aborrebant et quod natura malignam eam cognoscerent. Qui requirenti regi, de facta quidem communione uel permixtione confessi sunt, aliud uero nihil acerbum scire de patre dixerunt. Cumque magis torquerentur et inneces sitatibus essent superque ministri atroces in eos insisterent, ad gratiam anti patri confessi sunt quod odium circa patrem<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> et inimicitias alexander haberet, et persuaderet eis, herodem quidem spernere uelut superfluum et cooperientem senectutis suae tempora dum annos aetatis caelaret et ad se iam respicere tamquam regnum habentem et in uito patre et quod alii nullatenus sed sibi citius primus locus uenturus esset non propter genus tantum sed preparati onibus paratam ei dominationem esse quia plures qui cuncta perse pati uel facere essent parati.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num235" id="latin-book16-num235" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Haec cum herodes audisset totus in furore metuque tractus, ea quae ad contumeliam dicta cognouit moleste tulit. Speculatores eis de quibus suspicabatur opposuit, et dum in opinione uel odio cunctos haberet, arbitrium protutela concipiens multum contra in fontes acerbus factus est. Sed magis ualidi uidebantur ei et terribiles quod non frequenter nominabat propter in solitam conuersationem, et si forte uocasset statim de interitu suo securi non erant. Postea uero omnes propinqui dum nihil habuissent firmum ad spem suae salutis contra se conuersi existimabant utile siquis anticipans alium accusset, et hoc sibi salutem posse conferre si suis facinoribus alios onerarent, et eo cadebant in quo ceteros insidiabantur immitere, nam regis paenitentia ne eos occideret quod non manifeste peccasent intercedebat ipsi. 					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num244" id="latin-book16-num244" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Horum autem omnium malorum antipater auctorerat, qui patris inconstantiam intelexerat, cum iam dudum ei consedisset unde magis suadere uidebatur ut auferretur unus quisque potentium. Tunc ergo rex andromachum ceteris expulso de conloquio uel fiducia, reliquos fidelissimos alexandri cum tormentis interrogabat, ut siquid contra se conflatum scirent edicerent. Quid moriebantur cuidum non haberent quod dicerent. Ille uero consumebatur quia tales quales existimabat non inueniebat. Callidus autem antipater quod ex ueritate ad constantiam et fidem deducere non ualebat, plus incitabat requirendo a pluribus latentem coniurationem, pro inde cum aliqui ex pluribus ortis retulisset quod cognosceret adulescentem cum laudaretur corporis eius magnitudo uel fagit tandi peritIa, cumque alia quae ad uirtutem super omnes haberet, haec sibi dixisse potius bona naturae officere dum pater inuideret. Et it circo ambulando cum eo sese humiliare ne longior appareret. In uenationibus uero cum sagittaret illo presente non recte iaculari propter genitoris inuidiam quam de gloria sua haberet. Cumque uerbum scrutaretur et remissio poenarum corporis interuenis sed, addebat quod fratrem aritobolum conscium haberet, ut inuanatione patrem perimentes ad romam confugerent regnumque peterent. Repertas uera et litteras adulescentis ad fratrem aristobolum in quibus patrem accusabat non iuste fecisse dum<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>terram tribuisset antipatro ducentorum talentorum talentorum reditus. Quibus relictis putauit herodis uerum existere quod de filiis suspicabatur et statim adprehendens alexandrum ligauit. Deinde uero remisit suam atrocitatem dum nec quae audisset crederet, et extimaret nihil dignum pro insidiis ex his conflatum apparuisse, sed querela esset uel iuuenilis teremeritas et quod manifeste interficientes romae confugerent non ueri simile uidebatur. Et maius aliquod sperans inuenire iniquitatis filii signum dicebat non sibi placere temerarie filium colligasse. Torquens autem amicos nobilis si mos alexandri non paucos, nihil penitus de quibus suspicabatur consessos inuenit. Cumque in hoc multus apparatus existeret et terrore uel turba palatium plenum esset unus quidam iuuenis ut in necessitatibus peruenit romam dixit transmisisse alexandrum et petisse ut cicius euocaretur a cesare habere se manifeste causam suggerere contra patrem quod regem parthorum tyridatim contra romanoss sibi reconciliasset, addens quia uenenum etiam alexander in ascalone ei parasset.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book16-num254" id="latin-book16-num254" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Tum herodes haec audiens et credens quod solatium temeritatis inuenisset, statim de ueneno precepit inquiri, quod tamen nullatenus potuit inuenire. Magnitudinem ergo malorum alexander uolens confirmare, negare quidem distulit, incitando temeritatem patris ad multa maiora delicta. Foraan autem et pro hoc amputare uolens facilitatem eius quam in accusationibus credendis habebat. Tamen nullatenus obtinuit dum omne regnum concutere uoluisset, siquidem litteras in quatuor libris destinauit dicens, quod non oporteret, torqueri quemquam nec ulterius hoc procedere quia reuera insidiae factae essent, in quas coniurasse feroram uel fidelissimos eius amicos afferebat. Id circo nec satisfactio ueritatis habebatur, sed indiscrete perdiciones pronuntiabantur. Cumque aliquibus uincula et aliis mortes aliis uero insperate dolores infligeret, turpiter regnum a priore felicitate de honestatum est. Et feuissima erat hero diuita dum turbatus nemini crederet, magnumque expectationis tormentum haberet, quod saepius super uenturum sibi filium crederet, ita noctu uel die mente turbatus in furorem et infaniam poene lapsus est.</tei-p>

XII. Igitur herodes sicut predixi consumptis suis pecuniis. Audiens hyrcanum ante se regem aperuisse tumulum dauid et tria milia talenturum inuenisse multo plus credens deposita quae, ad omnes sumptus suos sufficerent tumulum aperiens ingreditur noctu, dum nequaquam uellet hoc ciuitatem sentire unde si delissimos amicos tantum ducens pecunias quidem depositas sicut hyrcanus non inuenit, ornatum uero et uasa aurea plura tulit. Dumque omne studium poneret, et inquisitionem diligentiorem faceret ac uellet interius ingredi ad urnas inquibus dauid uel salomonis corpora posita erant, duo eius satellites flammis exusti sunt ab interiore parte occurentibus. Tunc ille timore perterritus egredi egreditur et propiaculo monumentum ex lapide candido ante ianuam magnificentissimis construxit expensis Cuius et nicolaus historiografus meminit sed descensum regis obtauit dum inhonestum hoc factum cognosceret quod semper in suis egit constriptis. Nam uiuente rege et cum eo degens ad gratias eius et fauorem eius tantum modo dicebat quae ad gloriam eius pertinebant. Multas uero iniquitates eius mutabat et cum multo studio caelabat. Nam mariae filiorumque eius mortes crudeliter factas ad satisfactiones cupiens perducere ut luxuriosa millam et adulescentes patris insidiatores accusauit. Res gestas autem regis amplioribus laudibus extollens, delictis eius studiose satisfacit uenia danda est quia non historia sed laudem conscripsit. Nos uero generi asamona eorum regum propinqui, et cum honore sacerdotum habentes aliquid mentiri non putauimus. Ideoque cum ueritate gestorum memoriam recensemus,
					in domesticis uero malis herodes constitutus affligebatur. [...]
					[...] Nam multi ex regis ira accipientes audaciam accusabant propinquos et amicos eius, quibus ita inter se dispositis nulla requies erat, siquidem salome inimica filiis mariae aristobolo suam filiam con uinctam nullatanus fidem ei seruare demittebat, dum flecteret eam ut quicquid locutus secrete fuisset nuntiare sibi. Et in altercationibus quae inter iugales saepius contingunt cogebat puellam dicere quae de marito sciebat. Illa uero dicebat quod saepius memoriam suae matris mariae faceret et quod patrem odio haberet. Frequenter autem terminaretur quia si principatum optineret filios quos herodes ab aliis uxoribus habebat, magistros litterarum in agris constitueret dum apta esset ad hoc opus quam habebant circa studia diligentia. Vxores uero si quando uiderent maternum in dui ornatum pro praesentibus ornamentis ciliciis intercludi ne solem uiderent, quae confestim per salome regi nunciata, dolorem eius inflammabant. Vrguebatur uero multo peius omnibus credens et inuicem se accusantibus tunc autem filiis interminatus satisfactionibus eorum ad praesens mollitus. In posterum atrocius exarsit.
					Nam ferora cum ad alexandrum uenisset et filiam archelai glafiram sicut praediximus habentem, salomem inquit dicentem audiui, quod herodes in amore glafire suae nurus incidisset et minime disiderii solatium possit inuenire. Quod ille audiens adulescentia uel emulatione commotus, quae honoris causa circa puellam ab herode fiebat, propter amorem haec eadem facere suspicabatur. Dolorem  ergo minus tollerans, patri nuntiauit cum lacrimis quae ferora dixisset. Herodes autem multo magis feruens, et mendacium inpudice criminationis non ferens turbatur, et saepius exclamans maliuolentiam familiarum qualis ipse erga eos fuisset, et qualis eos inuenisset. Conuocauit feroram quem huius modi adgressus pessime omnium in quo ad tam in mensam uel infandam in deuotinem peruenisti, ut alia de nobis existimes aut loquaris. Nonne uideo tuam uoluntatem quia non im meam iniuriam talia uerba producere sed insidias et uenena inmittere filio pro mea perditone festinasti. Quid enim alter nisi bonitate retentus quam hic puer in se habet portate potuisset in patrem non uindicare tam crudelem opinionem. Prius enim gladium in dextra quam hoc uerbum in animo eius debebas inmittere contra patrem. Quid autem conaris male loquendo de me nisi uteorum fauorem fraudibus tibi concilies. Nam talia dixisti, quae tuae impiaetatis fuissent cogitanda. Abscede iam pessime crica fratrem atque benefactorem, et tecum quidem haec malicia conscientiae conuiuat. Ego uero uindico sicut soleo meos, nec uindicans merito in eis sed magis beneficiis exornans quibus indigni esse nascuntur.

Repertas uera et litteras adulescentis ad fratrem aristobolum in quibus patrem accusabat non iuste fecisse dumterram tribuisset antipatro ducentorum talentorum talentorum reditus. Quibus relictis putauit herodis uerum existere quod de filiis suspicabatur et statim adprehendens alexandrum ligauit. Deinde uero remisit suam atrocitatem dum nec quae audisset crederet, et extimaret nihil dignum pro insidiis ex his conflatum apparuisse, sed querela esset uel iuuenilis teremeritas et quod manifeste interficientes romae confugerent non ueri simile uidebatur. Et maius aliquod sperans inuenire iniquitatis filii signum dicebat non sibi placere temerarie filium colligasse. Torquens autem amicos nobilis si mos alexandri non paucos, nihil penitus de quibus suspicabatur consessos inuenit. Cumque in hoc multus apparatus existeret et terrore uel turba palatium plenum esset unus quidam iuuenis ut in necessitatibus peruenit romam dixit transmisisse alexandrum et petisse ut cicius euocaretur a cesare habere se manifeste causam suggerere contra patrem quod regem parthorum tyridatim contra romanoss sibi reconciliasset, addens quia uenenum etiam alexander in ascalone ei parasset.
					Tum herodes haec audiens et credens quod solatium temeritatis inuenisset, statim de ueneno precepit inquiri, quod tamen nullatenus potuit inuenire. Magnitudinem ergo malorum alexander uolens confirmare, negare quidem distulit, incitando temeritatem patris ad multa maiora delicta. Foraan autem et pro hoc amputare uolens facilitatem eius quam in accusationibus credendis habebat. Tamen nullatenus obtinuit dum omne regnum concutere uoluisset, siquidem litteras in quatuor libris destinauit dicens, quod non oporteret, torqueri quemquam nec ulterius hoc procedere quia reuera insidiae factae essent, in quas coniurasse feroram uel fidelissimos eius amicos afferebat. Salomen autem noctu super se ingressam et cum inuito concubuisse, cunctosqui simul illic contra eum iure uenturos, quatenus eum occidentes  per ficere quod semper habere in expectatione meditasset inter hos etiam ptolomeus et sapinius fidelissimi regis accusantur, nam nihil aliud uidebatur quam sirabies quaedam incidisset beluarum more aut amicissimi contra se armarentur. Id circo nec satisfactio ueritatis habebatur, sed indiscrete perdiciones pronuntiabantur. Cumque aliquibus uincula et aliis mortes aliis uero insperate dolores infligeret, turpiter regnum a priore felicitate de honestatum est. Et feuissima erat hero diuita dum turbatus nemini crederet, magnumque expectationis tormentum haberet, quod saepius super uenturum sibi filium crederet, ita noctu uel die mente turbatus in furorem et infaniam poene lapsus est.

Greek.html: <tei-div2 type="chapter" n="12" data-synthetic-chapter="alignment-derived"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num179" xml:id="greek-book16-num179" id="greek-book16-num179" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="12" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" hidden="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[179]</tei-num> Ὁ γὰρ Ἡρώδης πολλοῖς τοῖς ἀναλώμασιν εἴς τε τὰς ἔξω καὶ τὰς ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ χρώμενος, ἀκηκοὼς ἔτι τάχιον ὡς Ὑρκανὸς ὁ πρὸ αὐτοῦ βασιλεὺς ἀνοίξας τὸν Δαυίδου τάφον ἀργυρίου λάβοι τρισχίλια τάλαντα κειμένων πολὺ πλειόνων ἔτι καὶ δυναμένων εἰς ἅπαν ἐπαρκέσαι ταῖς χορηγίαις, ἐκ πλείονος μὲν δι᾽ ἐννοίας εἶχεν τὴν ἐπιχείρησιν, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[180]</tei-num> ἐν δὲ τῷ τότε νυκτὸς ἀνοίξας τὸν τάφον εἰσέρχεται πραγματευσάμενος ἥκιστα μὲν τῇ πόλει φανερὸς εἶναι, παρειληφὼς δὲ τοὺς πιστοτάτους τῶν φίλων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[181]</tei-num> ἀποθέσιμα μὲν οὖν χρήματα καθάπερ Ὑρκανὸς οὐχ εὗρεν, κόσμον δὲ χρυσοῦν καὶ κειμηλίων πολύν, ὃν ἀνείλετο πάντα. σπουδὴν δ᾽ εἶχεν ἐπιμελεστέραν ποιούμενος τὴν ἔρευναν ἐνδοτέρω τε χωρεῖν καὶ κατὰ τὰς θήκας, ἐν αἷς ἦν τοῦ Δαυΐδου καὶ τοῦ Σολομῶνος τὰ σώματα. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[182]</tei-num> καὶ δύο μὲν αὐτῷ τῶν δορυφόρων διεφθάρησαν φλογὸς ἔνδοθεν εἰσιοῦσιν ἀπαντώσης, ὡς ἐλέγετο, περίφοβος δ᾽ αὐτὸς ἐξῄει, καὶ τοῦ δέους ἱλαστήριον μνῆμα λευκῆς πέτρας ἐπὶ τῷ στομίῳ κατεσκευάσατο πολυτελὲς τῇ δαπάνῃ. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[183]</tei-num> τούτου καὶ Νικόλαος ὁ κατ᾽ αὐτὸν ἱστοριογράφος μέμνηται τοῦ κατασκευάσματος, οὐ μὴν ὅτι καὶ κατῆλθεν, οὐκ εὐπρεπῆ τὴν πρᾶξιν ἐπιστάμενος. διατελεῖ δὲ καὶ τἆλλα τοῦτον τὸν τρόπον χρώμενος τῇ γραφῇ: <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[184]</tei-num> ζῶντι γὰρ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ καὶ σὺν αὐτῷ κεχαρισμένως ἐκείνῳ καὶ καθ᾽ ὑπηρεσίαν ἀνέγραφεν, μόνων ἁπτόμενος τῶν εὔκλειαν αὐτῷ φερόντων, πολλὰ δὲ καὶ τῶν ἐμφανῶς ἀδίκων ἀντικατασκευάζων καὶ μετὰ πάσης σπουδῆς ἐπικρυπτόμενος, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[185]</tei-num> ὅς γε καὶ τὸν Μαριάμμης θάνατον καὶ τῶν παίδων αὐτῆς οὕτως ὠμῶς τῷ βασιλεῖ πεπραγμένον εἰς εὐπρέπειαν ἀνάγειν βουλόμενος ἐκείνης τε ἀσέλγειαν καὶ τῶν νεανίσκων ἐπιβουλὰς καταψεύδεται, καὶ διατετέλεκεν τῇ γραφῇ τὰ μὲν πεπραγμένα δικαίως τῷ βασιλεῖ περιττότερον ἐγκωμιάζων, ὑπὲρ δὲ τῶν παρανομηθέντων ἐσπουδασμένως ἀπολογούμενος. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[186]</tei-num> ἐκείνῳ μὲν οὖν πολλὴν ἄν τις, ὡς ἔφην, ἔχοι τὴν συγγνώμην: οὐ γὰρ ἱστορίαν τοῖς ἄλλοις, ἀλλὰ ὑπουργίαν τῷ βασιλεῖ ταύτην ἐποιεῖτο. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[187]</tei-num> ἡμεῖς δὲ καὶ γένους ὄντες ἀγχοῦ τῶν ἐξ Ἀσαμωναίου βασιλέων καὶ διὰ τοῦτο σὺν τιμῇ τὴν ἱερωσύνην ἔχοντες τὸ ψεύσασθαί τι περὶ αὐτῶν οὐκ εὐπρεπὲς ὑπειληφότες καθαρῶς καὶ δικαίως ἐκτίθεμεν τὰς πράξεις, πολλοὺς μὲν τῶν ἐγγόνων τῶν ἐκείνου καὶ βασιλεύοντας ἔτι δι᾽ ἐντροπῆς ἔχοντες, τὴν δ᾽ ἀλήθειαν πρὸ ἐκείνων τετιμηκότες, ἣν ὅτε δικαίως ἐγίνετο συνέβη τε παρ᾽ αὐτοῖς ἐκείνοις ὀργῆ τυγχάνειν.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num188" xml:id="greek-book16-num188" id="greek-book16-num188" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[188]</tei-num> Ἡρώδης δὲ διὰ τὴν ἐπιχείρησιν, ἣν ἐποιήσατο τῷ τάφῳ, χεῖρον ἐδόκει πράττειν ἐν τοῖς κατὰ τὴν οἰκίαν, εἴτε δὴ τοῦ μηνίματος ἐπιδόντος εἰς ἃ μάλιστα καὶ πρότερον ἐνόσει πλείω γενέσθαι πρὸς ἀνηκέστους ἐξελθεῖν συμφοράς, εἴτε καὶ τῆς τύχης ἐν ἐκείνῳ τὴν ἐπίθεσιν ποιουμένης ἐν οἷς τὸ κατὰ τὴν αἰτίαν εὔκαιρον οὐ μικρὰν πίστιν παρεῖχεν τοῦ διὰ τὴν ἀσέβειαν αὐτῷ τὰς συμφορὰς ἀπηντηκέναι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[189]</tei-num> στάσις γὰρ ἦν ὥσπερ ἐμφυλίου πολέμου κατὰ τὴν αὐλὴν καὶ μίση πρὸς ἀλλήλους ἀνθυπερβαλλομένων ταῖς διαβολαῖς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[190]</tei-num> ἐστρατήγει δ᾽ ἀεὶ κατὰ τῶν ἀδελφῶν Ἀντίπατρος δεινὸς ὢν ἔξωθεν μὲν περιβάλλειν αὐτοὺς ταῖς αἰτίαις, αὐτὸς δὲ πολλάκις ἀπολογουμένου τόπον λαμβάνων, ἵν᾽ ᾖ τὸ δοκοῦν εὔνουν πιστὸν αὐτῷ πρὸς τὰς ἐπιχειρήσεις ὧν ἐδόκει. καὶ τούτῳ τῷ τρόπῳ ποικίλως ἐκπεριεληλύθει τὸν πατέρα μόνος ὑπὲρ τῆς ἐκείνου σωτηρίας ἅπαντα πράττειν αὐτὸς πεπιστευκώς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[191]</tei-num> ὁ δὲ καὶ Πτολεμαῖον, ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ διοικητὴς τῶν τῆς βασιλείας πραγμάτων, Ἀντιπάτρῳ συνίστη καὶ μετὰ τῆς ἐκείνου μητρὸς ὑπὲρ τῶν ἐπειγόντων ἐβουλεύετο. καὶ καθόλου τὰ πάντα ἦσαν οὗτοι καὶ πράττειν ὅσα θέλοιεν καὶ πρὸς δύσνοιαν ἄγειν τὸν βασιλέα τῶν ἔξωθεν οἷς ἐδόκει συμφέρειν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[192]</tei-num> οἱ δ᾽ ἐκ τῆς Μαριάμμης χαλεπώτερον ἀεὶ διετίθεντο, καὶ τὴν αἰτίαν ὑπ᾽ εὐγενείας οὐκ ἔφερον παρεωσμένοι καὶ τάξιν ἀτιμοτέραν ἔχοντες. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[193]</tei-num> αἵ γε μὴν γυναῖκες, ἡ μὲν Ἀλεξάνδρῳ συνοικοῦσα θυγάτηρ Ἀρχελάου Γλαφύρα μῖσος εἶχεν εἰς τὴν Σαλώμην κατά τε τὴν πρὸς τὸν ἄνδρα διάθεσιν κἀκ τοῦ πρὸς τὴν ἐκείνης θυγατέρα δοκεῖν ὑπερηφανώτερον διακεῖσθαι: συνῴκει μὲν γὰρ Ἀριστοβούλῳ, τὴν δὲ ἰσοτιμίαν αὐτῆς ἀναξιοπάθει Γλαφύρα.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num194" xml:id="greek-book16-num194" id="greek-book16-num194" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[194]</tei-num> Δευτέρας οὖν ταύτης ἔριδος ἐμπεπτωκυίας οὐδ᾽ ὁ τοῦ βασιλέως ἀδελφὸς Φερώρας ἔξω ταραχῆς ἦν, ἰδίαν δὲ ὑπόθεσιν ὑποψίας καὶ μίσους εἶχεν: ἐμπεπτώκει μὲν γὰρ εἰς ἔρωτα δουλευούσης αὐτῷ γυναικός, ἥττητο δὲ τῆς ἀνθρώπου μεμηνότως ἐπὶ τοσοῦτον κρατούμενος, ὥστ᾽ αὐτῷ καὶ τῆς τοῦ βασιλέως ἐγγυηθείσης θυγατρὸς τὴν μὲν ὑπερηφανῆσαι, πρὸς δὲ τῇ δούλῃ τὸν νοῦν εἶχεν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[195]</tei-num> ἤχθετο δὲ ἀτιμασθεὶς Ἡρώδης τῷ πολλὰ μὲν εὐεργετῆσαι τὸν ἀδελφόν, δυνάμει δὲ καὶ κοινωνὸν ἔχειν τῆς βασιλείας, οὐχ ὅμοιον εἰς τὰς ἀμοιβὰς ὁρῶν, κἀν τῷ προσώπῳ δυστυχεῖν ᾤετο. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[196]</tei-num> καὶ τὴν μὲν κόρην μὴ τυχὼν Φερώρα δικαίου παιδὶ Φασαήλου δίδωσιν, αὐτὸς δὲ χρόνου διελθόντος οἰόμενος ἤδη παρηκμακέναι τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν τἀδελφῷ περί τε τῶν πρώτων ᾐτιᾶτο καὶ τὴν δευτέραν ἠξίου λαμβάνειν, Κύπρος ἐκαλεῖτο. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[197]</tei-num> Φερώρᾳ δὲ συμβουλεύει Πτολεμαῖος ἤδη ποτὲ παυσαμένῳ τῆς εἰς τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἀτιμίας καταβαλεῖν τὸν ἔρωτα: καὶ γὰρ αἰσχρὸν εἶναι δούλης ἡττώμενον ἀποστερεῖν μὲν αὑτὸν τῆς εὐνοίας τῆς παρὰ βασιλέως, αἴτιον δὲ κἀκείνῳ ταραχῆς καὶ μίσους πρὸς αὐτὸν καθίστασθαι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[198]</tei-num> ταῦτ᾽ ἐκεῖνος ἰδὼν λυσιτελήσοντα τῷ καὶ πρότερον ἐν διαβολαῖς γενόμενος συνεγνῶσθαι, τὴν μὲν ἄνθρωπον ἤδη καὶ παῖδα ἐξ αὐτῆς ἔχων ἀποπέμπεται, βασιλεῖ δ᾽ ὡμολόγει λήψεσθαι τὴν δευτέραν αὐτοῦ θυγατέρα καὶ τριακοστὴν ἡμέραν συνέθετο τοῦ γάμου, συνεπομνύμενος ὡς οὐδὲν ἔτι κοινώνημα πρὸς τὴν ἀποπεμφθεῖσαν ἔσται. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[199]</tei-num> διελθουσῶν δὲ τῶν τριάκοντα ἡμερῶν τοσοῦτον ἦν ἥττων τοῦ ἔρωτος, ὥστε μηδὲν μὲν ἔτι ποιῆσαι τῶν ὡμολογημένων, πάλιν δὲ διατελεῖν ἐπὶ τῇ πρώτῃ. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[200]</tei-num> ταῦτα φανερῶς ἤδη τὸν Ἡρώδην ἐλύπει καὶ πρὸς ὀργὴν ἦγεν. ἦσαν οὖν λόγοι τινὲς ἀεὶ παραπίπτοντες παρ᾽ αὐτοῦ, καὶ πολλοὶ τὴν ὀργὴν τοῦ βασιλέως ἀφορμὴν τῶν κατὰ Φερώρου διαβολῶν ἐποιοῦντο. διέλειπεν δὲ οὐκ ἔσθ᾽ ἥτις ἡμέρα οὐδ᾽ ὥρα, καθ᾽ ἣν ἀτρεμεῖν αὐτῷ συνέβαινεν, ἀλλ᾽ ἀεί τι προσέπιπτεν καινῶν ἀγωνισμάτων συγγενῶν καὶ φιλτάτων εἰς ἀλλήλους πεποιημένων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[201]</tei-num> τοῦτο μὲν γὰρ ἡ Σαλώμη χαλεπὴ καὶ δύσνους οὖσα τοῖς ἐκ Μαριάμμης οὐδὲ τὴν ἑαυτῆς θυγατέρα συνοικοῦσαν Ἀριστοβούλῳ θατέρῳ τῶν νεανίσκων εἴα τῇ τοῦ γάμου πρὸς ἐκεῖνον εὐνοίᾳ χρῆσθαι, λέγειν τε εἴ τι λαλήσειεν κατ᾽ ἰδίαν ἀναπείθουσα καὶ μηνύειν ἑαυτῇ κἀν τοῖς προσκρούμασιν, οἷα συμβαίνει, πολλὰς ὑποψίας εἰσάγουσα. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[202]</tei-num> δι᾽ ὧν αὐτὴ μὲν ἅπαντα τὰ κατ᾽ ἐκείνους ἐμάνθανεν, δύσνουν δὲ τὴν παῖδα τῷ νεανίσκῳ πεποιήκει. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[203]</tei-num> χαριζομένη δ᾽ ἐκείνη τῇ μητρὶ πολλάκις ἔλεγεν, ὡς μέμνηνται μὲν ἰδιάζοντες ἐκεῖνοι τῆς Μαριάμμης, ἐστυγήκασι δὲ τὸν πατέρα, συνεχὲς δὲ διαπειλοῦσιν, εἰ τύχοιεν αὐτοί ποτε τῆς ἀρχῆς, τοὺς μὲν ἐκ τῶν ἄλλων γυναικῶν παῖδας Ἡρώδῃ γεγενημένους κωμογραμματεῖς καταστήσειν: ἁρμόσειν γὰρ εἰς τοιαύτην χρείαν τὸ νῦν ἐπιμελὲς αὐτῶν καὶ πρὸς παιδείαν ἐσπουδασμένον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[204]</tei-num> τὰς δὲ γυναῖκας, εἴ ποτε καὶ ταύτας ἴδοιεν τοῦ μητρῴου κόσμου μετειληφυίας, ἀντὶ τῆς παρούσης ἁβρότητος ἀπειλεῖν, ὡς τρύχεσιν ἠμφιεσμέναι καθειργοῦνται μηδὲ τὸν ἥλιον βλέπουσαι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[205]</tei-num> ταῦτ᾽ εὐθὺς ἀπηγγέλλετο διὰ τῆς Σαλώμης τῷ βασιλεῖ: κἀκεῖνος ἤκουεν μὲν ἀλγεινῶς, ἐπειρᾶτο δὲ διορθοῦν, ἐκακοῦτο δὲ ταῖς ὑποψίαις καὶ χείρων ἀεὶ γινόμενος ἅπασιν κατὰ πάντων ἐπίστευεν. οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ τότε μὲν ἐπιπλήξας τοῖς παισὶν ἀπολογησαμένων ῥᾴων εἰς τὸν καιρὸν ἐγίνετο, ταῖς δ᾽ ἑξῆς πολὺ χείρω προσέπεσεν.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num206" xml:id="greek-book16-num206" id="greek-book16-num206" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[206]</tei-num> Ὁ γὰρ Φερώρας ἐλθὼν παρὰ τὸν Ἀλέξανδρον ἔχοντα τὴν Ἀρχελάου θυγατέρα Γλαφύραν, ὡς ἐδηλώσαμεν, Σαλώμης ἔφη λεγούσης ἀκηκοέναι τὸν Ἡρώδην ἡττῆσθαι τοῦ τῆς Γλαφύρας ἔρωτος καὶ δυσπαρηγόρητον αὐτῷ τὴν ἐπιθυμίαν εἶναι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[207]</tei-num> τοῦτο οὖν ἐκεῖνος ἀκούσας ὑπό τε νεότητος καὶ ζηλοτυπίας ἐξεκαίετο καὶ τὰ κατὰ τιμὴν εἰς τὴν παῖδα γινόμενα παρ᾽ Ἡρώδου, πολλάκις δ᾽ ἦσαν αἱ τοιαῦται φιλοφρονήσεις, ἐπὶ τὸ χεῖρον ἐλάμβανεν ἐξ ὑπονοιῶν διὰ τὸν ἐκπεσόντα λόγον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[208]</tei-num> οὐκ ἐκαρτέρησέν τε τὴν ὀδύνην τοῦ πράγματος, ἀλλὰ ἐλθὼν πρὸς τὸν πατέρα καταμηνύει τὰ ὑπὸ τοῦ Φερώρα ῥηθέντα μετὰ δακρύων. Ἡρώδης δὲ πολὺ μᾶλλον ἐκπαθὴς γενόμενος καὶ τὸ σὺν αἰσχύνῃ τῆς διαβολῆς ἐψευσμένον οὐ φέρων ἐτετάρακτο. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[209]</tei-num> καὶ πολλάκις μὲν ὠδύρετο τὴν πονηρίαν τῶν οἰκείων οἷος εἰς αὐτοὺς γενόμενος οἵων τυγχάνοι, μεταπέμπεται δὲ τὸν Φερώραν καὶ προσονειδίσας ‘κάκιστε πάντων, εἶπεν, εἰς τοῦτο τῆς ἀμέτρου καὶ περιττῆς ἦλθες ἀχαριστίας, ὡς τοιαῦτα μὲν περὶ ἡμῶν νοῆσαι, τοιαῦτα δὲ λαλεῖν; <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[210]</tei-num> ἆρ᾽ οὐχ ὁρῶ τὴν σὴν προαίρεσιν, ὡς οὐ βλασφημίας ἐστοχασμένος τοὺς τοιούτους λόγους τῷ παιδὶ προσήνεγκας, ἐπιβουλὴν δὲ καὶ φάρμακον αὐτοὺς ποιούμενος τῆς ἐμῆς ἀπωλείας; τίς γὰρ ἄν, εἰ μὴ δαιμόνων ἀγαθῶν ἔτυχεν, ὥσπερ οὗτος ὁ παῖς, ἠνέσχετο τὸν πατέρα μὴ τίσασθαι διὰ τοιαύτην ὑποψίαν; <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[211]</tei-num> πότερον δὲ λόγον εἰς τὴν ψυχὴν ἢ ξίφος εἰς τὴν δεξιὰν ἐμβαλεῖν αὐτῷ δοκεῖς κατὰ τοῦ γεγεννηκότος; τί δέ σοι βούλεται τὸ μισοῦντά τε αὐτὸν καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ πρὸς μόνην τὴν κατ᾽ ἐμοῦ βλασφημίαν εὔνοιαν ὑποκρίνασθαι καὶ περὶ τούτων λέγειν, ἃ τῆς σῆς ἀσεβείας ἦν καὶ νοῆσαι καὶ διαβαλεῖν; <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[212]</tei-num> ἔρρε κάκιστος εἰς εὐεργέτην καὶ ἀδελφὸν γενόμενος. καὶ σοὶ μὲν ἡ συνείδησις αὕτη συζήσειεν, ἐγὼ δὲ νικῴην ἀεὶ τοὺς ἐμοὺς μήτε ἀμυνόμενος κατ᾽ ἀξίαν καὶ μειζόνως εὐεργετῶν ἢ τυχεῖν εἰσι δίκαιοι.’</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num213" xml:id="greek-book16-num213" id="greek-book16-num213" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[213]</tei-num> Τοιαῦτα μὲν οὖν ὁ βασιλεύς. Φερώρας δ᾽ ἐπ᾽ αὐτοφώρῳ τῇ μοχθηρίᾳ Σαλώμην ἔφη ταῦτα συμπείσειν καὶ παρ᾽ ἐκείνης εἶναι τοὺς λόγους. ἡ δὲ ὡς μόνον ἤκουσεν, ἐτύγχανεν δὲ παροῦσα, πιθανῶς ἀνεβόησεν, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[214]</tei-num> ὡς οὐδὲν εἴη παρ᾽ αὐτῆς τοιοῦτον, καὶ ὅτι διὰ σπουδῆς ἐστιν ἅπασιν εἰς μῖσος ἀγαγεῖν αὐτὴν τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ πάντα τρόπον ἐνέχειν διὰ τὴν εὔνοιαν, ἣν ἔχοι περὶ τὸν Ἡρώδην ἀεὶ προγινώσκουσα τοὺς κινδύνους. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[215]</tei-num> ἐν δὲ τῷ παρόντι καὶ μᾶλλον ἐπιβουλεύεσθαι: μόνη γὰρ ἀναπείθουσα τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἐκβάλλειν ἣν εἶχε γυναῖκα, λαμβάνειν δὲ θυγατέρα τὴν βασιλέως εἰκότως ὑπ᾽ ἐκείνου μεμισῆσθαι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[216]</tei-num> τοιαῦτα λεγούσης καὶ πολλάκις μὲν ἐπιδραττομένης τῶν τριχῶν, πολλάκις δὲ τυπτούσης τὰ στέρνα, ἡ μὲν ὄψις εἶχέ τι πρὸς τὴν ἄρνησιν πιθανόν, ἡ δὲ κακοήθεια τοῦ τρόπου τὴν ἐν τοῖς γινομένοις ὑπόκρισιν ἀπεσήμαινεν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[217]</tei-num> ὁ δὲ Φερώρας εἰς μέσον ἀπείληπτο μηδὲν εὔσχημον εἰς ἀπολογίαν ἔχων, εἰπεῖν μὲν ὡμολογηκώς, ἀκοῦσαι δ᾽ οὐ πιστευόμενος. ἐγένετο δ᾽ ἐπὶ πλεῖον ἥ τε σύγχυσις καὶ ἡ τῶν λόγων εἰς ἀλλήλους ἅμιλλα. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[218]</tei-num> τέλος δὲ ὁ βασιλεὺς τόν τε ἀδελφὸν καὶ τὴν ἀδελφὴν μεμισηκὼς ἀπεπέμπετο καὶ τὸν υἱὸν ἐπαινέσας τῆς ἐγκρατείας καὶ τοῦ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀνενεγκεῖν τοὺς λόγους ὀψὲ τῆς ὥρας περὶ θεραπείαν τοῦ σώματος ἐγένετο. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[219]</tei-num> τοιαύτης δὲ τῆς μάχης ἐμπεσούσης κακῶς ἤκουσεν ἡ Σαλώμη: παρ᾽ αὐτῆς γὰρ ἐδόκει κεκινῆσθαι τὰ περὶ τὴν διαβολήν: αἵ τε τοῦ βασιλέως γυναῖκες ἤχθοντο φύσει δυσχερεστάτην εἰδυῖαι καὶ γινομένην ἄλλοτ᾽ ἄλλην κατὰ καιροὺς ἐχθρὰν καὶ φίλην. ἔλεγον οὖν ἀεί τι πρὸς τὸν Ἡρώδην κατ᾽ αὐτῆς καί τι συμπεσὸν ἐπὶ μεῖζον ἤγαγεν τὴν εἰς τοῦτο παρρησίαν.</tei-p><tei-p sameas="#latin-book16-num220" xml:id="greek-book16-num220" id="greek-book16-num220"
