latin.html:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-2-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="23"><tei-div2 n="2" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed=""><tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num23" id="latin-book17-num23" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Tunc autem uolens aduersus trachonitas munitus existere, cogitauit uicum iudaeis aedificare non distante magnitudine ciuitatis ut per hoc inaccessibiles hostibus faceret limites suae prouinciae. Et cognoscens uirum quendam iudaeum ex babylonia cum aequitibus quingentis et sagittariis plurimis cognatorum etiam multitudinem usque ad centum ferme numerum uirorum eufratam fluuium transmeasse, et in antiochia in loco qui dicitur dafne syriae conuersari cum saturnino qui tunc ibidem imperator militiae consistebat. Illum ei locum ad habitandum benigna largitate cui balatha nomen erat caedere compromisit. Euocabat ergo eum cum tota multitudine omnium qui eum fuerant consecuti, spondens daturum se terram in regionem quaedicitur bathanea. Determinauerat enim eum in trachonitidem constituendum uolens eius habitationem obstaculum contra hostes habere. Promittebat itaque illam regionem sine tributis esse daturum et liberos fore quae moris erat illius regionis habitatoribus exibere inmunemque eis terram et nullis illationibus obnoxiam prebiturum.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num26" id="latin-book17-num26" data-origname="p" data-processed="">His persuasus babynius uenit et suscipiens regionem oppida, et municipia plura construxit.<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>Et uicum bathira nomine constituens obstaculum erat et oppositio quaedam ille uiret indigens aduersus trachonitas, et iudaeis de babylonia ad hierosilimm per sacrificiorum tempora uenientibus nequis eorum latrociniis trachonitarum insidiisque lederentur, et aduentabant ad eum plurimi, maximeque illi undique concurrebant aquibus paternus mos iudaeorum et instituta colebantur. Quibus rebus illa regio breui populosa facta est propter quod inmunis ab omnibus functionibus permanebat uiuente dum taxat herode. Ceterum post quam philippus filius eius principatum regni suscepit, modicas paruo tempore illis functiones inposuit, agrippas uero maior et filius eius qui omonimus quoque illi constabat eos ad modum grauare. Non tamen eis de libertate ipsorum cum possent ullam intulere molestiam sed romanide inde dominattum illius regionis adepti, libertatis quidem eorum etiam ipsi seruare dignitatem., inpositionibus autem eos functionum usque quaque grauauerunt. Et haec quidem oportuno tempore diligenter exequar oratione procedente.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num29" id="latin-book17-num29" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Zamaris autem babylonius inter haec uita defungitur qui ad possidendam qui ad possidendam illam regionem ab herode fuerat adquisitus, quique cum uirtute uiuens filios optimos quoque reliquerat iacimum quidem qui fortitudine darus extabat. Is aequites babylonios qui sub illo fuerant continebat et aeli, quos rex efficiebat ab unde muneribus. Sed iacimus in senectute defunctus philippum filium dereliquit, et manubonum et aliis uirtutis artibus usui supra quam libet accomodum. Ob hoc fida illa amicitia et firmissimus fauor cum agrippa rege prouenerat. Militiamque totam quam rex habebat iste curabat et ubicumque deducendam ratio postulabat eius regimine ducebatur</tei-p>
				</tei-div2>
				<tei-div2 n="3" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed="">
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num32" id="latin-book17-num32" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="3" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>III Herode autem inquibus rettuli constituto, in antipatrum spectabant cuncta negotia, propter quod utilis ac propitius a rege putabatur, et rex hoc firmitatem non amiserat potestatis quam ei pater<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00413.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="205r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>promptius indulgebat spe quasi fauoris eius ac fidei, ad haec erat etiam adderiuandam inde potestatem audacissimus quoniam incognita erat patri eius nequitia, et quoniam ad fidem faciendam indicendo callebat. Erat etiam cunctis terribilis non tantum magnitudine potestatis quantum peruersitate morum, et quod erat ad male loquendum procacissimus. Maxime autem cum foras accurabat uicissimque curabatur nam eum callide ualde circum uenerat antipater et maxime per mulieres ad occupandos eius animos ambigerat. Deditus quippe fuerat feroras uxori matrique eius atque sorori licet mulierum genus orreret ob iniuriam filiarum suarum uirginum, uerum tamen has patiebatur ab his quae ducebatur, et nihil ab eo sine illis mulieribus agebatur. Nam hominem illum etiam medicaminibus adcurabant, sed et sibi met in uicem cooperari nequaquam mutuo fauore cessabant. Ita enim eas omnimodis antipater induxerat partim per semet ipsum partim etiam per propriam matrem. Nam idem haec quattuor mulieres sentiebant idemque loquebantur. Ferorae tamen circa antipatrum in non nullis minimis sanerebus sententia mutabatur. Erat autem illis incontrarium nitens regis foror, iam diu cuncta circum inspiciens, et amicitiam eorum in perniciem herodis construi cernens, et adnun ciando non abstinens, illi autem sentientes molestam esse regi suam ad inuicem beniuolentiam consilium ineunt ut manifesta eorum non esset amicititia neque palam conuentum facerent. Odium autem et male loquia ubi tempus exigeret contra semet ipsos confingerent. Maxime autem subherodis praesentia. Ut ad eum de semet ipsis talia deferrent, secreto uero beniuolentia inter eos firmior cerciorque constaret et siquidem illi gerebant, salomam autem nihil prorsus latebat neque primum eorum propositum ad huius modi negotia festinare. Neque tunc quando secretas machinationes construebant. Cuncta quippe illorum illa mulier indagabat quae amplificans et atrociora faciens, ad fratem<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>proprium perferebat secretos eorum conuentus insinuans et conuiuia et consulationes occulte se motimque confestasque ad eius interitum tendere nisi maturius proderentur. Indicabat quoque illos in manifesto quidem aduersario semet suos quasi constare et ad laesiones mutuas fincte loqui finiteque festinare, secrete et ab alterutris remoti, beniuolentiam inter se confirmare maximam, et quotiens in quibusque negotiis singulis fierent, illud agere quod amicitia postularet et polliceri sibi etiam pugnare contra quos opus esset, modo ut illud astu uel fauore mutuo non sentirentur efficere. Illa quidem haec et huiusmodi inuestigabat omnia et integra ad fratem conueniens cuncta deferebat sentientem quidem iam etiam ipsum plurima per semet ipsum sed audiendum aliquid licet excitatus sororis accusationibus retardantem. Erat et enim etiam portio quaedam iudaeorum hominum de scrupulositate et subtilitate paterne legis gloriantium et culturam diuinatis simulantium a quibus inducabantur mulieres illae supra memoratae, hi pharisei dicebantur qui possent maxime regi non modicum afferre prefidium. Erant enim procaces ad bellum gerendum lesionesque inferendas inmaturius eleuaticum igitur cuncta gens iudaica iure iurando iurasset. Caesaris se propriam fore et omnibus regis fauere, isti uiri non iurauerunt. Erant autem numero supra sex fere milia, quod rex pecuniario damno multauerat. Illi uero beniuolentiam quasi prouicis situdine referentes, futurorum sibi agnitionem nutu diuinatis infusam esse praedicabant quod herodi uidelicet terminus regni iam esset ex superna maiestate decretus, tam ipsi quam enim uniuersae cognationi. lllam autem regnum possessuram atque feroram uel filios qui exeorum femine descensuri. Et haec quidem regni nunci abantur non enim saloniam ista fugiebant, et quoniam plurimos regalis aure corrumpere niterentur Rex autem interfecit pharisaeos qui causa seditionis extiterant, et uago an eunuchum et carum quendam qui tunc primatum inter eos <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00414.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="205v" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>habebat honestatis dignitate decoratum filiosque eius peremit, omnesque ei cognatione uel familiaritate coniunctos, quibus ille farisaeus praesagabat. Magnificabatur autem apud eos etiam uagoa sicuti pater et plurimis rebus benemeritus ac profuturus apud regem futurum. In manibus enim eius cuncta fore praedicabat prebente illi et coniugii firmitatem et filiorum ueluti propriis filiis.</tei-p>
				</tei-div2>
				<tei-div2 n="4" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed="">
					</tei-div2></tei-div>

Illum ei locum ad habitandum benigna largitate cui balatha nomen erat caedere compromisit. Euocabat ergo eum cum tota multitudine omnium qui eum fuerant consecuti, spondens daturum se terram in regionem quaedicitur bathanea. Determinauerat enim eum in trachonitidem constituendum uolens eius habitationem obstaculum contra hostes habere. Promittebat itaque illam regionem sine tributis esse daturum et liberos fore quae moris erat illius regionis habitatoribus exibere inmunemque eis terram et nullis illationibus obnoxiam prebiturum. His persuasus babynius uenit et suscipiens regionem oppida, et municipia plura construxit.Et uicum bathira nomine constituens obstaculum erat et oppositio quaedam ille uiret indigens aduersus trachonitas, et iudaeis de babylonia ad hierosilimm per sacrificiorum tempora uenientibus nequis eorum latrociniis trachonitarum insidiisque lederentur, et aduentabant ad eum plurimi, maximeque illi undique concurrebant aquibus paternus mos iudaeorum et instituta colebantur. Quibus rebus illa regio breui populosa facta est propter quod inmunis ab omnibus functionibus permanebat uiuente dum taxat herode. Ceterum post quam philippus filius eius principatum regni suscepit, modicas paruo tempore illis functiones inposuit, agrippas uero maior et filius eius qui omonimus quoque illi constabat eos ad modum grauare. Non tamen eis de libertate ipsorum cum possent ullam intulere molestiam sed romanide inde dominattum illius regionis adepti, libertatis quidem eorum etiam ipsi seruare dignitatem., inpositionibus autem eos functionum usque quaque grauauerunt. Et haec quidem oportuno tempore diligenter exequar oratione procedente. Zamaris autem babylonius inter haec uita defungitur qui ad possidendam qui ad possidendam illam regionem ab herode fuerat adquisitus, quique cum uirtute uiuens filios optimos quoque reliquerat iacimum quidem qui fortitudine darus extabat. Is aequites babylonios qui sub illo fuerant continebat et aeli, quos rex efficiebat ab unde muneribus. Sed iacimus in senectute defunctus philippum filium dereliquit, et manubonum et aliis uirtutis artibus usui supra quam libet accomodum. Ob hoc fida illa amicitia et firmissimus fauor cum agrippa rege prouenerat. Militiamque totam quam rex habebat iste curabat et ubicumque deducendam ratio postulabat eius regimine ducebatur III Herode autem inquibus rettuli constituto, in antipatrum spectabant cuncta negotia, propter quod utilis ac propitius a rege putabatur, et rex hoc firmitatem non amiserat potestatis quam ei paterpromptius indulgebat spe quasi fauoris eius ac fidei, ad haec erat etiam adderiuandam inde potestatem audacissimus quoniam incognita erat patri eius nequitia, et quoniam ad fidem faciendam indicendo callebat. Erat etiam cunctis terribilis non tantum magnitudine potestatis quantum peruersitate morum, et quod erat ad male loquendum procacissimus. Maxime autem cum foras accurabat uicissimque curabatur nam eum callide ualde circum uenerat antipater et maxime per mulieres ad occupandos eius animos ambigerat. Deditus quippe fuerat feroras uxori matrique eius atque sorori licet mulierum genus orreret ob iniuriam filiarum suarum uirginum, uerum tamen has patiebatur ab his quae ducebatur, et nihil ab eo sine illis mulieribus agebatur. Nam hominem illum etiam medicaminibus adcurabant, sed et sibi met in uicem cooperari nequaquam mutuo fauore cessabant. Ita enim eas omnimodis antipater induxerat partim per semet ipsum partim etiam per propriam matrem. Nam idem haec quattuor mulieres sentiebant idemque loquebantur. Ferorae tamen circa antipatrum in non nullis minimis sanerebus sententia mutabatur. Erat autem illis incontrarium nitens regis foror, iam diu cuncta circum inspiciens, et amicitiam eorum in perniciem herodis construi cernens, et adnun ciando non abstinens, illi autem sentientes molestam esse regi suam ad inuicem beniuolentiam consilium ineunt ut manifesta eorum non esset amicititia neque palam conuentum facerent. Odium autem et male loquia ubi tempus exigeret contra semet ipsos confingerent. Maxime autem subherodis praesentia. Ut ad eum de semet ipsis talia deferrent, secreto uero beniuolentia inter eos firmior cerciorque constaret et siquidem illi gerebant, salomam autem nihil prorsus latebat neque primum eorum propositum ad huius modi negotia festinare. Neque tunc quando secretas machinationes construebant. Cuncta quippe illorum illa mulier indagabat quae amplificans et atrociora faciens, ad fratemproprium perferebat secretos eorum conuentus insinuans et conuiuia et consulationes occulte se motimque confestasque ad eius interitum tendere nisi maturius proderentur. Indicabat quoque illos in manifesto quidem aduersario semet suos quasi constare et ad laesiones mutuas fincte loqui finiteque festinare, secrete et ab alterutris remoti, beniuolentiam inter se confirmare maximam, et quotiens in quibusque negotiis singulis fierent, illud agere quod amicitia postularet et polliceri sibi etiam pugnare contra quos opus esset, modo ut illud astu uel fauore mutuo non sentirentur efficere. Illa quidem haec et huiusmodi inuestigabat omnia et integra ad fratem conueniens cuncta deferebat sentientem quidem iam etiam ipsum plurima per semet ipsum sed audiendum aliquid licet excitatus sororis accusationibus retardantem. Erat et enim etiam portio quaedam iudaeorum hominum de scrupulositate et subtilitate paterne legis gloriantium et culturam diuinatis simulantium a quibus inducabantur mulieres illae supra memoratae, hi pharisei dicebantur qui possent maxime regi non modicum afferre prefidium. Erant enim procaces ad bellum gerendum lesionesque inferendas inmaturius eleuaticum igitur cuncta gens iudaica iure iurando iurasset. Caesaris se propriam fore et omnibus regis fauere, isti uiri non iurauerunt. Erant autem numero supra sex fere milia, quod rex pecuniario damno multauerat. Illi uero beniuolentiam quasi prouicis situdine referentes, futurorum sibi agnitionem nutu diuinatis infusam esse praedicabant quod herodi uidelicet terminus regni iam esset ex superna maiestate decretus, tam ipsi quam enim uniuersae cognationi. lllam autem regnum possessuram atque feroram uel filios qui exeorum femine descensuri. Et haec quidem regni nunci abantur non enim saloniam ista fugiebant, et quoniam plurimos regalis aure corrumpere niterentur Rex autem interfecit pharisaeos qui causa seditionis extiterant, et uago an eunuchum et carum quendam qui tunc primatum inter eos habebat honestatis dignitate decoratum filiosque eius peremit, omnesque ei cognatione uel familiaritate coniunctos, quibus ille farisaeus praesagabat. Magnificabatur autem apud eos etiam uagoa sicuti pater et plurimis rebus benemeritus ac profuturus apud regem futurum. In manibus enim eius cuncta fore praedicabat prebente illi et coniugii firmitatem et filiorum ueluti propriis filiis.

greek.html:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-2-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="23"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num23" xml:id="greek-book17-num23" id="greek-book17-num23" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[23]</tei-num> Τότε δὲ βουλόμενος πρὸς Τραχωνίτας ἀσφαλὴς εἶναι, κώμην πόλεως μέγεθος οὐκ ἀποδέουσαν ἔγνω Ἰουδαίων κτίσαι ἐν μέσῳ, δυσέμβολόν τε ποιεῖν τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῖς πολεμίοις ἐξ ἐγγίονος ὁρμώμενος ἐκ τοῦ ὀξέος κακουργεῖν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[24]</tei-num> καὶ ἐπιστάμενος ἄνδρα Ἰουδαῖον ἐκ τῆς Βαβυλωνίας σὺν πεντακοσίοις ἱπποτοξόταις πᾶσι καὶ συγγενῶν πλήθει εἰς ἑκατὸν ἀνδρῶν τὸν Εὐφράτην διαβεβηκότα κατὰ τύχας ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τῇ ἐπὶ Δάφνῃ τῆς Συρίας διαιτᾶσθαι Σατορνίνου τοῦ τότε στρατηγοῦντος εἰς ἐνοίκησιν αὐτῷ δεδωκότος χωρίον, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[25]</tei-num> Οὐλαθὰ ὄνομα αὐτῷ, μετεπέμπετο τοῦτον σὺν τῷ πλήθει τῶν ἑπομένων, παρέξειν ὑπισχνούμενος γῆν ἐν τοπαρχίᾳ τῇ λεγομένῃ Βαταναίᾳ, ὡρίζετο δὲ αὕτη τῇ Τραχωνίτιδι, βουλόμενος πρόβλημα τὴν κατοίκησιν αὐτοῦ κτᾶσθαι, ἀτελῆ τε τὴν χώραν ἐπηγγέλλετο καὶ αὐτοὺς εἰσφορῶν ἀπηλλαγμένους ἁπασῶν, αἳ εἰωθυῖαι ἐγκατοικεῖν τὴν γῆν ἄπρακτον παρασχόμενος.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num26" xml:id="greek-book17-num26" id="greek-book17-num26" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[26]</tei-num> Τούτοις πεισθεὶς ὁ Βαβυλώνιος ἀφικνεῖται καὶ λαβὼν τὴν γῆν φρούρια ᾠκοδομήσατο καὶ κώμην, Βαρθύραν ὄνομα αὐτῇ θέμενος. πρόβλημά τε ἦν οὗτος ὁ ἀνὴρ καὶ τοῖς ἐγχωρίοις τὰ πρὸς τοὺς Τραχωνίτας καὶ Ἰουδαίων τοῖς ἐκ Βαβυλῶνος ἀφικνουμένοις κατὰ θυσίαν ἐπὶ Ἱεροσολύμων τοῦ μὴ λῃστείαις ὑπὸ τῶν Τραχωνιτῶν κακουργεῖσθαι, πολλοί τε ὡς αὐτὸν ἀφίκοντο καὶ ἁπανταχόθεν, οἷς τὰ Ἰουδαίων θεραπεύεται πάτρια. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[27]</tei-num> καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ χώρα σφόδρα πολυάνθρωπος ἀδείᾳ τοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσιν ἀτελοῦς, ἃ παρέμεινεν αὐτοῖς Ἡρώδου ζῶντος. Φίλιππος δὲ υἱὸς ἐκείνου παραλαβὼν τὴν ἀρχὴν ὀλίγα τε καὶ ἐπ᾽ ὀλίγοις αὐτοὺς ἐπράξατο, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[28]</tei-num> Ἀγρίππας μέντοι γε ὁ μέγας καὶ ὁ παῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁμώνυμος καὶ πάνυ ἐξετρύχωσαν αὐτούς, οὐ μέντοι τὰ τῆς ἐλευθερίας κινεῖν ἠθέλησαν. παρ᾽ ὧν Ῥωμαῖοι δεξάμενοι τὴν ἀρχὴν τοῦ μὲν ἐλευθέρου καὶ αὐτοὶ τηροῦσιν τὴν ἀξίωσιν, ἐπιβολαῖς δὲ τῶν φόρων εἰς τὸ πάμπαν ἐπίεσαν αὐτούς. καὶ τάδε μὲν ᾗ καιρὸς ἀκριβώσομαι προϊόντος τοῦ λόγου.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num29" xml:id="greek-book17-num29" id="greek-book17-num29" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[29]</tei-num> Τελευτᾷ δὲ Ζάμαρις ὁ Βαβυλώνιος, ὃς ἐπὶ κτήσει τῆσδε τῆς χώρας Ἡρώδῃ προσποιεῖται, ζήσας τε μετὰ ἀρετῆς καὶ παῖδας λειπόμενος ἀγαθούς, Ἰάκειμον μέν, ὃς ἀνδρείᾳ γενόμενος ἐπιφανὴς ἱππεύειν συνεκρότησε τὸ ὑφ᾽ αὑτῷ Βαβυλώνιον, καὶ ἴλη τῶνδε τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐδορυφόρει τούσδε τοὺς βασιλέας. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[30]</tei-num> καὶ Ἰάκειμος δὲ ἐν γήρᾳ τελευτῶν Φίλιππον τὸν υἱὸν κατέλιπεν ἄνδρα κατὰ χεῖρας ἀγαθὸν καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ἀρετῇ χρῆσθαι παρ᾽ ὁντινοῦν ἀξιόλογον. διόπερ φιλία <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[31]</tei-num> τε πιστὴ καὶ εὔνοια ἀσφαλὴς αὐτῷ πρὸς Ἀγρίππαν γίνεται τὸν βασιλέα, στρατιάν τε ὁπόσην ὁ βασιλεὺς ἔτρεφεν οὗτος ἀσκῶν διετέλει καὶ ὅπη ἐξοδεύειν δεήσειεν ἡγούμενος.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num32" xml:id="greek-book17-num32" id="greek-book17-num32" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="3" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[32]</tei-num> Ἡρώδου δ᾽ ἐν οἷς εἶπον ὄντος ἀφεώρα τὰ πάντα πράγματα εἰς Ἀντίπατρον, κἀφ᾽ οἷς ὠφελήσειεν κυροῦν οὐκ ἀπήλλακτο ἐξουσίας ἐπικεχωρηκότος τε τοῦ πατρὸς ἐλπίδι εὐνοίας καὶ πίστεως, καὶ περαιτέρω κτᾶσθαι τὴν ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τολμηρὸς καθιστάμενος διὰ τὸ ἄδηλος τῷ πατρὶ εἶναι κακουργῶν κἀφ᾽ οἷς εἴπειεν πιστότατος. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[33]</tei-num> ἦν τε πᾶσιν φοβερὸς οὐχ οὕτως ἰσχύι τῆς ἐξουσίας, ὡς τοῦ κακοτρόπου τῷ προμηθεῖ: μάλιστα δ᾽ αὐτὸν Φερώρας ἐθεράπευεν καὶ ἀντεθεραπεύετο δεινῶς, πάνυ τοῦ Ἀντιπάτρου περιστοιχίσαντος αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν γυναικωνῖτιν συνισταμένου τὰ πρὸς αὐτόν: <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[34]</tei-num> ἐδεδούλωτο γὰρ Φερώρας γαμετῇ τε καὶ μητρὶ ταύτης καὶ ἀδελφῇ καὶ ταῦτα μισῶν τὰς ἀνθρώπους ὕβρει θυγατέρων αὐτοῦ παρθένων: ἀλλ᾽ ὅμως ἠνείχετο, πράσσειν τε οὐδὲν ἦν δίχα τῶν γυναικῶν ἐκπεριωδευκυιῶν τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ ἀλλήλαις εὐνοίᾳ συμπράσσειν τὰ πάντα μὴ ἀπηλλαγμένων, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[35]</tei-num> ὥστε παντοίως ὁ Ἀντίπατρος ὑπῆκτο αὐτὰς καὶ δι᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ διὰ τῆς μητρός: ταὐτὸν γὰρ αἵδε αἱ τέσσαρες γυναῖκες ἔλεγον. καὶ Φερώρᾳ δὲ πρὸς Ἀντίπατρον ἐπ᾽ οὐδαμινοῖς τισιν αἱ γνῶμαι διήλλασσον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[36]</tei-num> ἀντίσπασμα δ᾽ ἦν αὐτοῖς βασιλέως ἡ ἀδελφὴ περισκοποῦσά τε ἐκ πλείονος τὰ πάντα καὶ τὴν εὔνοιαν αὐτῶν ἐπὶ κακοῖς τοῖς Ἡρώδου πρασσομένην εἰδυῖά τε καὶ μηνύειν οὐκ ἀποτετραμμένη. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[37]</tei-num> καὶ γνόντες ἐν ἀπεχθείᾳ βασιλεῖ τὴν εὔνοιαν αὐτῶν οὖσαν ἐπινοοῦσιν ὥστε φανερὰν μὲν μὴ εἶναι τὴν πρὸς ἀλλήλους αὐτῶν σύνοδον, μίσους δὲ καὶ λοιδοριῶν ᾗ καιρὸς προσποίησιν, καὶ μάλιστα Ἡρώδου παρατυγχάνοντος ἢ οἳ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀπαγγέλλειν ἔμελλον, κρυπτῶς δὲ τὰ τῆς εὐνοίας ὀχυρώτερα καθίστασθαι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[38]</tei-num> καὶ ἔπρασσον οὕτως. ἐλάνθανεν δὲ τὴν Σαλώμην οὔτε πρῶτον ἡ διάνοια αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τοιοῖσδε ὡρμημένων οὔτε ἐπειδὴ * χρῆσθαι οὐκ ἀπήλλακτο αὐτή: πάντα δὲ ἀνίχνευέν τε καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν μειζόνως ἐκδεινοῦσα ἀπεσήμαινεν συνόδους τε κρυπτὰς καὶ πότους βουλευτήριά τε ἀφανῶς κατεσκευασμένα, ὧν μὴ ἐπ᾽ ὀλέθρῳ τῷ ἐκείνου συντιθεμένων κἂν πεφανερῶσθαι μὴ κεκωλῦσθαι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[39]</tei-num> νῦν δὲ τοὺς μὲν ἐκ τοῦ προὔπτου διαφόρους καὶ τὰ πάντα ἐπὶ βλάβῃ τῇ ἀλλήλων λέγοντας, εἰς δὲ τὸ ἀφανὲς τοῖς πολλοῖς τὴν εὔνοιαν ἀνατιθεμένους καὶ ὁπότε ἀλλήλοις συμμονωθεῖεν φίλια πράσσειν μὴ ἀπηλλαγμένους, ὁμολογεῖν πολεμεῖν πρὸς οὓς λανθάνειν χρώμενοι εὐνοίᾳ τῇ ἀλλήλων ἐσπουδάκοιεν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[40]</tei-num> καὶ ἡ μὲν ταῦτ᾽ ἀνίχνευέν τε καὶ ἀκριβῶν τυγχάνουσα τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἀνέφερεν συνιέντι μὲν ἤδη τὰ πολλὰ καὶ δι᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, εἰς δὲ τὸ θαρσεῖν οὐ διακενῆς ὑπονοῶν καθισταμένῳ διαβολαῖς τῆς ἀδελφῆς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[41]</tei-num> καὶ ἦν γὰρ μόριόν τι Ἰουδαϊκὸν ἀνθρώπων ἐπ᾽ ἐξακριβώσει μέγα φρονοῦν τοῦ πατρίου καὶ νόμων οἷς χαίρει τὸ θεῖον προσποιουμένων, οἷς ὑπῆκτο ἡ γυναικωνῖτις, Φαρισαῖοι καλοῦνται, βασιλεῖ δυναμένῳ μάλιστα πράσσειν προμηθεῖς κἀκ τοῦ προὔπτου εἰς τὸ πολεμεῖν τε καὶ βλάπτειν ἐπηρμένοι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[42]</tei-num> παντὸς γοῦν τοῦ Ἰουδαϊκοῦ βεβαιώσαντος δι᾽ ὅρκων ἦ μὴν εὐνοήσειν Καίσαρι καὶ τοῖς βασιλέως πράγμασιν, οἵδε οἱ ἄνδρες οὐκ ὤμοσαν ὄντες ὑπὲρ ἑξακισχίλιοι, καὶ αὐτοὺς βασιλέως ζημιώσαντος χρήμασιν ἡ Φερώρου γυνὴ τὴν ζημίαν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν εἰσφέρει. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[43]</tei-num> οἱ δὲ ἀμειβόμενοι τὴν εὔνοιαν αὐτῆς, πρόγνωσιν δὲ ἐπεπίστευντο ἐπιφοιτήσει τοῦ θεοῦ, προύλεγον, ὡς Ἡρώδῃ μὲν καταπαύσεως ἀρχῆς ὑπὸ θεοῦ ἐψηφισμένης αὐτῷ τε καὶ γένει τῷ ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ, τῆς δὲ βασιλείας εἴς τε ἐκείνην περιηξούσης καὶ Φερώραν παῖδάς τε οἳ εἶεν αὐτοῖς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[44]</tei-num> καὶ τάδε, οὐ γὰρ ἐλάνθανεν τὴν Σαλώμην, ἐξάγγελτα βασιλεῖ ἦν, καὶ ὅτι τῶν περὶ τὴν αὐλὴν διαφθείροιέν τινας. καὶ βασιλεὺς τῶν τε Φαρισαίων τοὺς αἰτιωτάτους ἀναιρεῖ καὶ Βαγώαν τὸν εὐνοῦχον Κᾶρόν τέ τινα τῶν τότε προύχοντα ἀρετῇ τοῦ εὐπρεποῦς καὶ παιδικὰ ὄντα αὐτοῦ. κτείνει δὲ καὶ πᾶν ὅ τι τοῦ οἰκείου συνειστήκει οἷς ὁ Φαρισαῖος ἔλεγεν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[45]</tei-num> ἦρτο δὲ ὁ Βαγώας ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν ὡς πατήρ τε καὶ εὐεργέτης ὀνομασθησόμενος τοῦ ἐπικατασταθησομένου προρρήσει βασιλέως: κατὰ χεῖρα γὰρ ἐκείνῳ τὰ πάντ᾽ εἶναι, παρέξοντος αὐτῷ γάμου τε ἰσχὺν καὶ παιδώσεως τέκνων γνησίων.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
greek.text: [23] Τότε δὲ βουλόμενος πρὸς Τραχωνίτας ἀσφαλὴς εἶναι, κώμην πόλεως μέγεθος οὐκ ἀποδέουσαν ἔγνω Ἰουδαίων κτίσαι ἐν μέσῳ, δυσέμβολόν τε ποιεῖν τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ τοῖς πολεμίοις ἐξ ἐγγίονος ὁρμώμενος ἐκ τοῦ ὀξέος κακουργεῖν. [24] καὶ ἐπιστάμενος ἄνδρα Ἰουδαῖον ἐκ τῆς Βαβυλωνίας σὺν πεντακοσίοις ἱπποτοξόταις πᾶσι καὶ συγγενῶν πλήθει εἰς ἑκατὸν ἀνδρῶν τὸν Εὐφράτην διαβεβηκότα κατὰ τύχας ἐν Ἀντιοχείᾳ τῇ ἐπὶ Δάφνῃ τῆς Συρίας διαιτᾶσθαι Σατορνίνου τοῦ τότε στρατηγοῦντος εἰς ἐνοίκησιν αὐτῷ δεδωκότος χωρίον, [25] Οὐλαθὰ ὄνομα αὐτῷ, μετεπέμπετο τοῦτον σὺν τῷ πλήθει τῶν ἑπομένων, παρέξειν ὑπισχνούμενος γῆν ἐν τοπαρχίᾳ τῇ λεγομένῃ Βαταναίᾳ, ὡρίζετο δὲ αὕτη τῇ Τραχωνίτιδι, βουλόμενος πρόβλημα τὴν κατοίκησιν αὐτοῦ κτᾶσθαι, ἀτελῆ τε τὴν χώραν ἐπηγγέλλετο καὶ αὐτοὺς εἰσφορῶν ἀπηλλαγμένους ἁπασῶν, αἳ εἰωθυῖαι ἐγκατοικεῖν τὴν γῆν ἄπρακτον παρασχόμενος. [26] Τούτοις πεισθεὶς ὁ Βαβυλώνιος ἀφικνεῖται καὶ λαβὼν τὴν γῆν φρούρια ᾠκοδομήσατο καὶ κώμην, Βαρθύραν ὄνομα αὐτῇ θέμενος. πρόβλημά τε ἦν οὗτος ὁ ἀνὴρ καὶ τοῖς ἐγχωρίοις τὰ πρὸς τοὺς Τραχωνίτας καὶ Ἰουδαίων τοῖς ἐκ Βαβυλῶνος ἀφικνουμένοις κατὰ θυσίαν ἐπὶ Ἱεροσολύμων τοῦ μὴ λῃστείαις ὑπὸ τῶν Τραχωνιτῶν κακουργεῖσθαι, πολλοί τε ὡς αὐτὸν ἀφίκοντο καὶ ἁπανταχόθεν, οἷς τὰ Ἰουδαίων θεραπεύεται πάτρια. [27] καὶ ἐγένετο ἡ χώρα σφόδρα πολυάνθρωπος ἀδείᾳ τοῦ ἐπὶ πᾶσιν ἀτελοῦς, ἃ παρέμεινεν αὐτοῖς Ἡρώδου ζῶντος. Φίλιππος δὲ υἱὸς ἐκείνου παραλαβὼν τὴν ἀρχὴν ὀλίγα τε καὶ ἐπ᾽ ὀλίγοις αὐτοὺς ἐπράξατο, [28] Ἀγρίππας μέντοι γε ὁ μέγας καὶ ὁ παῖς αὐτοῦ καὶ ὁμώνυμος καὶ πάνυ ἐξετρύχωσαν αὐτούς, οὐ μέντοι τὰ τῆς ἐλευθερίας κινεῖν ἠθέλησαν. παρ᾽ ὧν Ῥωμαῖοι δεξάμενοι τὴν ἀρχὴν τοῦ μὲν ἐλευθέρου καὶ αὐτοὶ τηροῦσιν τὴν ἀξίωσιν, ἐπιβολαῖς δὲ τῶν φόρων εἰς τὸ πάμπαν ἐπίεσαν αὐτούς. καὶ τάδε μὲν ᾗ καιρὸς ἀκριβώσομαι προϊόντος τοῦ λόγου. [29] Τελευτᾷ δὲ Ζάμαρις ὁ Βαβυλώνιος, ὃς ἐπὶ κτήσει τῆσδε τῆς χώρας Ἡρώδῃ προσποιεῖται, ζήσας τε μετὰ ἀρετῆς καὶ παῖδας λειπόμενος ἀγαθούς, Ἰάκειμον μέν, ὃς ἀνδρείᾳ γενόμενος ἐπιφανὴς ἱππεύειν συνεκρότησε τὸ ὑφ᾽ αὑτῷ Βαβυλώνιον, καὶ ἴλη τῶνδε τῶν ἀνδρῶν ἐδορυφόρει τούσδε τοὺς βασιλέας. [30] καὶ Ἰάκειμος δὲ ἐν γήρᾳ τελευτῶν Φίλιππον τὸν υἱὸν κατέλιπεν ἄνδρα κατὰ χεῖρας ἀγαθὸν καὶ τὰ ἄλλα ἀρετῇ χρῆσθαι παρ᾽ ὁντινοῦν ἀξιόλογον. διόπερ φιλία [31] τε πιστὴ καὶ εὔνοια ἀσφαλὴς αὐτῷ πρὸς Ἀγρίππαν γίνεται τὸν βασιλέα, στρατιάν τε ὁπόσην ὁ βασιλεὺς ἔτρεφεν οὗτος ἀσκῶν διετέλει καὶ ὅπη ἐξοδεύειν δεήσειεν ἡγούμενος. [32] Ἡρώδου δ᾽ ἐν οἷς εἶπον ὄντος ἀφεώρα τὰ πάντα πράγματα εἰς Ἀντίπατρον, κἀφ᾽ οἷς ὠφελήσειεν κυροῦν οὐκ ἀπήλλακτο ἐξουσίας ἐπικεχωρηκότος τε τοῦ πατρὸς ἐλπίδι εὐνοίας καὶ πίστεως, καὶ περαιτέρω κτᾶσθαι τὴν ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τολμηρὸς καθιστάμενος διὰ τὸ ἄδηλος τῷ πατρὶ εἶναι κακουργῶν κἀφ᾽ οἷς εἴπειεν πιστότατος. [33] ἦν τε πᾶσιν φοβερὸς οὐχ οὕτως ἰσχύι τῆς ἐξουσίας, ὡς τοῦ κακοτρόπου τῷ προμηθεῖ: μάλιστα δ᾽ αὐτὸν Φερώρας ἐθεράπευεν καὶ ἀντεθεραπεύετο δεινῶς, πάνυ τοῦ Ἀντιπάτρου περιστοιχίσαντος αὐτὸν καὶ τὴν γυναικωνῖτιν συνισταμένου τὰ πρὸς αὐτόν: [34] ἐδεδούλωτο γὰρ Φερώρας γαμετῇ τε καὶ μητρὶ ταύτης καὶ ἀδελφῇ καὶ ταῦτα μισῶν τὰς ἀνθρώπους ὕβρει θυγατέρων αὐτοῦ παρθένων: ἀλλ᾽ ὅμως ἠνείχετο, πράσσειν τε οὐδὲν ἦν δίχα τῶν γυναικῶν ἐκπεριωδευκυιῶν τὸν ἄνθρωπον καὶ ἀλλήλαις εὐνοίᾳ συμπράσσειν τὰ πάντα μὴ ἀπηλλαγμένων, [35] ὥστε παντοίως ὁ Ἀντίπατρος ὑπῆκτο αὐτὰς καὶ δι᾽ αὐτοῦ καὶ διὰ τῆς μητρός: ταὐτὸν γὰρ αἵδε αἱ τέσσαρες γυναῖκες ἔλεγον. καὶ Φερώρᾳ δὲ πρὸς Ἀντίπατρον ἐπ᾽ οὐδαμινοῖς τισιν αἱ γνῶμαι διήλλασσον. [36] ἀντίσπασμα δ᾽ ἦν αὐτοῖς βασιλέως ἡ ἀδελφὴ περισκοποῦσά τε ἐκ πλείονος τὰ πάντα καὶ τὴν εὔνοιαν αὐτῶν ἐπὶ κακοῖς τοῖς Ἡρώδου πρασσομένην εἰδυῖά τε καὶ μηνύειν οὐκ ἀποτετραμμένη. [37] καὶ γνόντες ἐν ἀπεχθείᾳ βασιλεῖ τὴν εὔνοιαν αὐτῶν οὖσαν ἐπινοοῦσιν ὥστε φανερὰν μὲν μὴ εἶναι τὴν πρὸς ἀλλήλους αὐτῶν σύνοδον, μίσους δὲ καὶ λοιδοριῶν ᾗ καιρὸς προσποίησιν, καὶ μάλιστα Ἡρώδου παρατυγχάνοντος ἢ οἳ πρὸς αὐτὸν ἀπαγγέλλειν ἔμελλον, κρυπτῶς δὲ τὰ τῆς εὐνοίας ὀχυρώτερα καθίστασθαι. [38] καὶ ἔπρασσον οὕτως. ἐλάνθανεν δὲ τὴν Σαλώμην οὔτε πρῶτον ἡ διάνοια αὐτῶν ἐπὶ τοιοῖσδε ὡρμημένων οὔτε ἐπειδὴ * χρῆσθαι οὐκ ἀπήλλακτο αὐτή: πάντα δὲ ἀνίχνευέν τε καὶ πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν μειζόνως ἐκδεινοῦσα ἀπεσήμαινεν συνόδους τε κρυπτὰς καὶ πότους βουλευτήριά τε ἀφανῶς κατεσκευασμένα, ὧν μὴ ἐπ᾽ ὀλέθρῳ τῷ ἐκείνου συντιθεμένων κἂν πεφανερῶσθαι μὴ κεκωλῦσθαι. [39] νῦν δὲ τοὺς μὲν ἐκ τοῦ προὔπτου διαφόρους καὶ τὰ πάντα ἐπὶ βλάβῃ τῇ ἀλλήλων λέγοντας, εἰς δὲ τὸ ἀφανὲς τοῖς πολλοῖς τὴν εὔνοιαν ἀνατιθεμένους καὶ ὁπότε ἀλλήλοις συμμονωθεῖεν φίλια πράσσειν μὴ ἀπηλλαγμένους, ὁμολογεῖν πολεμεῖν πρὸς οὓς λανθάνειν χρώμενοι εὐνοίᾳ τῇ ἀλλήλων ἐσπουδάκοιεν. [40] καὶ ἡ μὲν ταῦτ᾽ ἀνίχνευέν τε καὶ ἀκριβῶν τυγχάνουσα τῷ ἀδελφῷ ἀνέφερεν συνιέντι μὲν ἤδη τὰ πολλὰ καὶ δι᾽ ἑαυτοῦ, εἰς δὲ τὸ θαρσεῖν οὐ διακενῆς ὑπονοῶν καθισταμένῳ διαβολαῖς τῆς ἀδελφῆς. [41] καὶ ἦν γὰρ μόριόν τι Ἰουδαϊκὸν ἀνθρώπων ἐπ᾽ ἐξακριβώσει μέγα φρονοῦν τοῦ πατρίου καὶ νόμων οἷς χαίρει τὸ θεῖον προσποιουμένων, οἷς ὑπῆκτο ἡ γυναικωνῖτις, Φαρισαῖοι καλοῦνται, βασιλεῖ δυναμένῳ μάλιστα πράσσειν προμηθεῖς κἀκ τοῦ προὔπτου εἰς τὸ πολεμεῖν τε καὶ βλάπτειν ἐπηρμένοι. [42] παντὸς γοῦν τοῦ Ἰουδαϊκοῦ βεβαιώσαντος δι᾽ ὅρκων ἦ μὴν εὐνοήσειν Καίσαρι καὶ τοῖς βασιλέως πράγμασιν, οἵδε οἱ ἄνδρες οὐκ ὤμοσαν ὄντες ὑπὲρ ἑξακισχίλιοι, καὶ αὐτοὺς βασιλέως ζημιώσαντος χρήμασιν ἡ Φερώρου γυνὴ τὴν ζημίαν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν εἰσφέρει. [43] οἱ δὲ ἀμειβόμενοι τὴν εὔνοιαν αὐτῆς, πρόγνωσιν δὲ ἐπεπίστευντο ἐπιφοιτήσει τοῦ θεοῦ, προύλεγον, ὡς Ἡρώδῃ μὲν καταπαύσεως ἀρχῆς ὑπὸ θεοῦ ἐψηφισμένης αὐτῷ τε καὶ γένει τῷ ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ, τῆς δὲ βασιλείας εἴς τε ἐκείνην περιηξούσης καὶ Φερώραν παῖδάς τε οἳ εἶεν αὐτοῖς. [44] καὶ τάδε, οὐ γὰρ ἐλάνθανεν τὴν Σαλώμην, ἐξάγγελτα βασιλεῖ ἦν, καὶ ὅτι τῶν περὶ τὴν αὐλὴν διαφθείροιέν τινας. καὶ βασιλεὺς τῶν τε Φαρισαίων τοὺς αἰτιωτάτους ἀναιρεῖ καὶ Βαγώαν τὸν εὐνοῦχον Κᾶρόν τέ τινα τῶν τότε προύχοντα ἀρετῇ τοῦ εὐπρεποῦς καὶ παιδικὰ ὄντα αὐτοῦ. κτείνει δὲ καὶ πᾶν ὅ τι τοῦ οἰκείου συνειστήκει οἷς ὁ Φαρισαῖος ἔλεγεν. [45] ἦρτο δὲ ὁ Βαγώας ὑπ᾽ αὐτῶν ὡς πατήρ τε καὶ εὐεργέτης ὀνομασθησόμενος τοῦ ἐπικατασταθησομένου προρρήσει βασιλέως: κατὰ χεῖρα γὰρ ἐκείνῳ τὰ πάντ᾽ εἶναι, παρέξοντος αὐτῷ γάμου τε ἰσχὺν καὶ παιδώσεως τέκνων γνησίων.

<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-2-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="23"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num23" xml:id="english-book17-num23" id="english-book17-num23" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[23]</tei-num> AND now it was that Herod, being desirous of securing himself on the side of the Trachonites, resolved to build a village as large as a city for the Jews, in the middle of that country, which might make his own country difficult to be assaulted, and whence he might be at hand to make sallies upon them, and do them a mischief. Accordingly, when he understood that there was a man that was a Jew come out of Babylon, with five hundred horsemen, all of whom could shoot their arrows as they rode on horde-back, and, with a hundred of his relations, had passed over Euphrates, and now abode at Antioch by Daphne of Syria, where Saturninus, who was then president, had given them a place for habitation, called Valatha, he sent for this man, with the multitude that followed him, and promised to give him land in the toparchy called Batanea, which country is bounded with Trachonitis, as desirous to make that his habitation a guard to himself. He also engaged to let him hold the country free from tribute, and that they should dwell entirely without paying such customs as used to be paid, and gave it him tax-free.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num26" xml:id="english-book17-num26" id="english-book17-num26" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[26]</tei-num> The Babylonian was reduced by these offers to come hither; so he took possession of the land, and built in it fortresses and a village, and named it Bathyra. Whereby this man became a safeguard to the inhabitants against the Trachonites, and preserved those Jews who came out of Babylon, to offer their sacrifices at Jerusalem, from being hurt by the Trachonite robbers; so that a great number came to him from all those parts where the ancient Jewish laws were observed, and the country became full of people, by reason of their universal freedom from taxes. This continued during the life of Herod; but when Philip, who was [tetrarch] after him, took the government, he made them pay some small taxes, and that for a little while only; and Agrippa the Great, and his son of the same name, although they harassed them greatly, yet would they not take their liberty away. From whom, when the Romans have now taken the government into their own hands, they still gave them the privilege of their freedom, but oppress them entirely with the imposition of taxes. Of which matter I shall treat more accurately in the progress of this history.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num29" xml:id="english-book17-num29" id="english-book17-num29" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[29]</tei-num> At length Zamaris the Babylonian, to whom Herod had given that country for a possession, died, having lived virtuously, and left children of a good character behind him; one of whom was Jacim, who was famous for his valor, and taught his Babylonians how to ride their horses; and a troop of them were guards to the forementioned kings. And when Jacim was dead in his old age, he left a son, whose name was Philip, one of great strength in his hands, and in other respects also more eminent for his valor than any of his contemporaries; on which account there was a confidence and firm friendship between him and king Agrippa. He had also an army which he maintained as great as that of a king, which he exercised and led wheresoever lie had occasion to march.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num32" xml:id="english-book17-num32" id="english-book17-num32" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="3" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[32]</tei-num> When the affairs of Herod were in the condition I have described, all the public affairs depended upon Antipater; and his power was such, that he could do good turns to as many as he pleased, and this by his father's concession, in hopes of his good-will and fidelity to him; and this till he ventured to use his power still further, because his wicked designs were concealed from his father, and he made him believe every thing he said. He was also formidable to all, not so much on account of the power and authority he had, as for the shrewdness of his vile attempts beforehand; but he who principally cultivated a friendship with him was Pheroras, who received the like marks of his friendship; while Antipater had cunningly encompassed him about by a company of women, whom he placed as guards about him; for Pheroras was greatly enslaved to his wife, and to her mother, and to her sister; and this notwithstanding the hatred he bare them for the indignities they had offered to his virgin daughters. Yet did he bear them, and nothing was to he done without the women, who had got this man into their circle, and continued still to assist each other in all things, insomuch that Antipater was entirely addicted to them, both by himself and by his mother; for these four women, said all one and the same thing; but the opinions of Pheroras and Antipater were different in some points of no consequence. But the king's sister [Salome] was their antagonist, who for a good while had looked about all their affairs, and was apprized that this their friendship was made in order to do Herod some mischief, and was disposed to inform the king of it. And since these people knew that their friendship was very disagreeable to Herod, as tending to do him a mischief, they contrived that their meetings should not be discovered; so they pretended to hate one another, and to abuse one another when time served, and especially when Herod was present, or when any one was there that would tell him: but still their intimacy was firmer than ever, when they were private. And this was the course they took. But they could not conceal from Salome neither their first contrivance, when they set about these their intentions, nor when they had made some progress in them; but she searched out every thing; and, aggravating the relations to her brother, declared to him, as well their secret assemblies and compotations, as their counsels taken in a clandestine manner, which if they were not in order to destroy him, they might well enough have been open and public. But to appearance they are at variance, and speak about one another as if they intended one another a mischief, but agree so well together when they are out of the sight of the multitude; for when they are alone by themselves, they act in concert, and profess that they will never leave off their friendship, but will fight against those from whom they conceal their designs. And thus did she search out these things, and get a perfect knowledge of them, and then told her brother of them, who understood also of himself a great deal of what she said, but still durst not depend upon it, because of the suspicions he had of his sister's calumnies. For there was a certain sect of men that were Jews, who valued themselves highly upon the exact skill they had in the law of their fathers, and made men believe they were highly favored by God, by whom this set of women were inveigled. These are those that are called the sect of the Pharisees, who were in a capacity of greatly opposing kings. A cunning sect they were, and soon elevated to a pitch of open fighting and doing mischief. Accordingly, when all the people of the Jews gave assurance of their good-will to Caesar, and to the king's government, these very men did not swear, being above six thousand; and when the king imposed a fine upon them, Pheroras's wife paid their fine for them. In order to requite which kindness of hers, since they were believed to have the foreknowledge of things to come by Divine inspiration, they foretold how God had decreed that Herod's government should cease, and his posterity should be deprived of it; but that the kingdom should come to her and Pheroras, and to their children. These predictions were not concealed from Salome, but were told the king; as also how they had perverted some persons about the palace itself; so the king slew such of the Pharisees as were principally accused, and Bagoas the eunuch, and one Carus, who exceeded all men of that time in comeliness, and one that was his catamite. He slew also all those of his own family who had consented to what the Pharisees foretold; and for Bagoas, he had been puffed up by them, as though he should be named the father and the benefactor of him who, by the prediction, was foretold to be their appointed king; for that this king would have all things in his power, and would enable Bagoas to marry, and to have children of his own body begotten.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

A cunning sect they were, and soon elevated to a pitch of open fighting and doing mischief. Accordingly, when all the people of the Jews gave assurance of their good-will to Caesar, and to the king's government, these very men did not swear, being above six thousand; and when the king imposed a fine upon them, Pheroras's wife paid their fine for them. In order to requite which kindness of hers, since they were believed to have the foreknowledge of things to come by Divine inspiration, they foretold how God had decreed that Herod's government should cease, and his posterity should be deprived of it; but that the kingdom should come to her and Pheroras, and to their children. These predictions were not concealed from Salome, but were told the king; as also how they had perverted some persons about the palace itself; so the king slew such of the Pharisees as were principally accused, and Bagoas the eunuch, and one Carus, who exceeded all men of that time in comeliness, and one that was his catamite. He slew also all those of his own family who had consented to what the Pharisees foretold; and for Bagoas, he had been puffed up by them, as though he should be named the father and the benefactor of him who, by the prediction, was foretold to be their appointed king; for that this king would have all things in his power, and would enable Bagoas to marry, and to have children of his own body begotten.

					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num52" id="latin-book17-num52" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="5" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>V. Suspectum autem patrem habens et timens antipater ne circa amplius eius odium processisset, scribit amicis romae postulans ut scriberent herodi. Quatenus celeriter antipatrum mitteret simulque cum eo munera digna mandaret, et testamentum etiam in quo post se regem decluraret antipatrum quoniam defunctus erat herodes qui ei ex filia pontificis fuerat procreatus. Quo facto pergit unaquaque cum antipatro et filleus arabs nihil ex his quae praeceperat caesar peragens, unde quoque antipater ante caesarem eius accusator extiterat pro quibus primus nicolaus paciebatur iniuriam. Accusabatur etiam et ab areta filleus eo quod plures occiderit in petra castello bene meritorum hominum preter suam conscientiam, maxime autem fondum uirum onmi uirtute decoratum iustitiaque pollentem, sed etiam fabatonem caesaris seruum. Silleus autem causas habuit ex hisdem criminibus praepagatas. Erat quidam corinthus herodis regis unus ex custodum corporis, cui maxime cura plura committebat. Huic persuadet filleus pecunias magnas pollicens ut herodem occideret hoc etiam ille praemiserat. Quod agnoscens sabbatus filleo indicante statim regi denuntiat. Ille uero corinthum tormentis ex ami nans fecit omnia depalari. Detinuit autem et secundos arabas, confessioni credens corinthii, et filarchum quod fillei fuisset amicus. Qui etiam ipsi nam eos rex tormentis affecerat confessi fuerant quod eos exor taretur nuncians corinthum non agere molliter et sicubi opus esset rei ferro quo operarentur, ad perpetrandum facinus inter eos conplicitum. Ad haec etiam saturninus omnibus ei ab herode denunciatis romam eos destinat.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num58" id="latin-book17-num58" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Ferora uero fortiter in amore<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00415.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="206r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>coniugis permanente discedere ad propria herodes precepit. Ille uero gratanter accipiens ad suam tetrarchiam non moratus abscessit. Plurimum se iure iurando constringens non primum reuerti ante quam mortem herodis aduerteret. Proinde etiam ab herode morte conscricto paetitus, utue niret pro aliquibus sibi mandatis si mors contingeret in iungendis nullomodo persuasus est aduenire, ne iuris iurandi uiolatore existeret. Non tamen herodes in his rebus illius imitatur exemplum, meliorem circa feroram uolumtatem suae mentis ostendens. Nam paulo post ipse coepit aegritudine laborare, ad quem herodes non euocatus aduenit, sed etiam mortuum eum recipit atque ad hierosolimam detulit, et iusta ei honorabiliter magnificeque celebrauit ingentemque luctum super eum supra quam quisquam, ratus erat exposuit. Hoc antipatro licet romam nauigasset malorum tamen extitit aduer satumque principium. Ex hinc iam coepit fratricidii factio denudari. Narrabo itaque omnem super hoc hominis rationem exemplum generi homuno in futura tempora permansurum ad hutilitatem qui uoluerint uirtutis esse cultores.</tei-p>

<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-3-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="46"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num46" xml:id="greek-book17-num46" id="greek-book17-num46" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="4" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[46]</tei-num> Ἡρώδης δὲ κολάσας τῶν Φαρισαίων τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῖσδε ἐληλεγμένους συνέδριόν τε ποιεῖται τῶν φίλων καὶ κατηγορίαν τῆς Φερώρου γυναικός, τήν τε ὕβριν τῶν παρθένων τῇ τόλμῃ τῆς γυναικὸς ἀνατιθεὶς καὶ ἔγκλημα ταύτην ἀτιμίαν αὐτῷ ποιούμενος, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[47]</tei-num> ὥστε ἀγωνοθετῶν στάσιν αὐτῷ πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν πόλεμον ἐκ φύσεως αὐτοῖς καὶ λόγῳ καὶ δι᾽ ἔργων ὁπόσα δύναιτο, τήν τε διάλυσιν τῆς ζημίας τῆς ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἐπιβληθείσης τέλεσι διαφευχθείσης τοῖς ἐκείνης, τῶν τε νῦν πεπραγμένων οὐδὲν ὅ τι οὐ μετ᾽ αὐτῆς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[48]</tei-num> ‘ἀνθ᾽ ὧν, ὦ Φερώρα, καλῶς εἶχεν οὐ δεήσει οὐδὲ γνωμῶν εἰσηγήσεως τῶν ἐμῶν αὐτοκέλευστον ἀποπέμπεσθαι γυναῖκα ταύτην ὡς πολέμου τοῦ πρός μέ σοι αἰτίαν ἐσομένην: καὶ νῦν, εἴπερ ἀντιποιῇ συγγενείας τῆς ἐμῆς, ἀπείπασθαι τήνδε τὴν γαμετήν: μενεῖς γὰρ οὕτως ἀδελφός τε καὶ στέργειν οὐκ ἀπηλλαγμένος.’ <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[49]</tei-num> Φερώρας δὲ καίπερ λόγων ἀρετῇ περιωθούμενος οὔτε συγγενείας τῆς πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἔλεγε κινήσειν δίκαιον οὐδὲν οὔτε τῶν πρὸς τὴν γαμετὴν εὐνοιῶν, αἱρεῖσθαί τε πρότερον θανεῖν ἢ ζῶν τολμᾶν ἀπεστερῆσθαι γυναικὸς αὐτῷ κεχαρισμένης. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[50]</tei-num> Ἡρώδης δὲ Φερώρᾳ μὲν ὑπερεβάλλετο τὴν ἐπὶ τούτοις ὀργὴν καίπερ ἀνήδονον τιμωρίαν εἰσπεπραγμένος, Ἀντιπάτρῳ δὲ ἀπεῖπε καὶ μητρὶ τῇ ἐκείνου Φερώρᾳ τε μὴ ὁμιλεῖν καὶ τῶν γυναικῶν φυλάσσεσθαι τὸ εἰς ταὐτὸν συνεσόμενον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[51]</tei-num> οἱ δ᾽ ὡμολόγουν μέν, συνῄεσαν δὲ ᾗ καιρὸς καὶ συνεκώμαζον Φερώρας καὶ Ἀντίπατρος. ἐφοίτα δὲ λόγος ὁμιλεῖν καὶ Ἀντιπάτρῳ τὴν Φερώρου γυναῖκα συμπρασσούσης αὐτοῖς τὰ εἰς τὴν σύνοδον τῆς Ἀντιπάτρου μητρός.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num52" xml:id="greek-book17-num52" id="greek-book17-num52" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="5" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[52]</tei-num> Ὑφορώμενος δὲ τὸν πατέρα καὶ δεδιώς, μὴ εἰς πλεῖον προχωροίη τὰ τοῦ μίσους ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ, γράφει πρὸς τοὺς ἐν Ῥώμῃ φίλους κελεύων ἐπιστέλλειν Ἡρώδῃ πέμπειν ᾗ τάχος Ἀντίπατρον ὡς Καίσαρα. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[53]</tei-num> οὗ γενομένου ἔπεμπεν Ἡρώδης Ἀντίπατρον δῶρα συμπέμψας ἀξιολογώτατα καὶ διαθήκην, ἐν ᾗ μετ᾽ αὐτὸν Ἀντίπατρον ἀπεδείκνυε βασιλέα, ἢ φθάντος τελευτῆσαι Ἡρώδην τὸν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως θυγατρὸς υἱὸν αὐτῷ γεγενημένον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[54]</tei-num> συνεξορμᾷ δ᾽ Ἀντιπάτρῳ καὶ Σύλλαιος ὁ Ἄραψ μηδὲν ὧν προσέταξε Καῖσαρ διαπεπραγμένος, καὶ Ἀντίπατρος αὐτοῦ κατηγορεῖ ἐπὶ Καίσαρος περὶ ὧν πρότερον Νικόλαος. κατηγορεῖτο δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ Ἀρέτα Σύλλαιος, ὡς πολλοὺς ἀπεκτονὼς τῶν ἐν Πέτρᾳ ἀξιολόγων παρὰ γνώμην τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ μάλιστα Σόαιμον ἄνδρα τῇ ἐς πάντα ἀρετῇ τιμᾶσθαι δικαιότατον, ἀνῃρηκέναι δὲ καὶ Φάβατον Καίσαρος δοῦλον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[55]</tei-num> καὶ Σύλλαιος αἰτίαν εἶχεν ἐκ τοιῶνδε ἐγκλημάτων: Κόρινθος ἦν Ἡρώδου σωματοφύλαξ τοῦ βασιλέως μάλιστα πιστευόμενος ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ. τοῦτον πείθει Σύλλαιος ἐπὶ χρήμασι μεγάλοις Ἡρώδην ἀποκτεῖναι, καὶ ὑπέσχετο. μαθὼν οὖν Φάβατος Συλλαίου πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰρηκότος διηγεῖται πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[56]</tei-num> ὁ δὲ τόν τε Κόρινθον βασανίζει συλλαβὼν καὶ πάντα ἀνάπυστα ἦν αὐτῷ. συλλαμβάνει δὲ καὶ δευτέρους Ἄραβας καταγορεύσει τῇ Κορίνθου πειθόμενος τὸν μὲν φύλαρχον ὄντα τὸν δὲ Συλλαίου φίλον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[57]</tei-num> οἳ καὐτοί, βασανίζει γὰρ αὐτοὺς ὁ βασιλεύς, ὡμολόγουν ὅτι παρεῖεν ἐξοτρύνοντες μὴ μαλακίζεσθαι Κόρινθον καὶ εἴ που δεήσειεν καὶ συγχειρουργήσοντες αὐτῷ τὸν φόνον. καὶ Σατορνῖνος δηλώσεως αὐτῷ πάντων ὑπὸ Ἡρώδου γενομένης εἰς Ῥώμην ἐξέπεμψεν αὐτούς.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num58" xml:id="greek-book17-num58" id="greek-book17-num58" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[58]</tei-num> Φερώραν δὲ ἰσχυρῶς ἐμμένοντα εὐνοίᾳ τῆς γυναικὸς ἀναχωρεῖν εἰς τὴν αὑτοῦ Ἡρώδης κελεύει. ὁ δὲ ἀσμένως ἐπὶ τὴν τετραρχίαν ἀπῆρεν, πολλὰ ὀμόσας οὐ πρότερον ἥξειν ἢ πύθοιτο Ἡρώδην τετελευτηκότα, ὥστε καὶ νοσήσαντος τοῦ βασιλέως ἀξιωθεὶς ἥκειν ἐπί τινων πίστεσιν ἐντολῶν, εἰ μέλλοι τελευτᾶν, οὐχ ὑπήκουσεν ἐπὶ τιμῇ τοῦ ὅρκου. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[59]</tei-num> οὐ μὴν Ἡρώδης γε μιμεῖται τὸ ἐπὶ τοιοῖσδε ἐκείνου γνώμην προαποφηνάμενον ἣν ἔχει, ἀλλ᾽ ἧκεν ὡς τὸν Φερώραν, ἐπειδὴ ὕστερον ἄρχεται νοσεῖν, καὶ μετακλήσεως αὐτῷ μὴ γενομένης, θανόντα δὲ περιστείλας ἐπὶ Ἱεροσολύμων ἀγόμενος ταφῆς ἠξίου καὶ πένθος μέγα ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ προέθετο. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[60]</tei-num> τοῦτο Ἀντιπάτρῳ καίτοι γε ἐπὶ Ῥώμης πεπλευκότι κακῶν ἐγένετο ἀρχὴ τῆς ἀδελφοκτονίας αὐτὸν τινυμένου θεοῦ. διηγήσομαι δὲ τὸν πάντα περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον παράδειγμα τῷ ἀνθρωπείῳ γενησόμενον τοῦ ἀρετῇ πολιτεύσοντος ἐπὶ πᾶσιν.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
greek.text: [46] Ἡρώδης δὲ κολάσας τῶν Φαρισαίων τοὺς ἐπὶ τοῖσδε ἐληλεγμένους συνέδριόν τε ποιεῖται τῶν φίλων καὶ κατηγορίαν τῆς Φερώρου γυναικός, τήν τε ὕβριν τῶν παρθένων τῇ τόλμῃ τῆς γυναικὸς ἀνατιθεὶς καὶ ἔγκλημα ταύτην ἀτιμίαν αὐτῷ ποιούμενος, [47] ὥστε ἀγωνοθετῶν στάσιν αὐτῷ πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν πόλεμον ἐκ φύσεως αὐτοῖς καὶ λόγῳ καὶ δι᾽ ἔργων ὁπόσα δύναιτο, τήν τε διάλυσιν τῆς ζημίας τῆς ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἐπιβληθείσης τέλεσι διαφευχθείσης τοῖς ἐκείνης, τῶν τε νῦν πεπραγμένων οὐδὲν ὅ τι οὐ μετ᾽ αὐτῆς. [48] ‘ἀνθ᾽ ὧν, ὦ Φερώρα, καλῶς εἶχεν οὐ δεήσει οὐδὲ γνωμῶν εἰσηγήσεως τῶν ἐμῶν αὐτοκέλευστον ἀποπέμπεσθαι γυναῖκα ταύτην ὡς πολέμου τοῦ πρός μέ σοι αἰτίαν ἐσομένην: καὶ νῦν, εἴπερ ἀντιποιῇ συγγενείας τῆς ἐμῆς, ἀπείπασθαι τήνδε τὴν γαμετήν: μενεῖς γὰρ οὕτως ἀδελφός τε καὶ στέργειν οὐκ ἀπηλλαγμένος.’ [49] Φερώρας δὲ καίπερ λόγων ἀρετῇ περιωθούμενος οὔτε συγγενείας τῆς πρὸς τὸν ἀδελφὸν ἔλεγε κινήσειν δίκαιον οὐδὲν οὔτε τῶν πρὸς τὴν γαμετὴν εὐνοιῶν, αἱρεῖσθαί τε πρότερον θανεῖν ἢ ζῶν τολμᾶν ἀπεστερῆσθαι γυναικὸς αὐτῷ κεχαρισμένης. [50] Ἡρώδης δὲ Φερώρᾳ μὲν ὑπερεβάλλετο τὴν ἐπὶ τούτοις ὀργὴν καίπερ ἀνήδονον τιμωρίαν εἰσπεπραγμένος, Ἀντιπάτρῳ δὲ ἀπεῖπε καὶ μητρὶ τῇ ἐκείνου Φερώρᾳ τε μὴ ὁμιλεῖν καὶ τῶν γυναικῶν φυλάσσεσθαι τὸ εἰς ταὐτὸν συνεσόμενον. [51] οἱ δ᾽ ὡμολόγουν μέν, συνῄεσαν δὲ ᾗ καιρὸς καὶ συνεκώμαζον Φερώρας καὶ Ἀντίπατρος. ἐφοίτα δὲ λόγος ὁμιλεῖν καὶ Ἀντιπάτρῳ τὴν Φερώρου γυναῖκα συμπρασσούσης αὐτοῖς τὰ εἰς τὴν σύνοδον τῆς Ἀντιπάτρου μητρός. [52] Ὑφορώμενος δὲ τὸν πατέρα καὶ δεδιώς, μὴ εἰς πλεῖον προχωροίη τὰ τοῦ μίσους ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ, γράφει πρὸς τοὺς ἐν Ῥώμῃ φίλους κελεύων ἐπιστέλλειν Ἡρώδῃ πέμπειν ᾗ τάχος Ἀντίπατρον ὡς Καίσαρα. [53] οὗ γενομένου ἔπεμπεν Ἡρώδης Ἀντίπατρον δῶρα συμπέμψας ἀξιολογώτατα καὶ διαθήκην, ἐν ᾗ μετ᾽ αὐτὸν Ἀντίπατρον ἀπεδείκνυε βασιλέα, ἢ φθάντος τελευτῆσαι Ἡρώδην τὸν ἐκ τῆς τοῦ ἀρχιερέως θυγατρὸς υἱὸν αὐτῷ γεγενημένον. [54] συνεξορμᾷ δ᾽ Ἀντιπάτρῳ καὶ Σύλλαιος ὁ Ἄραψ μηδὲν ὧν προσέταξε Καῖσαρ διαπεπραγμένος, καὶ Ἀντίπατρος αὐτοῦ κατηγορεῖ ἐπὶ Καίσαρος περὶ ὧν πρότερον Νικόλαος. κατηγορεῖτο δὲ καὶ ὑπὸ Ἀρέτα Σύλλαιος, ὡς πολλοὺς ἀπεκτονὼς τῶν ἐν Πέτρᾳ ἀξιολόγων παρὰ γνώμην τὴν αὐτοῦ καὶ μάλιστα Σόαιμον ἄνδρα τῇ ἐς πάντα ἀρετῇ τιμᾶσθαι δικαιότατον, ἀνῃρηκέναι δὲ καὶ Φάβατον Καίσαρος δοῦλον. [55] καὶ Σύλλαιος αἰτίαν εἶχεν ἐκ τοιῶνδε ἐγκλημάτων: Κόρινθος ἦν Ἡρώδου σωματοφύλαξ τοῦ βασιλέως μάλιστα πιστευόμενος ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ. τοῦτον πείθει Σύλλαιος ἐπὶ χρήμασι μεγάλοις Ἡρώδην ἀποκτεῖναι, καὶ ὑπέσχετο. μαθὼν οὖν Φάβατος Συλλαίου πρὸς αὐτὸν εἰρηκότος διηγεῖται πρὸς τὸν βασιλέα. [56] ὁ δὲ τόν τε Κόρινθον βασανίζει συλλαβὼν καὶ πάντα ἀνάπυστα ἦν αὐτῷ. συλλαμβάνει δὲ καὶ δευτέρους Ἄραβας καταγορεύσει τῇ Κορίνθου πειθόμενος τὸν μὲν φύλαρχον ὄντα τὸν δὲ Συλλαίου φίλον. [57] οἳ καὐτοί, βασανίζει γὰρ αὐτοὺς ὁ βασιλεύς, ὡμολόγουν ὅτι παρεῖεν ἐξοτρύνοντες μὴ μαλακίζεσθαι Κόρινθον καὶ εἴ που δεήσειεν καὶ συγχειρουργήσοντες αὐτῷ τὸν φόνον. καὶ Σατορνῖνος δηλώσεως αὐτῷ πάντων ὑπὸ Ἡρώδου γενομένης εἰς Ῥώμην ἐξέπεμψεν αὐτούς. [58] Φερώραν δὲ ἰσχυρῶς ἐμμένοντα εὐνοίᾳ τῆς γυναικὸς ἀναχωρεῖν εἰς τὴν αὑτοῦ Ἡρώδης κελεύει. ὁ δὲ ἀσμένως ἐπὶ τὴν τετραρχίαν ἀπῆρεν, πολλὰ ὀμόσας οὐ πρότερον ἥξειν ἢ πύθοιτο Ἡρώδην τετελευτηκότα, ὥστε καὶ νοσήσαντος τοῦ βασιλέως ἀξιωθεὶς ἥκειν ἐπί τινων πίστεσιν ἐντολῶν, εἰ μέλλοι τελευτᾶν, οὐχ ὑπήκουσεν ἐπὶ τιμῇ τοῦ ὅρκου. [59] οὐ μὴν Ἡρώδης γε μιμεῖται τὸ ἐπὶ τοιοῖσδε ἐκείνου γνώμην προαποφηνάμενον ἣν ἔχει, ἀλλ᾽ ἧκεν ὡς τὸν Φερώραν, ἐπειδὴ ὕστερον ἄρχεται νοσεῖν, καὶ μετακλήσεως αὐτῷ μὴ γενομένης, θανόντα δὲ περιστείλας ἐπὶ Ἱεροσολύμων ἀγόμενος ταφῆς ἠξίου καὶ πένθος μέγα ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ προέθετο. [60] τοῦτο Ἀντιπάτρῳ καίτοι γε ἐπὶ Ῥώμης πεπλευκότι κακῶν ἐγένετο ἀρχὴ τῆς ἀδελφοκτονίας αὐτὸν τινυμένου θεοῦ. διηγήσομαι δὲ τὸν πάντα περὶ αὐτοῦ λόγον παράδειγμα τῷ ἀνθρωπείῳ γενησόμενον τοῦ ἀρετῇ πολιτεύσοντος ἐπὶ πᾶσιν.

<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-3-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="46"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num46" xml:id="english-book17-num46" id="english-book17-num46" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="4" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[46]</tei-num> WHEN Herod had punished those Pharisees who had been convicted of the foregoing crimes, he gathered an assembly together of his friends, and accused Pheroras's wife; and ascribing the abuses of the virgins to the impudence of that woman, brought an accusation against her for the dishonor she had brought upon them: that she had studiously introduced a quarrel between him and his brother, and, by her ill temper, had brought them into a state of war, both by her words and actions; that the fines which he had laid had not been paid, and the offenders had escaped punishment by her means; and that nothing which had of late been done had been done without her; "for which reason Pheroras would do well, if he would of his own accord, and by his own command, and not at my entreaty, or as following my opinion, put this his wife away, as one that will still be the occasion of war between thee and me. And now, Pheroras, if thou valuest thy relation to me, put this wife of thine away; for by this means thou wilt continue to be a brother to me, and wilt abide in thy love to me." Then said Pheroras, (although he was pressed hard by the former words,) that as he would not do so unjust a thing as to renounce his brotherly relation to him, so would he not leave off his affection for his wife; that he would rather choose to die than to live, and be deprived of a wife that was so dear unto him. Hereupon Herod put off his anger against Pheroras on these accounts, although he himself thereby underwent a very uneasy punishment. However, he forbade Antipater and his mother to have any conversation with Pheroras, and bid them to take care to avoid the assemblies of the women; which they promised to do, but still got together when occasion served, and both Ptieroras and Antipater had their own merry meetings. The report went also, that Antipater had criminal conversation with Pheroras's wife, and that they were brought together by Antipater's mother.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num52" xml:id="english-book17-num52" id="english-book17-num52" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="5" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[52]</tei-num> But Antipater had now a suspicion of his father, and was afraid that the effects of his hatred to him might increase; so he wrote to his friends at Rome, and bid them to send to Herod, that he would immediately send Antipater to Caesar; which when it was done, Herod sent Antipater thither, and sent most noble presents along with him; as also his testament, wherein Antipater was appointed to be his successor; and that if Antipater should die first, his son [Herod Philip] by the high priest's daughter should succeed. And, together with Antipater, there went to Rome Sylleus the Arabian, although he had done nothing of all that Caesar had enjoined him. Antipater also accused him of the same crimes of which he had been formerly accused by Herod. Sylleus was also accused by Aretas, that without his consent he had slain many of the chief of the Arabians at Petra; and particularly Soemus, a man that deserved to be honored by all men; and that he had slain Fabatus, a servant of Caesar. These were the things of which Sylleus was accused, and that on the occasion following: There was one Corinthus, belonging to Herod, of the guards of the king's body, and one who was greatly trusted by him. Sylleus had persuaded this man with the offer of a great sum of money to kill Herod; and he had promised to do it. When Fabatus had been made acquainted with this, for Sylleus had himself told him of it, he informed the king of it; who caught Corinthus, and put him to the torture, and thereby got out of him the whole conspiracy. He also caught two other Arabians, who were discovered by Corinthus; the one the head of a tribe, and the other a friend to Sylleus, who both were by the king brought to the torture, and confessed that they were come to encourage Corinthus not to fail of doing what he had undertaken to do; and to assist him with their own hands in the murder, if need should require their assistance. So Saturninns, upon Herod's discovering the whole to him, sent them to Rome.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num58" xml:id="english-book17-num58" id="english-book17-num58" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[58]</tei-num> At this time Herod commanded Pheroras, that since he was so obstinate in his affection for his wife, he should retire into his own tetrarchy; which he did very willingly, and sware many oaths that he would not come again till he heard that Herod was dead. And indeed when, upon a sickness of the king, he was desired to come to him before he died, that he might intrust him with some of his injunctions, he had such a regard to his oath, that he would not come to him; yet did not Herod so retain his hatred to Pheroras, but remitted of his purpose [not to see him], which he before had, and that for such great causes as have been already mentioned: but as soon as he began to be ill, he came to him, and this without being sent for; and when he was dead, he took care of his funeral, and had his body brought to Jerusalem, and buried there, and appointed a solemn mourning for him. This [death of Pheroras] became the origin of Antipater's misfortunes, although he were already sailed for Rome, God now being about to punish him for the murder of his brethren, I will explain the history of this matter very distinctly, that it may be for a warning to mankind, that they take care of conducting their whole lives by the rules of virtue.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>

<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-4-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="61"><tei-div2 n="6" type="chapter" data-origname="div2" data-processed=""><tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num61" id="latin-book17-num61" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="6" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>VI. Eerora igitur mortuo humatoque celebritate magnifica duo ex liberis eius qui ab eo honore habebantur ad herodem ueniunt postulantes, ne multam mortem fratris relinqueret. Quin potius inquisitionem faceret acerbae mortis et calamitose repentineque translationis. Illo autem attonito facto liberorum sermonibus, fidelia namque narrabant ad coniugem die proxima ante quam egritudinem incurreret eum cenasse retulerunt, uenenum autem in cibo sumpsisse ex eoque perisse. Quod uenenum ad latum esset ab arabica muliere amoris faciendi gratia. Amare se namque fingebat re autem uera ad interitum erat ferorae petitum. Sunt quippe ad uenena confici<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>enda artificios sime arabicae mulieres persuasum illi dicebat ut uenenum uenundaret. Ad loca quippe illa uenisse referebat matrem ferorae coniugis et sororem, unde illud uenenum ad portantes caenam illi praeparauere in qua illo ueneno sumpto periit. His uerbis protinus excitatus ancillas earum mulierum tormentis examinat. <tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="7" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>VII. Inter quas aliquas etiam liberarum et ad huc in occultore manente negotio quia nulla illarum aliquid depalaret, nouissima quedam inflictis ei magnis extormento doloribus nihil quidem aliud dixunt, nisi deum inuocans ut talibus suppliciis antipatri matrem traderet in praecata est quae omnium illorum malorum causa consisteret. Haec ad instandum herodem magis magisque coegerunt ut cuncta mulierum illarum secreta tormentis erueret. Tunc omnia palam facta sunt et conuiuia et conuentus secreto facti se piissime sed etiam sermocinationes quae ad ipsos et ad filium solum fuerant facte, uel illa quae ab eo ad mulieres deferebantur, erant autem munera centum talentorum ut secreto ferorae persuaderent quicquid antipater imperaret, prodebatur etiam odium qui in patrem concitarentur et lamentationes quas ad matrem propriam frequentabat quod tam prolixime pater aduiueret, sibilam inminere senium ut etiam ei si regnum ueniret non liceret iucunde iam uiuere per aetatis grauitudinem atque molestiam ad haec etiam multos sibi frates in regno illo quo adulescere et fratrum plures filios exquibus omnibus minus spem suam tutam haberet. His etiam addebat dixisse quod per idem iam tempus fratri potius in regno suo lincentiam habere concederet, crudelitatem quoque plurimam regis accusare et filiorum cedes sequoque timere ne usque ad ipsum hoc malum pertingeret, artem quoque romam pergendi consiliumque narrabat.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num68" id="latin-book17-num68" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Feroram quoque adsuam tetrarchiam ex eius discessisse sententia. Quibus herodes auditis cognoscebat sororis uae sermones quos ad sese pede tulerat. Incitabatur autem rex super antipatri nequitia<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00416.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="206v" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>iussitque matrem eius ornamenta sua cuncta contradere quae multorum constarent praetio talentorum. Quae postquam abstulit reiecit eam et in amicitiam mulierum ferore pro damnatione dedicauit. Ampli autem aduersus filium iracundiam regis incendebat, uir samarites antipater nomine qui filio regis antipatro curator extabat. Nam cum alia quidem eius in tormentis aperuisset, illud quoque prodiderat, quoniam uenenum mortiferum confecerat, dederatque ferorae, iubens ut post eius abscensum cum iam spatium aliquanti temporis cucurisset ubi ratio prouocaret patri protinus propinaret, et dicebat attulisse illud uenenum ex aegypto anti filium unum examicis antipatri, transmissum autem ferorae per theudionem fratrem matris antipatri et hoc modo ad uxorem ferore deuenisse dantem marito ad custodiendum Quod illa quoque fabebatur rege scrutante negotium et procurrens tamquam uenenum ad latura, misit se detecto deorsum non tamen interiit. Quo cadens inpedes terra suscepta sit. Ac de inde post quam recreauit animam promittit ei herodes salutem eiusque domesticis dum modo nequaquam ab ea occultaretur ueritas, neque se illi malum pro ingratitudine redditurum iurabat, si cuncta cum ueritate proderet uel modum quo gesta constarent. Ad haec illa dicebat iusta atque ab aliis se nuntiata firmabat ad latum esse uenenum ex aegypto ad antifalo medico, quippe esse fratre enim agebat a quo prouisum fuerat, per theudionem autem uiro suo transmissum, se uero illud custotire a ferora susceptum, aduersum ipsum sane ab antipatro praeparatum. Cum igitur feroras egritudine teneretur et eum aduentu tuo consolationeque curares uidens circa se tuam beniuolentiam concidit mente deiecta et me conuocans o mulier inquit induxunt me antipater aduersus patrem suum fratrem meum consilia in qua constituens. Nam uenenum<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>in eius pernitiem nundinatus est. Nunc itaque quoniam frater ergame nec ante iniquum aliquid gessit et nunc propositum bone uoluntatis ostendit. Me autem non multum de hac luce sentiore cessurum a gene cum conscientia fratricidii ad nostros pro genitores abierim. Illud uenenum ad portans epistolamque antipatri me uidente conbure. Ego autem plurimum enim igni contradens, aliquantulum reseruaui, ut ferora defuncto sime o rex male fortassis ad tenderes ut illo usa saeculi huius necessitates effugerent. Haec dicens et uenenum et pixida in medium protulit. Sed etiam frater antifili et mater eius eadem fatebantur tormentorum conpulsi uehementi. Apoxidam quoque illam nihil hominus agnoscebant. Accusabatur filia pontificis uxor regis tamquam omnium conscia fuisset sed ea celare maluerit Obque illa quidem herodes emisit. Filium autem eius ex testamento deleuit in ceteris permanente, sed etiam socerum pontificatu priuauit symonem boethi, substituit uero mathiam theofili hierosolimitem genere.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num79" id="latin-book17-num79" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Dum ea geruntur Bathillus quoque ex liberos antipatri uenit ex roma et tormentis examinatus inuenitur uenenum aliud attulisse quod matri daret antipatri et illa ferore tradendum ut si primum uenenum minus regem fortitan permisset, et hoc maturius uterentur. Aportabat etiam litteras ab amicis herodis romae constitutis consilio antipatri et dictatione compositas accusationem habentes archelai atque philippi quod quasi de patre quererentur pro nece aristoboli et alexandri. Semet ipsos quoque hero miserari nuntiabant, et euocabantur quidem a patre ueluti non ab alias res nisi ut etiam ipsos extingueret. Haec quippe magnorum munerum amici gerebant opitulantes antipatro Scripsit etiam antipater patri de fratribus culparum genera magna confingens omni modo eos ad iudicans etatem eorum ausam ascribens qua impelli possent nequitiam suam patrare praepositi. Ipse uero certamini quod cum filleo<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00417.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="207r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>gerebat magno studio fuit intentus, et accusationi primorum uiuorum romae constitutorum se totum dederet. Munilia quoque praetiosa ducentis talentis empta parauerat. Miretur fortasse aliquis quoniam tantis aduersus eum in iudaea motis turbinibus ferme septem mensuum tempore decurrente nihil illi fuerit nunciatum. Causa uero huius rei erat obseruatio uiarum atque custodia et odium hominum quo circa eum cum execratione tenebantur. Nullus et enim erat qui pronus esset proprio periculo illius tutamen salutemque conquirere</tei-p>

latin.text: VI. Eerora igitur mortuo humatoque celebritate magnifica duo ex liberis eius qui ab eo honore habebantur ad herodem ueniunt postulantes, ne multam mortem fratris relinqueret. Quin potius inquisitionem faceret acerbae mortis et calamitose repentineque translationis. Illo autem attonito facto liberorum sermonibus, fidelia namque narrabant ad coniugem die proxima ante quam egritudinem incurreret eum cenasse retulerunt, uenenum autem in cibo sumpsisse ex eoque perisse. Quod uenenum ad latum esset ab arabica muliere amoris faciendi gratia. Amare se namque fingebat re autem uera ad interitum erat ferorae petitum. Sunt quippe ad uenena conficienda artificios sime arabicae mulieres persuasum illi dicebat ut uenenum uenundaret. Ad loca quippe illa uenisse referebat matrem ferorae coniugis et sororem, unde illud uenenum ad portantes caenam illi praeparauere in qua illo ueneno sumpto periit. His uerbis protinus excitatus ancillas earum mulierum tormentis examinat. VII. Inter quas aliquas etiam liberarum et ad huc in occultore manente negotio quia nulla illarum aliquid depalaret, nouissima quedam inflictis ei magnis extormento doloribus nihil quidem aliud dixunt, nisi deum inuocans ut talibus suppliciis antipatri matrem traderet in praecata est quae omnium illorum malorum causa consisteret. Haec ad instandum herodem magis magisque coegerunt ut cuncta mulierum illarum secreta tormentis erueret. Tunc omnia palam facta sunt et conuiuia et conuentus secreto facti se piissime sed etiam sermocinationes quae ad ipsos et ad filium solum fuerant facte, uel illa quae ab eo ad mulieres deferebantur, erant autem munera centum talentorum ut secreto ferorae persuaderent quicquid antipater imperaret, prodebatur etiam odium qui in patrem concitarentur et lamentationes quas ad matrem propriam frequentabat quod tam prolixime pater aduiueret, sibilam inminere senium ut etiam ei si regnum ueniret non liceret iucunde iam uiuere per aetatis grauitudinem atque molestiam ad haec etiam multos sibi frates in regno illo quo adulescere et fratrum plures filios exquibus omnibus minus spem suam tutam haberet. His etiam addebat dixisse quod per idem iam tempus fratri potius in regno suo lincentiam habere concederet, crudelitatem quoque plurimam regis accusare et filiorum cedes sequoque timere ne usque ad ipsum hoc malum pertingeret, artem quoque romam pergendi consiliumque narrabat. Feroram quoque adsuam tetrarchiam ex eius discessisse sententia. Quibus herodes auditis cognoscebat sororis uae sermones quos ad sese pede tulerat. Incitabatur autem rex super antipatri nequitiaiussitque matrem eius ornamenta sua cuncta contradere quae multorum constarent praetio talentorum. Quae postquam abstulit reiecit eam et in amicitiam mulierum ferore pro damnatione dedicauit. Ampli autem aduersus filium iracundiam regis incendebat, uir samarites antipater nomine qui filio regis antipatro curator extabat. Nam cum alia quidem eius in tormentis aperuisset, illud quoque prodiderat, quoniam uenenum mortiferum confecerat, dederatque ferorae, iubens ut post eius abscensum cum iam spatium aliquanti temporis cucurisset ubi ratio prouocaret patri protinus propinaret, et dicebat attulisse illud uenenum ex aegypto anti filium unum examicis antipatri, transmissum autem ferorae per theudionem fratrem matris antipatri et hoc modo ad uxorem ferore deuenisse dantem marito ad custodiendum Quod illa quoque fabebatur rege scrutante negotium et procurrens tamquam uenenum ad latura, misit se detecto deorsum non tamen interiit. Quo cadens inpedes terra suscepta sit. Ac de inde post quam recreauit animam promittit ei herodes salutem eiusque domesticis dum modo nequaquam ab ea occultaretur ueritas, neque se illi malum pro ingratitudine redditurum iurabat, si cuncta cum ueritate proderet uel modum quo gesta constarent. Ad haec illa dicebat iusta atque ab aliis se nuntiata firmabat ad latum esse uenenum ex aegypto ad antifalo medico, quippe esse fratre enim agebat a quo prouisum fuerat, per theudionem autem uiro suo transmissum, se uero illud custotire a ferora susceptum, aduersum ipsum sane ab antipatro praeparatum. Cum igitur feroras egritudine teneretur et eum aduentu tuo consolationeque curares uidens circa se tuam beniuolentiam concidit mente deiecta et me conuocans o mulier inquit induxunt me antipater aduersus patrem suum fratrem meum consilia in qua constituens. Nam uenenumin eius pernitiem nundinatus est. Nunc itaque quoniam frater ergame nec ante iniquum aliquid gessit et nunc propositum bone uoluntatis ostendit. Me autem non multum de hac luce sentiore cessurum a gene cum conscientia fratricidii ad nostros pro genitores abierim. Illud uenenum ad portans epistolamque antipatri me uidente conbure. Ego autem plurimum enim igni contradens, aliquantulum reseruaui, ut ferora defuncto sime o rex male fortassis ad tenderes ut illo usa saeculi huius necessitates effugerent. Haec dicens et uenenum et pixida in medium protulit. Sed etiam frater antifili et mater eius eadem fatebantur tormentorum conpulsi uehementi. Apoxidam quoque illam nihil hominus agnoscebant. Accusabatur filia pontificis uxor regis tamquam omnium conscia fuisset sed ea celare maluerit Obque illa quidem herodes emisit. Filium autem eius ex testamento deleuit in ceteris permanente, sed etiam socerum pontificatu priuauit symonem boethi, substituit uero mathiam theofili hierosolimitem genere. Dum ea geruntur Bathillus quoque ex liberos antipatri uenit ex roma et tormentis examinatus inuenitur uenenum aliud attulisse quod matri daret antipatri et illa ferore tradendum ut si primum uenenum minus regem fortitan permisset, et hoc maturius uterentur. Aportabat etiam litteras ab amicis herodis romae constitutis consilio antipatri et dictatione compositas accusationem habentes archelai atque philippi quod quasi de patre quererentur pro nece aristoboli et alexandri. Semet ipsos quoque hero miserari nuntiabant, et euocabantur quidem a patre ueluti non ab alias res nisi ut etiam ipsos extingueret. Haec quippe magnorum munerum amici gerebant opitulantes antipatro Scripsit etiam antipater patri de fratribus culparum genera magna confingens omni modo eos ad iudicans etatem eorum ausam ascribens qua impelli possent nequitiam suam patrare praepositi. Ipse uero certamini quod cum filleogerebat magno studio fuit intentus, et accusationi primorum uiuorum romae constitutorum se totum dederet. Munilia quoque praetiosa ducentis talentis empta parauerat. Miretur fortasse aliquis quoniam tantis aduersus eum in iudaea motis turbinibus ferme septem mensuum tempore decurrente nihil illi fuerit nunciatum. Causa uero huius rei erat obseruatio uiarum atque custodia et odium hominum quo circa eum cum execratione tenebantur. Nullus et enim erat qui pronus esset proprio periculo illius tutamen salutemque conquirere
