<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-4-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="61"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num61" xml:id="greek-book17-num61" id="greek-book17-num61" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="6" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[61]</tei-num> Ἐπειδὴ Φερώρας τελευτᾷ ταφνίται ἐγεγόνεισαν αὐτοῦ ἀπελεύθεροι δύο τῶν Φερώρᾳ τιμίων οὗτοι προσελθόντες Ἡρώδῃ ἠξίουν μὴ ἀνεκδίκητον καταλιπεῖν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ τὸν νεκρόν, ἀλλὰ ζήτησιν ποιεῖσθαι τῆς ἀλόγου τε καὶ δυστυχοῦς μεταστάσεως. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[62]</tei-num> τοῦ δ᾽ ἐπιστραφέντος τοῖς λόγοις, πιστὰ γὰρ ἐδόκει, δειπνῆσαι μὲν αὐτὸν ἔλεγον παρὰ τῇ γυναικὶ τῇ προτέρᾳ τῆς νόσου, φάρμακον δὲ προσκομισθὲν ἐν βρώματι μὴ πρότερον εἰωθότι ἐμφαγόντα ὑπὸ τούτου τελευτῆσαι: κομιστὸν μέντοι γενέσθαι τὸ φάρμακον ὑπὸ γυναικὸς ἐκ τῆς Ἀραβίας λόγῳ μὲν ἐπὶ προσποιήσεσιν ἐρώτων, φίλτρον γὰρ δὴ ὄνομα αὐτῷ εἶναι, τὸ δ᾽ ἀληθὲς ἐπὶ τῇ Φερώρου τελευτῇ. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[63]</tei-num> φαρμακιστόταται δέ εἰσι γυναικῶν αἱ ἐκ τῆς Ἀραβίας: ᾗ δὲ ταῦτα ἐπεκάλουν καὶ τῆς Συλλαίου ἐρωμένης ἐν ταῖς μάλιστα ὡμολόγητο εἶναι φίλη, πείσουσαί τε αὐτὴν ἐπὶ πράσει τοῦ φαρμάκου εἰς τοὺς τόπους ἐληλύθεσαν ἥ τε μήτηρ τῆς τοῦ Φερώρου γυναικὸς καὶ ἡ ἀδελφὴ καὶ ἐπανῆκον αὐτὴν ἀγόμεναι τοῦ δείπνου πρότερον ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[64]</tei-num> ὑπὸ τούτων ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν λόγων παροξυνθεὶς δούλας τε ἐβασάνιζε τῶν γυναικῶν <tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="7" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>καί τινας καὶ ἐλευθέρας, καὶ ὄντος ἀφανοῦς τοῦ πράγματος διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν ἐξειπεῖν τελευταία τις περιουσῶν αὐτῆς τῶν ἀλγηδόνων ἄλλο μὲν ἔφη οὐδέν, θεὸν δ᾽ ἐπικαλεῖσθαι τοιαῖσδε αἰκίαις δώσειν περιβαλεῖν τὴν Ἀντιπάτρου μητέρα κακῶν τῶν ἐπεχόντων αἰτίαν πᾶσιν γενομένην. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[65]</tei-num> ταῦτα εἰς ἐπίστασιν Ἡρώδην ἄγει, καὶ τὰ πάντα βασάνοις τῶν γυναικῶν ἀνάπυστα ἦν, οἵ τε κῶμοι καὶ κρυπταὶ σύνοδοι καὶ δὴ καὶ λόγων πρὸς μόνον τὸν υἱὸν εἰρημένων ἐξοίσεις πρὸς τὰς Φερώρου γυναῖκας: ἦν δὲ ταλάντων ἑκατὸν δωρεὰς ἐπικρύπτεσθαι φράζειν πρὸς Φερώραν τῷ Ἀντιπάτρῳ κέλευσις ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός: <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[66]</tei-num> μῖσός τε πρὸς τὸν πατέρα καὶ ὀλοφυρμοὶ πρὸς τὴν μητέρα, ὡς ἐπὶ μήκιστον τοῦ πατρὸς βιοῦν ἐξηγμένου καὶ αὐτῷ μηδὲν ἐλάσσονος τοῦ γήρως ἐπικειμένου, ὡς μηδ᾽ ἂν ἐλθοῦσαν τὴν βασιλείαν ὁμοίως εὐφρᾶναί ποτ᾽ αὐτόν: παρατρέφεσθαί τε πολλοὺς ἐπὶ τῇ βασιλείᾳ καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφῶν παῖδας οὐδαμῶς ἀδεῆ τὴν ἐλπίδα παρεχομένους τἀσφαλοῦς: <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[67]</tei-num> καὶ γὰρ δὴ καὶ νῦν, εἴ τι πάσχειν, αὐτὸν ἀδελφῷ μᾶλλον ἢ παιδὶ τῷ αὐτοῦ κελεύειν τὴν ἀρχὴν δίδοσθαι. ὠμότητά τε πολλὴν κατηγόρει τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ τὰς σφαγὰς τῶν υἱέων, φόβῳ τε μὴ καὶ αὐτῶν ἅπτοιτο ἤδη τὸν μὲν ἐπὶ Ῥώμης ἄρασθαι τέχνην ἐπινοῆσαι, Φερώραν δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς αὐτοῦ τετραρχίας.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num68" xml:id="greek-book17-num68" id="greek-book17-num68" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[68]</tei-num> Ταῦτα συνῇδεν γὰρ τοῖς λόγοις τῆς ἀδελφῆς, καὶ πολὺ τοῦ μὴ ἀπιστίαν ἔτι ὑποπτεύεσθαι συνῆγεν αὐτοῖς, ὁ βασιλεὺς κρατυνάμενος ἐπὶ κακίᾳ τῇ Ἀντιπάτρου τὴν Δῶριν τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν περὶ αὐτὴν κόσμον ταλάντων πολλῶν ὄντα ἀφελόμενος ἔπειτα αὐτὴν ἀποπέμπεται καὶ ταῖς Φερώρου γυναιξὶν φιλίαν ἐσπείσατο. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[69]</tei-num> μάλιστα δ᾽ ἐξώτρυνεν εἰς ὀργὴν κατὰ τοῦ παιδὸς τὸν βασιλέα Σαμαρείτης ἀνὴρ Ἀντίπατρος ἐπιτροπεύων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ βασιλέως Ἀντίπατρον, ἄλλα τε αὐτοῦ ἐν ταῖς βασάνοις κατειπὼν καὶ ὅτι παρασκευασάμενος φάρμακον θανάσιμον δοίη Φερώρᾳ κελεύσας παρὰ τὴν ἀποδημίαν αὐτοῦ, ἵν᾽ ὡς πλεῖστον ἀφεστήκοι τῶν ἐν τοιούτοις ὑποτοπασμῶν, τῷ πατρὶ δοῦναι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[70]</tei-num> καὶ κομίσαι μὲν Ἀντίφιλον ἐξ Αἰγύπτου τὸ φάρμακον ἕνα τῶν Ἀντιπάτρου φίλων, σταλῆναι δὲ ὡς Φερώραν διὰ Θευδίωνος μητρὸς Ἀντιπάτρου ἀδελφοῦ τοῦ βασιλέως παιδός, καὶ οὕτως ἐλθεῖν τὸ φάρμακον εἰς τὴν γυναῖκα τὴν Φερώρου δόντος φυλάσσειν τοῦ ἀνδρὸς αὐτῆς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[71]</tei-num> ἡ δὲ ὡμολόγει μὲν ἀνακρίναντος τοῦ βασιλέως, καὶ δραμοῦσα ὡς κομίσειεν ῥίπτει κατὰ τέγους ἑαυτήν, οὐ μὴν τελευτᾷ ἐπὶ πόδας τῆς πτώσεως γενομένης. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[72]</tei-num> καὶ οὕτως ἐπεὶ ἀνεκτήσατο αὐτὴν ἄδειάν τε αὐτῇ ὑπισχνούμενος καὶ τοῖς οἰκείοις μηδὲν ἐπ᾽ ἀφανισμῷ τἀληθοῦς τρεπομένῃ, τρίψειν γε μὴν κακοῖς τοῖς ὑστάτοις ἀγνωμονεῖν προθεμένην, ὑπισχνεῖται καὶ ὤμοσεν ἦ μὴν ἐρεῖν τὰ πάντα ὃν ἐπράχθη τρόπον, λέγουσα μὲν, ὡς ἔφασαν οἱ πολλοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀληθῆ τὰ πάντα. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[73]</tei-num> κεκόμισται γὰρ ἐκ τῆς Αἰγύπτου τὸ φάρμακον ὑπ᾽ Ἀντιφίλου, ἀδελφὸς δ᾽ ἐκείνῳ ἰατρὸς ὢν ἐπόρισεν, καὶ Θευδίωνος ὡς ἡμᾶς κομίσαντος ἐφύλασσον αὐτὴ παρὰ Φερώρου λαβοῦσα ἐπὶ σὲ ἡτοιμασμένον ὑπὸ Ἀντιπάτρου. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[74]</tei-num> ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐνόσει Φερώρας καὶ ἐθεράπευες αὐτὸν ἀφικόμενος, ὁρῶν σου τὴν εὔνοιαν, ᾗ περὶ αὐτὸν ἐχρῶ, ἐπεκλάσθη τε τῇ διανοίᾳ καὶ μετακαλέσας με, ‘ὦ γύναι, φησίν, περιώδευσέ με Ἀντίπατρος ἐπὶ πατρὶ μὲν τῷ αὐτοῦ, ἀδελφῷ δὲ τῷ 'μῷ, θανάσιμόν τε γνώμην συνθεὶς καὶ φάρμακον ᾧ διακονήσοιτο αὐτῇ πεπορισμένος. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[75]</tei-num> νῦν οὖν, ἐπειδὴ ὅ τε ἀδελφὸς οὐδὲν ἀρετῇ πρότερον ᾗ ἐχρῆτο περὶ ἐμοῦ ὑφαιρῶν ὦπται ἐμέ τε ἐλπὶς οὐκ εἰς μακρὰν ἀπέσεσθαι τοῦ βίου, φέρε μὴ γνώμῃ ἀδελφοκτόνῳ ἀποτισοίμην προπάτορας τοὺς ἐμαυτοῦ, τὸ φάρμακον καίειν τε ἐμοῦ βλέποντος, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[76]</tei-num> κομίσασά τε οὐδὲν εἰς ἀναβολὰς πράσσειν τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τὰς ἐπιστολάς.’ καὶ τὸ μὲν πλεῖστον καύσασαν τοῦ φαρμάκου τυχεῖν, ὑπολιπέσθαι δὲ ὀλίγον, ἵνα εἰ Φερώρου μεταστάντος περιέποι κακῶς αὐτὴν ὁ βασιλεύς, μεθίσταιτο αὐτῷ διάδρασιν ποιουμένη τῶν ἀναγκῶν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[77]</tei-num> ταῦτα εἰποῦσα τό τε φάρμακον καὶ τὴν πυξίδα εἰς τὸ μέσον παρῆγεν. καὶ ἀδελφὸς δὲ Ἀντιφίλου ἕτερος καὶ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ ἀνάγκαις τε καὶ βασάνων σφοδρότητι ταὐτὰ ἔλεγον καὶ ἐγνώριζον τὴν πυξίδα. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[78]</tei-num> κατηγορεῖτο δὲ καὶ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως ἡ θυγάτηρ, γυνὴ δὲ τοῦ βασιλέως, ὡς πάντων ἵστωρ τούτων γενομένη κρύπτειν προθυμηθεῖσα αὐτά. καὶ διὰ τάδε Ἡρώδης ἐκείνην τε ἐξέβαλεν καὶ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς ἐξήλειψε τῶν διαθηκῶν εἰς ὃ βασιλεύσοι μενουσῶν, καὶ τὸν πενθερὸν τὴν ἀρχιερωσύνην ἀφείλετο Σίμωνα τὸν τοῦ Βοηθοῦ, καθίσταται δὲ Ματθίαν τὸν Θεοφίλου Ἱεροσολυμίτην γένος.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num79" xml:id="greek-book17-num79" id="greek-book17-num79" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[79]</tei-num> Ἐν τούτῳ δὲ καὶ Βάθυλλος ἐκ Ῥώμης ἀπελεύθερος Ἀντιπάτρου παρῆν καὶ βασανισθεὶς εὑρίσκεται φάρμακον κομίζων δώσειν τε τῇ ἑαυτοῦ μητρὶ καὶ Φερώρᾳ, ὡς εἰ τὸ πρότερον μὴ ἅπτοιτο τοῦ βασιλέως, τούτῳ γοῦν μεταχειρίζοιντο αὐτόν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[80]</tei-num> ἀφίκετο δὲ γράμματα παρὰ τῶν ἐν Ῥώμῃ φίλων τῷ Ἡρώδῃ γνώμῃ καὶ ὑπαγορεύσει Ἀντιπάτρου ἐπὶ κατηγορίᾳ Ἀρχελάου καὶ Φιλίππου συγκείμενα, ὡς δῆθεν διαβάλλοιέν τε τὸν πατέρα ἐπὶ σφαγῇ τῶν περὶ Ἀριστόβουλον καὶ Ἀλέξανδρον, δι᾽ οἴκτου δὲ καὶ αὑτοὺς λαμβάνοιεν: ἤδη γὰρ καὶ ἐκαλοῦντο ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός, οὐχ ὡς ἐφ᾽ ἑτέροις, ἀλλ᾽ ἐπὶ τοῖς κἀκείνους προσαπολωλεκόσι κατακλήσεως αὐτῶν γινομένης. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[81]</tei-num> ταῦτα δὲ μεγάλων μισθῶν οἱ φίλοι τῷ Ἀντιπάτρῳ συνέπρασσον. γράφει δὲ καὐτὸς Ἀντίπατρος τῷ πατρὶ περὶ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ μεγίσταις τῶν αἰτιῶν καὶ παντελὲς ἀπαλλάσσειν φάσκων τὰ μειράκια, τῶν δὲ τῇ ἡλικίᾳ τὴν ἀνάθεσιν ποιούμενος. αὐτὸς δὲ τὰ περὶ Σύλλαιον ἠγωνίζετο καὶ θεραπεία τῶν πρώτων ἀνδρῶν ἐγεγόνει κόσμος τε ἀξιοπρεπὴς ταλάντων ἐώνητο διακοσίων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[82]</tei-num> θαυμάσειε δ᾽ ἄν τις, ὅτι τοσούτων ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ κατ᾽ αὐτοῦ κεκινημένων μησὶ πρότερον ἑπτὰ οὐδὲν αὐτῷ δῆλον γένοιτο: αἴτιον δ᾽ ἦν ἥ τε ἀκρίβεια καὶ φυλακὴ τῶν ὁδῶν καὶ μῖσος τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὰ πρὸς Ἀντίπατρον: οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἦν, ὃς προθύμως κινδύνῳ τῷ αὐτοῦ ποριστὴς τῶν ἐκείνου ἀσφαλειῶν καθίστατο.</tei-p>

greek.text: [61] Ἐπειδὴ Φερώρας τελευτᾷ ταφνίται ἐγεγόνεισαν αὐτοῦ ἀπελεύθεροι δύο τῶν Φερώρᾳ τιμίων οὗτοι προσελθόντες Ἡρώδῃ ἠξίουν μὴ ἀνεκδίκητον καταλιπεῖν τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ τὸν νεκρόν, ἀλλὰ ζήτησιν ποιεῖσθαι τῆς ἀλόγου τε καὶ δυστυχοῦς μεταστάσεως. [62] τοῦ δ᾽ ἐπιστραφέντος τοῖς λόγοις, πιστὰ γὰρ ἐδόκει, δειπνῆσαι μὲν αὐτὸν ἔλεγον παρὰ τῇ γυναικὶ τῇ προτέρᾳ τῆς νόσου, φάρμακον δὲ προσκομισθὲν ἐν βρώματι μὴ πρότερον εἰωθότι ἐμφαγόντα ὑπὸ τούτου τελευτῆσαι: κομιστὸν μέντοι γενέσθαι τὸ φάρμακον ὑπὸ γυναικὸς ἐκ τῆς Ἀραβίας λόγῳ μὲν ἐπὶ προσποιήσεσιν ἐρώτων, φίλτρον γὰρ δὴ ὄνομα αὐτῷ εἶναι, τὸ δ᾽ ἀληθὲς ἐπὶ τῇ Φερώρου τελευτῇ. [63] φαρμακιστόταται δέ εἰσι γυναικῶν αἱ ἐκ τῆς Ἀραβίας: ᾗ δὲ ταῦτα ἐπεκάλουν καὶ τῆς Συλλαίου ἐρωμένης ἐν ταῖς μάλιστα ὡμολόγητο εἶναι φίλη, πείσουσαί τε αὐτὴν ἐπὶ πράσει τοῦ φαρμάκου εἰς τοὺς τόπους ἐληλύθεσαν ἥ τε μήτηρ τῆς τοῦ Φερώρου γυναικὸς καὶ ἡ ἀδελφὴ καὶ ἐπανῆκον αὐτὴν ἀγόμεναι τοῦ δείπνου πρότερον ἡμέρᾳ μιᾷ. [64] ὑπὸ τούτων ὁ βασιλεὺς τῶν λόγων παροξυνθεὶς δούλας τε ἐβασάνιζε τῶν γυναικῶν καί τινας καὶ ἐλευθέρας, καὶ ὄντος ἀφανοῦς τοῦ πράγματος διὰ τὸ μηδεμίαν ἐξειπεῖν τελευταία τις περιουσῶν αὐτῆς τῶν ἀλγηδόνων ἄλλο μὲν ἔφη οὐδέν, θεὸν δ᾽ ἐπικαλεῖσθαι τοιαῖσδε αἰκίαις δώσειν περιβαλεῖν τὴν Ἀντιπάτρου μητέρα κακῶν τῶν ἐπεχόντων αἰτίαν πᾶσιν γενομένην. [65] ταῦτα εἰς ἐπίστασιν Ἡρώδην ἄγει, καὶ τὰ πάντα βασάνοις τῶν γυναικῶν ἀνάπυστα ἦν, οἵ τε κῶμοι καὶ κρυπταὶ σύνοδοι καὶ δὴ καὶ λόγων πρὸς μόνον τὸν υἱὸν εἰρημένων ἐξοίσεις πρὸς τὰς Φερώρου γυναῖκας: ἦν δὲ ταλάντων ἑκατὸν δωρεὰς ἐπικρύπτεσθαι φράζειν πρὸς Φερώραν τῷ Ἀντιπάτρῳ κέλευσις ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός: [66] μῖσός τε πρὸς τὸν πατέρα καὶ ὀλοφυρμοὶ πρὸς τὴν μητέρα, ὡς ἐπὶ μήκιστον τοῦ πατρὸς βιοῦν ἐξηγμένου καὶ αὐτῷ μηδὲν ἐλάσσονος τοῦ γήρως ἐπικειμένου, ὡς μηδ᾽ ἂν ἐλθοῦσαν τὴν βασιλείαν ὁμοίως εὐφρᾶναί ποτ᾽ αὐτόν: παρατρέφεσθαί τε πολλοὺς ἐπὶ τῇ βασιλείᾳ καὶ ἀδελφοὺς καὶ ἀδελφῶν παῖδας οὐδαμῶς ἀδεῆ τὴν ἐλπίδα παρεχομένους τἀσφαλοῦς: [67] καὶ γὰρ δὴ καὶ νῦν, εἴ τι πάσχειν, αὐτὸν ἀδελφῷ μᾶλλον ἢ παιδὶ τῷ αὐτοῦ κελεύειν τὴν ἀρχὴν δίδοσθαι. ὠμότητά τε πολλὴν κατηγόρει τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ τὰς σφαγὰς τῶν υἱέων, φόβῳ τε μὴ καὶ αὐτῶν ἅπτοιτο ἤδη τὸν μὲν ἐπὶ Ῥώμης ἄρασθαι τέχνην ἐπινοῆσαι, Φερώραν δὲ ἐπὶ τῆς αὐτοῦ τετραρχίας. [68] Ταῦτα συνῇδεν γὰρ τοῖς λόγοις τῆς ἀδελφῆς, καὶ πολὺ τοῦ μὴ ἀπιστίαν ἔτι ὑποπτεύεσθαι συνῆγεν αὐτοῖς, ὁ βασιλεὺς κρατυνάμενος ἐπὶ κακίᾳ τῇ Ἀντιπάτρου τὴν Δῶριν τὴν μητέρα αὐτοῦ πάντα τὸν περὶ αὐτὴν κόσμον ταλάντων πολλῶν ὄντα ἀφελόμενος ἔπειτα αὐτὴν ἀποπέμπεται καὶ ταῖς Φερώρου γυναιξὶν φιλίαν ἐσπείσατο. [69] μάλιστα δ᾽ ἐξώτρυνεν εἰς ὀργὴν κατὰ τοῦ παιδὸς τὸν βασιλέα Σαμαρείτης ἀνὴρ Ἀντίπατρος ἐπιτροπεύων τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ βασιλέως Ἀντίπατρον, ἄλλα τε αὐτοῦ ἐν ταῖς βασάνοις κατειπὼν καὶ ὅτι παρασκευασάμενος φάρμακον θανάσιμον δοίη Φερώρᾳ κελεύσας παρὰ τὴν ἀποδημίαν αὐτοῦ, ἵν᾽ ὡς πλεῖστον ἀφεστήκοι τῶν ἐν τοιούτοις ὑποτοπασμῶν, τῷ πατρὶ δοῦναι. [70] καὶ κομίσαι μὲν Ἀντίφιλον ἐξ Αἰγύπτου τὸ φάρμακον ἕνα τῶν Ἀντιπάτρου φίλων, σταλῆναι δὲ ὡς Φερώραν διὰ Θευδίωνος μητρὸς Ἀντιπάτρου ἀδελφοῦ τοῦ βασιλέως παιδός, καὶ οὕτως ἐλθεῖν τὸ φάρμακον εἰς τὴν γυναῖκα τὴν Φερώρου δόντος φυλάσσειν τοῦ ἀνδρὸς αὐτῆς. [71] ἡ δὲ ὡμολόγει μὲν ἀνακρίναντος τοῦ βασιλέως, καὶ δραμοῦσα ὡς κομίσειεν ῥίπτει κατὰ τέγους ἑαυτήν, οὐ μὴν τελευτᾷ ἐπὶ πόδας τῆς πτώσεως γενομένης. [72] καὶ οὕτως ἐπεὶ ἀνεκτήσατο αὐτὴν ἄδειάν τε αὐτῇ ὑπισχνούμενος καὶ τοῖς οἰκείοις μηδὲν ἐπ᾽ ἀφανισμῷ τἀληθοῦς τρεπομένῃ, τρίψειν γε μὴν κακοῖς τοῖς ὑστάτοις ἀγνωμονεῖν προθεμένην, ὑπισχνεῖται καὶ ὤμοσεν ἦ μὴν ἐρεῖν τὰ πάντα ὃν ἐπράχθη τρόπον, λέγουσα μὲν, ὡς ἔφασαν οἱ πολλοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων ἀληθῆ τὰ πάντα. [73] κεκόμισται γὰρ ἐκ τῆς Αἰγύπτου τὸ φάρμακον ὑπ᾽ Ἀντιφίλου, ἀδελφὸς δ᾽ ἐκείνῳ ἰατρὸς ὢν ἐπόρισεν, καὶ Θευδίωνος ὡς ἡμᾶς κομίσαντος ἐφύλασσον αὐτὴ παρὰ Φερώρου λαβοῦσα ἐπὶ σὲ ἡτοιμασμένον ὑπὸ Ἀντιπάτρου. [74] ἐπεὶ οὖν ἐνόσει Φερώρας καὶ ἐθεράπευες αὐτὸν ἀφικόμενος, ὁρῶν σου τὴν εὔνοιαν, ᾗ περὶ αὐτὸν ἐχρῶ, ἐπεκλάσθη τε τῇ διανοίᾳ καὶ μετακαλέσας με, ‘ὦ γύναι, φησίν, περιώδευσέ με Ἀντίπατρος ἐπὶ πατρὶ μὲν τῷ αὐτοῦ, ἀδελφῷ δὲ τῷ 'μῷ, θανάσιμόν τε γνώμην συνθεὶς καὶ φάρμακον ᾧ διακονήσοιτο αὐτῇ πεπορισμένος. [75] νῦν οὖν, ἐπειδὴ ὅ τε ἀδελφὸς οὐδὲν ἀρετῇ πρότερον ᾗ ἐχρῆτο περὶ ἐμοῦ ὑφαιρῶν ὦπται ἐμέ τε ἐλπὶς οὐκ εἰς μακρὰν ἀπέσεσθαι τοῦ βίου, φέρε μὴ γνώμῃ ἀδελφοκτόνῳ ἀποτισοίμην προπάτορας τοὺς ἐμαυτοῦ, τὸ φάρμακον καίειν τε ἐμοῦ βλέποντος, [76] κομίσασά τε οὐδὲν εἰς ἀναβολὰς πράσσειν τοῦ ἀνδρὸς τὰς ἐπιστολάς.’ καὶ τὸ μὲν πλεῖστον καύσασαν τοῦ φαρμάκου τυχεῖν, ὑπολιπέσθαι δὲ ὀλίγον, ἵνα εἰ Φερώρου μεταστάντος περιέποι κακῶς αὐτὴν ὁ βασιλεύς, μεθίσταιτο αὐτῷ διάδρασιν ποιουμένη τῶν ἀναγκῶν. [77] ταῦτα εἰποῦσα τό τε φάρμακον καὶ τὴν πυξίδα εἰς τὸ μέσον παρῆγεν. καὶ ἀδελφὸς δὲ Ἀντιφίλου ἕτερος καὶ μήτηρ αὐτοῦ ἀνάγκαις τε καὶ βασάνων σφοδρότητι ταὐτὰ ἔλεγον καὶ ἐγνώριζον τὴν πυξίδα. [78] κατηγορεῖτο δὲ καὶ τοῦ ἀρχιερέως ἡ θυγάτηρ, γυνὴ δὲ τοῦ βασιλέως, ὡς πάντων ἵστωρ τούτων γενομένη κρύπτειν προθυμηθεῖσα αὐτά. καὶ διὰ τάδε Ἡρώδης ἐκείνην τε ἐξέβαλεν καὶ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς ἐξήλειψε τῶν διαθηκῶν εἰς ὃ βασιλεύσοι μενουσῶν, καὶ τὸν πενθερὸν τὴν ἀρχιερωσύνην ἀφείλετο Σίμωνα τὸν τοῦ Βοηθοῦ, καθίσταται δὲ Ματθίαν τὸν Θεοφίλου Ἱεροσολυμίτην γένος. [79] Ἐν τούτῳ δὲ καὶ Βάθυλλος ἐκ Ῥώμης ἀπελεύθερος Ἀντιπάτρου παρῆν καὶ βασανισθεὶς εὑρίσκεται φάρμακον κομίζων δώσειν τε τῇ ἑαυτοῦ μητρὶ καὶ Φερώρᾳ, ὡς εἰ τὸ πρότερον μὴ ἅπτοιτο τοῦ βασιλέως, τούτῳ γοῦν μεταχειρίζοιντο αὐτόν. [80] ἀφίκετο δὲ γράμματα παρὰ τῶν ἐν Ῥώμῃ φίλων τῷ Ἡρώδῃ γνώμῃ καὶ ὑπαγορεύσει Ἀντιπάτρου ἐπὶ κατηγορίᾳ Ἀρχελάου καὶ Φιλίππου συγκείμενα, ὡς δῆθεν διαβάλλοιέν τε τὸν πατέρα ἐπὶ σφαγῇ τῶν περὶ Ἀριστόβουλον καὶ Ἀλέξανδρον, δι᾽ οἴκτου δὲ καὶ αὑτοὺς λαμβάνοιεν: ἤδη γὰρ καὶ ἐκαλοῦντο ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρός, οὐχ ὡς ἐφ᾽ ἑτέροις, ἀλλ᾽ ἐπὶ τοῖς κἀκείνους προσαπολωλεκόσι κατακλήσεως αὐτῶν γινομένης. [81] ταῦτα δὲ μεγάλων μισθῶν οἱ φίλοι τῷ Ἀντιπάτρῳ συνέπρασσον. γράφει δὲ καὐτὸς Ἀντίπατρος τῷ πατρὶ περὶ αὐτῶν ἐπὶ μεγίσταις τῶν αἰτιῶν καὶ παντελὲς ἀπαλλάσσειν φάσκων τὰ μειράκια, τῶν δὲ τῇ ἡλικίᾳ τὴν ἀνάθεσιν ποιούμενος. αὐτὸς δὲ τὰ περὶ Σύλλαιον ἠγωνίζετο καὶ θεραπεία τῶν πρώτων ἀνδρῶν ἐγεγόνει κόσμος τε ἀξιοπρεπὴς ταλάντων ἐώνητο διακοσίων. [82] θαυμάσειε δ᾽ ἄν τις, ὅτι τοσούτων ἐν Ἰουδαίᾳ κατ᾽ αὐτοῦ κεκινημένων μησὶ πρότερον ἑπτὰ οὐδὲν αὐτῷ δῆλον γένοιτο: αἴτιον δ᾽ ἦν ἥ τε ἀκρίβεια καὶ φυλακὴ τῶν ὁδῶν καὶ μῖσος τῶν ἀνθρώπων τὰ πρὸς Ἀντίπατρον: οὐδεὶς γὰρ ἦν, ὃς προθύμως κινδύνῳ τῷ αὐτοῦ ποριστὴς τῶν ἐκείνου ἀσφαλειῶν καθίστατο.

english.html:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-4-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="61"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num61" xml:id="english-book17-num61" id="english-book17-num61" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="6" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[61]</tei-num> AS soon as Pheroras was dead, and his funeral was over, two of Pheroras's freed-men, who were much esteemed by him, came to Herod, and entreated him not to leave the murder of his brother without avenging it, but to examine into such an unreasonable and unhappy death. When he was moved with these words, for they seemed to him to be true, they said that Pheroras supped with his wife the day before he fell sick, and that a certain potion was brought him in such a sort of food as he was not used to eat; but that when he had eaten, he died of it: that this potion was brought out of Arabia by a woman, under pretense indeed as a love-potion, for that was its name, but in reality to kill Pheroras; for that the Arabian women are skillful in making such poisons: and the woman to whom they ascribe this was confessedly a most intimate friend of one of Sylleus's mistresses; and that both the mother and the sister of Pheroras's wife had been at the places where she lived, and had persuaded her to sell them this potion, and had come back and brought it with them the day before that his supper. Hereupon the king was provoked, and put the women slaves to the torture, <tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="7" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>and some that were free with them; and as the fact did not yet appear, because none of them would confess it, at length one of them, under the utmost agonies, said no more but this, that she prayed that God would send the like agonies upon Antipater's mother, who had been the occasion of these miseries to all of them. This prayer induced Herod to increase the women's tortures, till thereby all was discovered; their merry meetings, their secret assemblies, and the disclosing of what he had said to his son alone unto Pheroras's women. (Now what Herod had charged Antipater to conceal, was the gift of a hundred talents to him not to have any conversation with Pheroras.) And what hatred he bore to his father; and that he complained to his mother how very long his father lived; and that he was himself almost an old man, insomuch that if the kingdom should come to him, it would not afford him any great pleasure; and that there were a great many of his brothers, or brothers' children, bringing up, that might have hopes of the kingdom as well as himself, all which made his own hopes of it uncertain; for that even now, if he should himself not live, Herod had ordained that the government should be conferred, not on his son, but rather on a brother. He also had accused the king of great barbarity, and of the slaughter of his sons; and that it was out of the fear he was under, lest he should do the like to him, that made him contrive this his journey to Rome, and Pheroras contrive to go to his own tetrarchy.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num68" xml:id="english-book17-num68" id="english-book17-num68" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[68]</tei-num> These confessions agreed with what his sister had told him, and tended greatly to corroborate her testimony, and to free her from the suspicion of her unfaithfulness to him. So the king having satisfied himself of the spite which Doris, Antipater's mother, as well as himself, bore to him, took away from her all her fine ornaments, which were worth many talents, and then sent her away, and entered into friendship with Pheroras's women. But he who most of all irritated the king against his son was one Antipater, the procurator of Antipater the king's son, who, when he was tortured, among other things, said that Antipater had prepared a deadly potion, and given it to Pheroras, with his desire that he would give it to his father during his absence, and when he was too remote to have the least suspicion cast upon him thereto relating; that Antiphilus, one of Antipater's friends, brought that potion out of Egypt; and that it was sent to Pheroras by Thendion, the brother of the mother of Antipater, the king's son, and by that means came to Pheroras's wife, her husband having given it her to keep. And when the king asked her about it, she confessed it; and as she was running to fetch it, she threw herself down from the house-top; yet did she not kill herself, because she fell upon her feet; by which means, when the king had comforted her, and had promised her and her domestics pardon, upon condition of their concealing nothing of the truth from him, but had threatened her with the utmost miseries if she proved ungrateful [and concealed any thing]: so she promised, and swore that she would speak out every thing, and tell after what manner every thing was done; and said what many took to be entirely true, that the potion was brought out of Egypt by Antiphilus; and that his brother, who was a physician, had procured it; and that when Thendion brought it us, she kept it upon Pheroras's committing it to her; and that it was prepared by Antipater for thee. When, therefore, Pheroras was fallen sick, and thou camest to him and tookest care of him, and when he saw the kindness thou hadst for him, his mind was overborne thereby. So he called me to him, and said to me, "O woman! Antipater hath circumvented me in this affair of his father and my brother, by persuading me to have a murderous intention to him, and procuring a potion to be subservient thereto; do thou, therefore, go and fetch my potion, (since my brother appears to have still the same virtuous disposition towards me which he had formerly, and I do not expect to live long myself, and that I may not defile my forefathers by the murder of a brother,) and burn it before my face:' that accordingly she immediately brought it, and did as her husband bade her; and that she burnt the greatest part of the potion; but that a little of it was left, that if the king, after Pheroras's death, should treat her ill, she might poison herself, and thereby get clear of her miseries." Upon her saying thus, she brought out the potion, and the box in which it was, before them all. Nay, there was another brother of Antiphilus, and his mother also, who, by the extremity of pain and torture, confessed the same things, and owned the box [to be that which had been brought out of Egypt]. The high priest's daughter also, who was the king's wife, was accused to have been conscious of all this, and had resolved to conceal it; for which reason Herod divorced her, and blotted her son out of his testament, wherein he had been mentioned as one that was to reign after him; and he took the high priesthood away from his father-in-law, Simeon the son of Boethus, and appointed Matthias the son of Theophilus, who was born at Jerusalem, to be high priest in his room.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num79" xml:id="english-book17-num79" id="english-book17-num79" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[79]</tei-num> While this was doing, Bathyllus also, Antipater's freed-man, came from Rome, and, upon the torture, was found to have brought another potion, to give it into the hands of Antipater's mother, and of Pheroras, that if the former potion did not operate upon the king, this at least might carry him off. There came also letters from Herod's friends at Rome, by the approbation and at the suggestion of Antipater, to accuse Archelaus and Philip, as if they calumniated their father on account of the slaughter of Alexander and Aristobulus, and as if they commiserated their deaths, and as if, because they were sent for home, (for their father had already recalled them,) they concluded they were themselves also to be destroyed. These letters had been procured by great rewards by Antipater's friends; but Antipater himself wrote to his father about them, and laid the heaviest things to their charge; yet did he entirely excuse them of any guilt, and said they were but young men, and so imputed their words to their youth. But he said that he had himself been very busy in the affair relating to Sylleus, and in getting interest among the great men; and on that account had bought splendid ornaments to present them withal, which cost him two hundred talents. Now one may wonder how it came about, that while so many accusations were laid against him in Judea during seven months before this time, he was not made acquainted with any of them. The causes of which were, that the roads were exactly guarded, and that men hated Antipater; for there was nobody who would run any hazard himself to gain him any advantages.</tei-p>
					</tei-div>
english.text: [61] AS soon as Pheroras was dead, and his funeral was over, two of Pheroras's freed-men, who were much esteemed by him, came to Herod, and entreated him not to leave the murder of his brother without avenging it, but to examine into such an unreasonable and unhappy death. When he was moved with these words, for they seemed to him to be true, they said that Pheroras supped with his wife the day before he fell sick, and that a certain potion was brought him in such a sort of food as he was not used to eat; but that when he had eaten, he died of it: that this potion was brought out of Arabia by a woman, under pretense indeed as a love-potion, for that was its name, but in reality to kill Pheroras; for that the Arabian women are skillful in making such poisons: and the woman to whom they ascribe this was confessedly a most intimate friend of one of Sylleus's mistresses; and that both the mother and the sister of Pheroras's wife had been at the places where she lived, and had persuaded her to sell them this potion, and had come back and brought it with them the day before that his supper. Hereupon the king was provoked, and put the women slaves to the torture, and some that were free with them; and as the fact did not yet appear, because none of them would confess it, at length one of them, under the utmost agonies, said no more but this, that she prayed that God would send the like agonies upon Antipater's mother, who had been the occasion of these miseries to all of them. This prayer induced Herod to increase the women's tortures, till thereby all was discovered; their merry meetings, their secret assemblies, and the disclosing of what he had said to his son alone unto Pheroras's women. (Now what Herod had charged Antipater to conceal, was the gift of a hundred talents to him not to have any conversation with Pheroras.) And what hatred he bore to his father; and that he complained to his mother how very long his father lived; and that he was himself almost an old man, insomuch that if the kingdom should come to him, it would not afford him any great pleasure; and that there were a great many of his brothers, or brothers' children, bringing up, that might have hopes of the kingdom as well as himself, all which made his own hopes of it uncertain; for that even now, if he should himself not live, Herod had ordained that the government should be conferred, not on his son, but rather on a brother. He also had accused the king of great barbarity, and of the slaughter of his sons; and that it was out of the fear he was under, lest he should do the like to him, that made him contrive this his journey to Rome, and Pheroras contrive to go to his own tetrarchy. [68] These confessions agreed with what his sister had told him, and tended greatly to corroborate her testimony, and to free her from the suspicion of her unfaithfulness to him. So the king having satisfied himself of the spite which Doris, Antipater's mother, as well as himself, bore to him, took away from her all her fine ornaments, which were worth many talents, and then sent her away, and entered into friendship with Pheroras's women. But he who most of all irritated the king against his son was one Antipater, the procurator of Antipater the king's son, who, when he was tortured, among other things, said that Antipater had prepared a deadly potion, and given it to Pheroras, with his desire that he would give it to his father during his absence, and when he was too remote to have the least suspicion cast upon him thereto relating; that Antiphilus, one of Antipater's friends, brought that potion out of Egypt; and that it was sent to Pheroras by Thendion, the brother of the mother of Antipater, the king's son, and by that means came to Pheroras's wife, her husband having given it her to keep. And when the king asked her about it, she confessed it; and as she was running to fetch it, she threw herself down from the house-top; yet did she not kill herself, because she fell upon her feet; by which means, when the king had comforted her, and had promised her and her domestics pardon, upon condition of their concealing nothing of the truth from him, but had threatened her with the utmost miseries if she proved ungrateful [and concealed any thing]: so she promised, and swore that she would speak out every thing, and tell after what manner every thing was done; and said what many took to be entirely true, that the potion was brought out of Egypt by Antiphilus; and that his brother, who was a physician, had procured it; and that when Thendion brought it us, she kept it upon Pheroras's committing it to her; and that it was prepared by Antipater for thee. When, therefore, Pheroras was fallen sick, and thou camest to him and tookest care of him, and when he saw the kindness thou hadst for him, his mind was overborne thereby. So he called me to him, and said to me, "O woman! Antipater hath circumvented me in this affair of his father and my brother, by persuading me to have a murderous intention to him, and procuring a potion to be subservient thereto; do thou, therefore, go and fetch my potion, (since my brother appears to have still the same virtuous disposition towards me which he had formerly, and I do not expect to live long myself, and that I may not defile my forefathers by the murder of a brother,) and burn it before my face:' that accordingly she immediately brought it, and did as her husband bade her; and that she burnt the greatest part of the potion; but that a little of it was left, that if the king, after Pheroras's death, should treat her ill, she might poison herself, and thereby get clear of her miseries." Upon her saying thus, she brought out the potion, and the box in which it was, before them all. Nay, there was another brother of Antiphilus, and his mother also, who, by the extremity of pain and torture, confessed the same things, and owned the box [to be that which had been brought out of Egypt]. The high priest's daughter also, who was the king's wife, was accused to have been conscious of all this, and had resolved to conceal it; for which reason Herod divorced her, and blotted her son out of his testament, wherein he had been mentioned as one that was to reign after him; and he took the high priesthood away from his father-in-law, Simeon the son of Boethus, and appointed Matthias the son of Theophilus, who was born at Jerusalem, to be high priest in his room. [79] While this was doing, Bathyllus also, Antipater's freed-man, came from Rome, and, upon the torture, was found to have brought another potion, to give it into the hands of Antipater's mother, and of Pheroras, that if the former potion did not operate upon the king, this at least might carry him off. There came also letters from Herod's friends at Rome, by the approbation and at the suggestion of Antipater, to accuse Archelaus and Philip, as if they calumniated their father on account of the slaughter of Alexander and Aristobulus, and as if they commiserated their deaths, and as if, because they were sent for home, (for their father had already recalled them,) they concluded they were themselves also to be destroyed. These letters had been procured by great rewards by Antipater's friends; but Antipater himself wrote to his father about them, and laid the heaviest things to their charge; yet did he entirely excuse them of any guilt, and said they were but young men, and so imputed their words to their youth. But he said that he had himself been very busy in the affair relating to Sylleus, and in getting interest among the great men; and on that account had bought splendid ornaments to present them withal, which cost him two hundred talents. Now one may wonder how it came about, that while so many accusations were laid against him in Judea during seven months before this time, he was not made acquainted with any of them. The causes of which were, that the roads were exactly guarded, and that men hated Antipater; for there was nobody who would run any hazard himself to gain him any advantages.

<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-5-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="83"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num83" id="latin-book17-num83" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="8" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>VIII Herodes sane antipatro scribente quod cuncta quae oporteret per agens maturius adueniret caelans suam indignationem rescribit iubens ne ulla desidia aditer agendum propediretur, nequid in eius adstentia ipse forte pateretur. Et simul quoque de matre ipsius minimum quiddam ex postulanda causatur promittens tamen ei se reconciliatum iri cum ipse protinus adueniret, et in omnibus erga eum dilectionem suae quam si mentis aperiebat, formidans ne forte quicquam suspicians differret in eundae uiae negotium atque romae demorans aliquas possi debilitates pararet. Et in regno romano numerus alicuius fieret administer, hasitaque inci licia litteras suscepit. Alias autem taranti in quarum testu ferorae declarabatur occasus, quibus lectis egre satis tulum et aspere non propter ferorae gratiam sed quia patris interitu ut promiserat non per acto defecerat. Circa celenderum autem ciliciae ueniens cepit de causa nauigationis imbigere utrum deberet domum sicut instituerat tendere abiectione matris adductus indubium. Tunc examicis pars suadebant expectare donec agnosceret quae domi mota gestaque fuissent. Alii uero ortanbantur ne nauigationem domi differret. Soluturum enim suo aduentum omnes causas aduersitatis agebant. Namneque tunc aliunde illos fluc<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>tus euenisse nisi eius abscentia facultatem accusatoribus uirtutemque prebuisset. His persuasus protinus nauigauit et exceptus est portu nomine sebasto quem herodes magnis opibus constructum sebastum ad honorem caesaris appellauit. In apertis iam malis erat antipater nullo ad eum comminus accedente nullo conloquente sicuti cum fuisset egressus uotis eum ac secundis praecibus prosequebantur Nunc econtra aduersis eum maledictis non prohibebantur excipere uerebantur enim cuncti quod poenam esset fratribus pro sua impietate soluturus.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num89" id="latin-book17-num89" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Ea tempestate contigerat forte uarum quintillum in hierosolimis agere qui successor saturnini ad syriae regionem fuerat destinatus. Venerat quippe consultatum herodi ab eodem postulatus pro causis inquarum dispositionibuus hesitabat. Quibus una consensum habentibus uenit antipater cunctis illi rebus incognitis. Quique ingressus aulam regiam indutus purpura et ipsum quidem ianitores excipiunt. Amicos autem qui circa illum erant aulam excedere prohibebant. Coepit itaque perturbari in quae mala deuenerit manifesto cognoscens. Denique pater salutatum accedentem repulit, fratri cidii simul accusans, et consilia obiectans super suimet ipsius interitu, quorum omnium auditorem ac iudicem inscrastinum uarum fore confirmat, et ille quidem tanto malo audito pariter atque inminente ipsa magnitudine fatigatus abscessit, cui mater et uxor accurrunt quae residua fueret de filiabus antigoni qui ante herodem in iudaea regnauerat, ex quibus uniuersa cognoscens coepit se certamini iuditioque</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num93" id="latin-book17-num93" data-origname="p" data-processed="">preparare sed die postera consessum faciunt uariis simul atque rex amici etiam utrorumque conuocantur. Aderant quoque regis consanguinei et salome soror et siqui nuntiaturi forent quae prodiderant examiniatione tormentorum, serui denique antipatri ex materno illi iure conuenientes qui paulo ante fuerant conprehensi epistolam deferentes antipatro quae fuerat in hanc perscripta sententiam ne ad patriam repe<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00418.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="207v" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>daret. Quod cuncta uidelicet ad patris notitiam reuelata peruenissent. Solumque illi suffugium remanisse uel caesarem uel sub patris potestate non cadere. Antipatro uero patris genibus prouoluto atque deprecanti ne iudicium de illo rebus incognitis permereretur. Quin potius facultate sibi auditori contributa perur gatum irise apud patrem posse firmabat, quem iubens herodes in medium perduci, ipse lamentari primitus coepit. Quod tales illi filios habere contigisset per quod ei fortune tales exurgerent, aut inde tantam diuinitatis indignationem comparauerat ut sua senectus in antipatri nequititias incidisset memorabat etiam enutriciones et educationes quas filiss studiose praebuerat, opum quoque ac facultatum affluentiam inquibus cumque temporibus ipsi cuperent semper illis protinus adiacere nullum esse inpedimentum quo uoluntas eorum consilio periculum mortis incideret, dum illi regnum impie rapere festinarent ante quam ipse legi naturae concideret. unde se ualde miserari dicebat antipatrum quarum spe subleuatus auderet, sine ulla refreratione ad talia tantaque prorumpere, quando quidem eum regni successorem etiam scribendo declarasset. Sed etiam uitae suae tempore in nullo minor existeret non daritudine dignitatis non uirtute potentiae quinquaginta denique illum talenta ex reditibus fumere ad haec trecenta talenta romam eunti dono dedisse, increpabat illum etiam de fratribus quod si uelut malignos accusauerit cur eorum imitator extitisset. si uero innocentes fuissent inique aduersus consanguineos crimina confecisset. Nam illa omnia quae de illis nuntiata fuissent a nullo alio nisi ab illo semet ipsum protinus aduertisset consilioque eius gessisse cuncta quae aduersus illos fuerint gesta, quod nunc prorsus absolueret isto herode illis in patricidii facinore succedente.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num99" id="latin-book17-num99" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Haec simul dicens profundebat et lacrimas quae illum inter clusa uoce loqui amplius non sinebant. Verum nicolaus damascenus regis amicus et in omnibus cum eo una semperque uersatus et<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>modum quo res geste fuerint adsecutus, rogabatur a rege ut ipse residua loqueretur quae cumque ad demonstrationem causae redar gutionemque proficerent. Sed antipater econtra conuersus ad patrem semet ipsum excusare nitebatur, enurabat itaque cuncta suae circa illum begnitatis exempla, honoresque sibi a patre concessos, quos minime praecepisset nisi uirtute dignus et officiis erga illum meritus haberetur, enim uero prouidisse se semper ut usui necessaria forent, consiliumque semper circumspectis rationibus antecepisse, ac si quando ad rem explanandam manu opus esset suo labore negotia cuncta peregisse neque credibile constaret, ut qui saepius ex aliorum insidiis patrem strenue liberaret. Nunc ipsum insidiatorem patris effici ut deleret omnia suae uirtutis uetera momumenta, moliminere pentini facinoris. Presertim cum successor iam regni fuisset ostensus, et simul etiam rerum honorumque potiretur quae usque ad presens tempus eum habere constaret, neque illud esse ueri simile prorsus agebat. ut qui cunctarum rerum dimidium sine suis periculo et cum uirtutis honestitate teneret uellet totum cum crimine atque periculis appetere incertus utrumne ualeret effectum suae cupidinis optinere. Presertim cum pro tali causa suos fratres uidisset extinctos, quorum facinoris et nunciatorum et accusatorum ipsum esse constaret quod nisi et accusatorum ipsum esse constaret quod nisiab ipso proderetur occultum procul dubio permaneret. Quorum etiam post modum quod esset malignitas eorum circa patrem ad fidem perducta, punitor extaret, et ibi quidem haec sua dicebat esse monimenta quibus conuersationem suam cum magna beniuolentia circa patrem agitasse probaretur, romae uero quae gesserit testem caesarem conuocabat quem iuxta ac deum fallere nemo posset quorum fidem facere litteras ab eodem caesare destinatas, quibus litteris aut rectum esse, fortiores aut fideliores reputare, accusationes hominum uolentium inter eos turbas et iurgia concitare, quas accusatio <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00419.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="208r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb> nes asuis inimicis consictas agebat, quas se reuerso ultra iam habere non possent. Causabatur etiam de tormentis quod eorum uiolentia factum esset ut falsa dicerentur doloris quippe ac necessitates eam esse naturam ut doceat eos qui subiecti sunt, illa loqui quae uiderint grata dominantibus quorum se potestate tormentis adigi sentiunt.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num106" id="latin-book17-num106" data-origname="p" data-processed="">His dictis mutatio est, totius facta consessus, satis et enim miserabantur antipatrum profusione lacrimarum et uultus humilitate miserabilem ita ut etiam inimicis lamentabilis apparetet iam quoque, flectebatur herodis animus inclinatus licet conaretur suam mentem aliis non esse manifestam. Nicolaus autem exorsus ab illis uerbis quibus rex principium fecerat causam amplificare coepit et cuncta quae uel tormentis eruta uel testibus erant relata proferens congregabat undique criminis probamenta maxime uero uirtutem regis et dementiam longa narratione proferebat qualiter nitriciones et educationes in studiis doctrinarum filiis suis inpenderat, quarum rerum labor in nullo ei profecisset accommodus in alias <tei-del hand="?" data-origname="del" data-processed="">in</tei-del> aliis calamitatibus inruenti, quamquam se non imitari diceret proprium filiorum inconsiderationem quod et adhuc fuissent adulescentuli et deceptui facile a prauis suasoribus currupti in transuersum declinasse, natureque iura reliquisse ut inmaturius quam oporteret regnandi cupidine raperentur. Antipatri uero furiam ammodum se prorsus expauescere non modo propter paterna beneficia in quibus eum affatim fuerat muneratus, quae cum essent tam multa magnaque eius tamen animum lenem reddere non qui uere, more uenenatorum repentium licet illa repentia quamlibet sint aspera beneficiis aliquatenus leniuntur. Non solum ergo in hoc expauescere se dicebat prauitatem antipatri uerum etiam quod fortune iam fratrum pro exemplo praecederent. Quiminus imitator eorum existens imperum suum a crudelitate retineret quamquam o antipater qui teremi tatis fratrum nuntiator extitisti et scruta<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>tor documentorum et punitor redargutorum cur non repulisti animum quem in illis te prodente culpamus, sed potius ad imitandum flagitium illorum insana libidine raptus es. Vnde claret quod nec illa a te protutamine gesta sunt patris sed prostratrum in felicium interitu festinata, ut illorum odium ostentando amator quasi patris credereris, quatenus possis ad eius insidias iter facilius adipisci, postatem a patre percipiens quo etiam ipsis operibus approbatur. Ambiebas enim ut frates interimerentur de nequitia redarguti, ut autem conscii eis proderentur minime curasti. Vnde certum tequoque cum illis aduersus patrem insidias construxisse accusationem illis preparans ut si forte ad effectum uenissent tibi lucrum patricidii prouenisset, ut ex duobus pro certaminibus tu fructus perciperet gaudiorum tuis moribus competentes et circa fratres quidem qualis extiteris manifestus es nam super eorum morte uelut de rebus gloria bare magnificis. Quod quidem esset dignum ita te sapere si tu non deterior extitisses. Sed te occulto aduersario patris extante claret quia illos non ueluti patris insidiatores habebas exosos, nam haut ita exorbitares similem nequitiam cupiens per petrare, sed timens ne regni fierent successores quos tibi uidebat iustius posse praeponi. Patrem autem super fratres extinguere festinabat, ne celeriter tua aduersus frates factio proderetur, et pro quibus tu merebaris poenas luere ab infelici patre supplicium summere conareris. Ac parricidium non commune cogitasti, sed quale uix a quoquam nunc usque inuita hominum uel uideri potuit uel audiri. Non solum enim filius patri insidias praeparabas, uerum diligenti quoque et beneficia multa praestanti socius regni quippe consta bas, successor in nomine indispositionibus particeps, in fruendo communis, Nam et successor ante iam denunciatus, et iucundiatatem ac fructum regni iam ante capere in nullo prohibitus ad spem etiam futuri gerendam ex sententia patris et litteris communitus, sed tu non ex herodis clementia rerum iudex eras sed tua uoluntate ac nequitia opera paterna pensabas uolens patre <tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00420.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="208v" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>in omnibus tibi oboediente etiam partem quam possedisset abripere et confingebas uerbis uelle saluare eum quem rebus ipsis et operibus interimere nitebaris, et non solum tu malignus extabat uerum etiam matrem prauis tuis replebas inuentionibus fratrumque uoluntatem aduersam seditiosamque reddebas quin etiam patrem bestiam ausus es appellare cum habeas ipse mentem omni serpente peiorem. Siquidem illorum aduersus patrem qui tetantis beneficiis numeratus est, et contra eum auxilia diuersa postulabas et artibus uariis per uiros atque mulieres utebaris. Quatenus interimeres hominem senio et aetate confectum, quasi ad nocendum non sufficeret sola tua ementis iniquitas, et nunc uenisti post tormenta liberorum atque seruorum quae prop terte uiris atque mulieribus constant inflicta et contra denuntiationes coniuratorum tuorum inficiatum ire festines, et non solum patrem hominibus auferre meditatus es sed etiam leges uirtutemque uari et ipsius iuris naturam ipsamque conaris interimere ueritatem ita ne tua confidis inpudentia ut etiam tormentis semet ipsum subici cum causeris de tormentis eorum qui examinati sunt, ut illi quidem qui ea dixerunt quae ad liberationem tui patris adtineant ueritatem minime tenuisse uideantur, tormenta uero quae tibi fuerint adibita uelis indagasse ueritatem. Nonne saluasuare nonne liberas regem factionem a suo sanguine sustinentem. Per maiestatem imperii romani per uitutem tuam obtestamur, ut hanc atrocissimam bestiam quae pro perditione fratrum patri se beniuolum esse simulabat. Quatenus posset solitarius et omni consanguinitate desertus de regno percellere adiudices atque condemnes. Non pronuntias hunc sceleratum ducendum ad necem, scies quoniam patricidium communis iniuria est et naturae ipsius et totius uitae hominum neque minus facinorosus reputandus est qui cogitauerit tam et si eum affectum non con<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>tigerit adipisci. Naturam ipsam iniuriat qui talibus supplicia non inportat.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num121" id="latin-book17-num121" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Addebat etiam illa quae mater antipatri, ad aliquos stoliditate muliebri locuta est, ario lationes quoque ac diuinationes super rege factas et sacrificia memorabat. Agebat item et quicquid antipater cum ferorae mulieribus lasci iure dicebatur. Commes sationes quoque sordidas amoresque narrabat. Denique examinationes tormentorum et testificationes plurimas inferebat, quae sanae plurimae constabant. Nam alias quidem ante parauerat alias ex repentinis nuntiis fummitates acceperat ex quibus priora magisque firmabantur. Plurimi quippe homines que antea timore antipatri silentio pretereunda mandabant, cernentes eum accusationibus primis adibilem et aduersa fortuna inimicis enim aperte promp teque contraditum, quod odio in effabili aduersus eum nitebantur omnia tunc prodebant. Incitabantur quoque accusandum non solum horrore factorum enim et magnitudine scele rumque uel patrauerat uel patratum ire praesumpserat inprobitate quam circa capa trem et fratris exerceuerat parricidiis, et quod semper eum senserant neque odium merite neque amorem benignitate circa quem piam habuisse, sed suae tantum commoditatis intuitum. Quorum omnium illud deum amplius ad grauabat quod nulli extiterant quires exaequo bonoque iudicabant, quod eorum animus odio amicitia iurecaret. Dicebant ergo se olim ista sensisse prohibitosque semper annunciando libertatem uero data in medium cuncta deferre. A quibus proferebantur multiformia probamenta, nequauquam accusari de falsitate ualentia quod neque benignitate circa herodem neque timore periculoso tacerent. Sed solum rerum iudicio, iniquitatem antipatri proferebant dicentes quod non in suis actibus antipater utilitatem herodis et munimen adtenderet, sed sola<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00421.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="209r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>nequitia ad illa facinora fuerit concitatus, propter quam omni poena dignum esse loquebantur. Multa etiam a plurimis sine ulla interrogatione dicebantur, ita ut antipater quamquam in omnibus rebus inpudens et admentiendum promptissimus atque callidissimus, tamen tunc tanta confusione fuit opresus ut neque negare neque contradicere ualuisset. Nicolao igitur finem dicendi redarguendique faciente uarus iubebat antipatrum ut se tantis criminibus expurgaret, si aliquas astructio nec haberet. Quibus obnoxius illorum quae inportata erant non esse monstra rentur. Nam ipse quoque obtare se patre certa nosse dicebat ut in nullo contra se cogitasse fieret manifestus. Accendebat autem etiam salome pectus crebro percutiens, et se interfici postulans siquid fortitan tale in ea probaretur. Herodes autem conuocans filium interrogabat iubens ut siquid aperiret, increpabaturque, a patre dicente quoniam inimicus omnino repertus es age nunc et qui tecum ad haec negotia operam dedere nullomodo moreris aperire. Ille autem in antifilum cuncta referebat nullumque alium causam horum extitisse firmabat. Herodes uero ad modum dolens uolebat romam ad caesarem filium destinare ut supplicium pro suis factionibus semeret timens ne fortassis amicorum subfragio ualeret effugere, ipsum quidem uinctum sicuti et antea custodiebat. latin.text: VIII Herodes sane antipatro scribente quod cuncta quae oporteret per agens maturius adueniret caelans suam indignationem rescribit iubens ne ulla desidia aditer agendum propediretur, nequid in eius adstentia ipse forte pateretur. Et simul quoque de matre ipsius minimum quiddam ex postulanda causatur promittens tamen ei se reconciliatum iri cum ipse protinus adueniret, et in omnibus erga eum dilectionem suae quam si mentis aperiebat, formidans ne forte quicquam suspicians differret in eundae uiae negotium atque romae demorans aliquas possi debilitates pararet. Et in regno romano numerus alicuius fieret administer, hasitaque inci licia litteras suscepit. Alias autem taranti in quarum testu ferorae declarabatur occasus, quibus lectis egre satis tulum et aspere non propter ferorae gratiam sed quia patris interitu ut promiserat non per acto defecerat. Circa celenderum autem ciliciae ueniens cepit de causa nauigationis imbigere utrum deberet domum sicut instituerat tendere abiectione matris adductus indubium. Tunc examicis pars suadebant expectare donec agnosceret quae domi mota gestaque fuissent. Alii uero ortanbantur ne nauigationem domi differret. Soluturum enim suo aduentum omnes causas aduersitatis agebant. Namneque tunc aliunde illos fluctus euenisse nisi eius abscentia facultatem accusatoribus uirtutemque prebuisset. His persuasus protinus nauigauit et exceptus est portu nomine sebasto quem herodes magnis opibus constructum sebastum ad honorem caesaris appellauit. In apertis iam malis erat antipater nullo ad eum comminus accedente nullo conloquente sicuti cum fuisset egressus uotis eum ac secundis praecibus prosequebantur Nunc econtra aduersis eum maledictis non prohibebantur excipere uerebantur enim cuncti quod poenam esset fratribus pro sua impietate soluturus. Ea tempestate contigerat forte uarum quintillum in hierosolimis agere qui successor saturnini ad syriae regionem fuerat destinatus. Venerat quippe consultatum herodi ab eodem postulatus pro causis inquarum dispositionibuus hesitabat. Quibus una consensum habentibus uenit antipater cunctis illi rebus incognitis. Quique ingressus aulam regiam indutus purpura et ipsum quidem ianitores excipiunt. Amicos autem qui circa illum erant aulam excedere prohibebant. Coepit itaque perturbari in quae mala deuenerit manifesto cognoscens. Denique pater salutatum accedentem repulit, fratri cidii simul accusans, et consilia obiectans super suimet ipsius interitu, quorum omnium auditorem ac iudicem inscrastinum uarum fore confirmat, et ille quidem tanto malo audito pariter atque inminente ipsa magnitudine fatigatus abscessit, cui mater et uxor accurrunt quae residua fueret de filiabus antigoni qui ante herodem in iudaea regnauerat, ex quibus uniuersa cognoscens coepit se certamini iuditioque preparare sed die postera consessum faciunt uariis simul atque rex amici etiam utrorumque conuocantur. Aderant quoque regis consanguinei et salome soror et siqui nuntiaturi forent quae prodiderant examiniatione tormentorum, serui denique antipatri ex materno illi iure conuenientes qui paulo ante fuerant conprehensi epistolam deferentes antipatro quae fuerat in hanc perscripta sententiam ne ad patriam repedaret. Quod cuncta uidelicet ad patris notitiam reuelata peruenissent. Solumque illi suffugium remanisse uel caesarem uel sub patris potestate non cadere. Antipatro uero patris genibus prouoluto atque deprecanti ne iudicium de illo rebus incognitis permereretur. Quin potius facultate sibi auditori contributa perur gatum irise apud patrem posse firmabat, quem iubens herodes in medium perduci, ipse lamentari primitus coepit. Quod tales illi filios habere contigisset per quod ei fortune tales exurgerent, aut inde tantam diuinitatis indignationem comparauerat ut sua senectus in antipatri nequititias incidisset memorabat etiam enutriciones et educationes quas filiss studiose praebuerat, opum quoque ac facultatum affluentiam inquibus cumque temporibus ipsi cuperent semper illis protinus adiacere nullum esse inpedimentum quo uoluntas eorum consilio periculum mortis incideret, dum illi regnum impie rapere festinarent ante quam ipse legi naturae concideret. unde se ualde miserari dicebat antipatrum quarum spe subleuatus auderet, sine ulla refreratione ad talia tantaque prorumpere, quando quidem eum regni successorem etiam scribendo declarasset. Sed etiam uitae suae tempore in nullo minor existeret non daritudine dignitatis non uirtute potentiae quinquaginta denique illum talenta ex reditibus fumere ad haec trecenta talenta romam eunti dono dedisse, increpabat illum etiam de fratribus quod si uelut malignos accusauerit cur eorum imitator extitisset. si uero innocentes fuissent inique aduersus consanguineos crimina confecisset. Nam illa omnia quae de illis nuntiata fuissent a nullo alio nisi ab illo semet ipsum protinus aduertisset consilioque eius gessisse cuncta quae aduersus illos fuerint gesta, quod nunc prorsus absolueret isto herode illis in patricidii facinore succedente. Haec simul dicens profundebat et lacrimas quae illum inter clusa uoce loqui amplius non sinebant. Verum nicolaus damascenus regis amicus et in omnibus cum eo una semperque uersatus etmodum quo res geste fuerint adsecutus, rogabatur a rege ut ipse residua loqueretur quae cumque ad demonstrationem causae redar gutionemque proficerent. Sed antipater econtra conuersus ad patrem semet ipsum excusare nitebatur, enurabat itaque cuncta suae circa illum begnitatis exempla, honoresque sibi a patre concessos, quos minime praecepisset nisi uirtute dignus et officiis erga illum meritus haberetur, enim uero prouidisse se semper ut usui necessaria forent, consiliumque semper circumspectis rationibus antecepisse, ac si quando ad rem explanandam manu opus esset suo labore negotia cuncta peregisse neque credibile constaret, ut qui saepius ex aliorum insidiis patrem strenue liberaret. Nunc ipsum insidiatorem patris effici ut deleret omnia suae uirtutis uetera momumenta, moliminere pentini facinoris. Presertim cum successor iam regni fuisset ostensus, et simul etiam rerum honorumque potiretur quae usque ad presens tempus eum habere constaret, neque illud esse ueri simile prorsus agebat. ut qui cunctarum rerum dimidium sine suis periculo et cum uirtutis honestitate teneret uellet totum cum crimine atque periculis appetere incertus utrumne ualeret effectum suae cupidinis optinere. Presertim cum pro tali causa suos fratres uidisset extinctos, quorum facinoris et nunciatorum et accusatorum ipsum esse constaret quod nisi et accusatorum ipsum esse constaret quod nisiab ipso proderetur occultum procul dubio permaneret. Quorum etiam post modum quod esset malignitas eorum circa patrem ad fidem perducta, punitor extaret, et ibi quidem haec sua dicebat esse monimenta quibus conuersationem suam cum magna beniuolentia circa patrem agitasse probaretur, romae uero quae gesserit testem caesarem conuocabat quem iuxta ac deum fallere nemo posset quorum fidem facere litteras ab eodem caesare destinatas, quibus litteris aut rectum esse, fortiores aut fideliores reputare, accusationes hominum uolentium inter eos turbas et iurgia concitare, quas accusatio nes asuis inimicis consictas agebat, quas se reuerso ultra iam habere non possent. Causabatur etiam de tormentis quod eorum uiolentia factum esset ut falsa dicerentur doloris quippe ac necessitates eam esse naturam ut doceat eos qui subiecti sunt, illa loqui quae uiderint grata dominantibus quorum se potestate tormentis adigi sentiunt. His dictis mutatio est, totius facta consessus, satis et enim miserabantur antipatrum profusione lacrimarum et uultus humilitate miserabilem ita ut etiam inimicis lamentabilis apparetet iam quoque, flectebatur herodis animus inclinatus licet conaretur suam mentem aliis non esse manifestam. Nicolaus autem exorsus ab illis uerbis quibus rex principium fecerat causam amplificare coepit et cuncta quae uel tormentis eruta uel testibus erant relata proferens congregabat undique criminis probamenta maxime uero uirtutem regis et dementiam longa narratione proferebat qualiter nitriciones et educationes in studiis doctrinarum filiis suis inpenderat, quarum rerum labor in nullo ei profecisset accommodus in alias in aliis calamitatibus inruenti, quamquam se non imitari diceret proprium filiorum inconsiderationem quod et adhuc fuissent adulescentuli et deceptui facile a prauis suasoribus currupti in transuersum declinasse, natureque iura reliquisse ut inmaturius quam oporteret regnandi cupidine raperentur. Antipatri uero furiam ammodum se prorsus expauescere non modo propter paterna beneficia in quibus eum affatim fuerat muneratus, quae cum essent tam multa magnaque eius tamen animum lenem reddere non qui uere, more uenenatorum repentium licet illa repentia quamlibet sint aspera beneficiis aliquatenus leniuntur. Non solum ergo in hoc expauescere se dicebat prauitatem antipatri uerum etiam quod fortune iam fratrum pro exemplo praecederent. Quiminus imitator eorum existens imperum suum a crudelitate retineret quamquam o antipater qui teremi tatis fratrum nuntiator extitisti et scrutator documentorum et punitor redargutorum cur non repulisti animum quem in illis te prodente culpamus, sed potius ad imitandum flagitium illorum insana libidine raptus es. Vnde claret quod nec illa a te protutamine gesta sunt patris sed prostratrum in felicium interitu festinata, ut illorum odium ostentando amator quasi patris credereris, quatenus possis ad eius insidias iter facilius adipisci, postatem a patre percipiens quo etiam ipsis operibus approbatur. Ambiebas enim ut frates interimerentur de nequitia redarguti, ut autem conscii eis proderentur minime curasti. Vnde certum tequoque cum illis aduersus patrem insidias construxisse accusationem illis preparans ut si forte ad effectum uenissent tibi lucrum patricidii prouenisset, ut ex duobus pro certaminibus tu fructus perciperet gaudiorum tuis moribus competentes et circa fratres quidem qualis extiteris manifestus es nam super eorum morte uelut de rebus gloria bare magnificis. Quod quidem esset dignum ita te sapere si tu non deterior extitisses. Sed te occulto aduersario patris extante claret quia illos non ueluti patris insidiatores habebas exosos, nam haut ita exorbitares similem nequitiam cupiens per petrare, sed timens ne regni fierent successores quos tibi uidebat iustius posse praeponi. Patrem autem super fratres extinguere festinabat, ne celeriter tua aduersus frates factio proderetur, et pro quibus tu merebaris poenas luere ab infelici patre supplicium summere conareris. Ac parricidium non commune cogitasti, sed quale uix a quoquam nunc usque inuita hominum uel uideri potuit uel audiri. Non solum enim filius patri insidias praeparabas, uerum diligenti quoque et beneficia multa praestanti socius regni quippe consta bas, successor in nomine indispositionibus particeps, in fruendo communis, Nam et successor ante iam denunciatus, et iucundiatatem ac fructum regni iam ante capere in nullo prohibitus ad spem etiam futuri gerendam ex sententia patris et litteris communitus, sed tu non ex herodis clementia rerum iudex eras sed tua uoluntate ac nequitia opera paterna pensabas uolens patre in omnibus tibi oboediente etiam partem quam possedisset abripere et confingebas uerbis uelle saluare eum quem rebus ipsis et operibus interimere nitebaris, et non solum tu malignus extabat uerum etiam matrem prauis tuis replebas inuentionibus fratrumque uoluntatem aduersam seditiosamque reddebas quin etiam patrem bestiam ausus es appellare cum habeas ipse mentem omni serpente peiorem. Siquidem illorum aduersus patrem qui tetantis beneficiis numeratus est, et contra eum auxilia diuersa postulabas et artibus uariis per uiros atque mulieres utebaris. Quatenus interimeres hominem senio et aetate confectum, quasi ad nocendum non sufficeret sola tua ementis iniquitas, et nunc uenisti post tormenta liberorum atque seruorum quae prop terte uiris atque mulieribus constant inflicta et contra denuntiationes coniuratorum tuorum inficiatum ire festines, et non solum patrem hominibus auferre meditatus es sed etiam leges uirtutemque uari et ipsius iuris naturam ipsamque conaris interimere ueritatem ita ne tua confidis inpudentia ut etiam tormentis semet ipsum subici cum causeris de tormentis eorum qui examinati sunt, ut illi quidem qui ea dixerunt quae ad liberationem tui patris adtineant ueritatem minime tenuisse uideantur, tormenta uero quae tibi fuerint adibita uelis indagasse ueritatem. Nonne saluasuare nonne liberas regem factionem a suo sanguine sustinentem. Per maiestatem imperii romani per uitutem tuam obtestamur, ut hanc atrocissimam bestiam quae pro perditione fratrum patri se beniuolum esse simulabat. Quatenus posset solitarius et omni consanguinitate desertus de regno percellere adiudices atque condemnes. Non pronuntias hunc sceleratum ducendum ad necem, scies quoniam patricidium communis iniuria est et naturae ipsius et totius uitae hominum neque minus facinorosus reputandus est qui cogitauerit tam et si eum affectum non contigerit adipisci. Naturam ipsam iniuriat qui talibus supplicia non inportat. Addebat etiam illa quae mater antipatri, ad aliquos stoliditate muliebri locuta est, ario lationes quoque ac diuinationes super rege factas et sacrificia memorabat. Agebat item et quicquid antipater cum ferorae mulieribus lasci iure dicebatur. Commes sationes quoque sordidas amoresque narrabat. Denique examinationes tormentorum et testificationes plurimas inferebat, quae sanae plurimae constabant. Nam alias quidem ante parauerat alias ex repentinis nuntiis fummitates acceperat ex quibus priora magisque firmabantur. Plurimi quippe homines que antea timore antipatri silentio pretereunda mandabant, cernentes eum accusationibus primis adibilem et aduersa fortuna inimicis enim aperte promp teque contraditum, quod odio in effabili aduersus eum nitebantur omnia tunc prodebant. Incitabantur quoque accusandum non solum horrore factorum enim et magnitudine scele rumque uel patrauerat uel patratum ire praesumpserat inprobitate quam circa capa trem et fratris exerceuerat parricidiis, et quod semper eum senserant neque odium merite neque amorem benignitate circa quem piam habuisse, sed suae tantum commoditatis intuitum. Quorum omnium illud deum amplius ad grauabat quod nulli extiterant quires exaequo bonoque iudicabant, quod eorum animus odio amicitia iurecaret. Dicebant ergo se olim ista sensisse prohibitosque semper annunciando libertatem uero data in medium cuncta deferre. A quibus proferebantur multiformia probamenta, nequauquam accusari de falsitate ualentia quod neque benignitate circa herodem neque timore periculoso tacerent. Sed solum rerum iudicio, iniquitatem antipatri proferebant dicentes quod non in suis actibus antipater utilitatem herodis et munimen adtenderet, sed solanequitia ad illa facinora fuerit concitatus, propter quam omni poena dignum esse loquebantur. Multa etiam a plurimis sine ulla interrogatione dicebantur, ita ut antipater quamquam in omnibus rebus inpudens et admentiendum promptissimus atque callidissimus, tamen tunc tanta confusione fuit opresus ut neque negare neque contradicere ualuisset. Cum periculo quidem meo, sed cum tua tamen utilitate conscripsi tibique, direxi. Hanc autem illa conscripsit uolens filleo coniungi. Scidi igitur hanc epistulam ne fortassis ego de mea uita peridi tare. Ad ipsum autem antipatrum scriptaerat quod eius iussionibus ministerium gesserat ut ad herodem scriberet eo quod quasi salo ma insidias illi praeparare festinaret. Sed etiam rescriptum enim epistolae quae quasi ad suam dominam fuerat a salomae destinata direxerat. Erat autem hac me iudaea quidem genere, in seruitio autem erat iuliae caesaris coniugis, et haec gerebat amicitia quam cum antipatro iunxerat. Conparata ab eodem antipatro magni pecuniarum muneribus ut enim aduersus patrem et nutricem suffragaretur insidiis. Herodes autem obstupe factus magnitudinem nequitiarum antipatri, inpellebatur quidem ut confestim eum perimeret uelud pro cellam magnarum turbinemque causarum. Et non solum sibi sed etiam sorori insidiantem domumque caesaris sua iniquitate corrumpentem. Accendebat autem etiam salome pectus crebro percutiens, et se interfici postulans siquid fortitan tale in ea probaretur. Herodes autem conuocans filium interrogabat iubens ut siquid aperiret, increpabaturque, a patre dicente quoniam inimicus omnino repertus es age nunc et qui tecum ad haec negotia operam dedere nullomodo moreris aperire. Ille autem in antifilum cuncta referebat nullumque alium causam horum extitisse firmabat. Herodes uero ad modum dolens uolebat romam ad caesarem filium destinare ut supplicium pro suis factionibus semeret timens ne fortassis amicorum subfragio ualeret effugere, ipsum quidem uinctum sicuti et antea custodiebat. Verum legatos misit cum litteris ad accusandum filium intimandaque omnia quae acme illi ad perficiendam factionem fuerat suffragata exemplaria quoque transmisit epistolarum.
