But then, as to the affairs of his family and children, in which indeed, according to his own opinion, he was also very fortunate, because he was able to conquer his enemies, yet, in my opinion, he was herein very unfortunate.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num193" xml:id="english-book17-num193" id="english-book17-num193" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[193]</tei-num> But then Salome and Alexas, before the king's death was made known, dismissed those that were shut up in the hippodrome, and told them that the king ordered them to go away to their own lands, and take care of their own affairs, which was esteemed by the nation a great benefit. <tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="14" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>And now the king's death was made public, when Salome and Alexas gathered the soldiery together in the amphitheater at Jericho; and the first thing they did was, they read Herod's letter, written to the soldiery, thanking them for their fidelity and good-will to him, and exhorting them to afford his son Archelaus, whom he had appointed for their king, like fidelity and good-will. After which Ptolemy, who had the king's seal intrusted to him, read the king's testament, which was to be of force no otherwise than as it should stand when Caesar had inspected it; so there was presently an acclamation made to Archelaus, as king; and the soldiers came by bands, and their commanders with them, and promised the same good-will to him, and readiness to serve him, which they had exhibited to Herod; and they prayed God to be assistant to him.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num196" xml:id="english-book17-num196" id="english-book17-num196" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="15" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[196]</tei-num> After this was over, they prepared for his funeral, it being Archelaus's care that the procession to his father's sepulcher should be very sumptuous. Accordingly, he brought out all his ornaments to adorn the pomp of the funeral. The body was carried upon a golden bier, embroidered with very precious stones of great variety, and it was covered over with purple, as well as the body itself; he had a diadem upon his head, and above it a crown of gold: he also had a scepter in his right hand. About the bier were his sons and his numerous relations; next to these was the soldiery, distinguished according to their several countries and denominations; and they were put into the following order: First of all went his guards, then the band of Thracians, and after them the Germans; and next the band of Galatians, every one in their habiliments of war; and behind these marched the whole army in the same manner as they used to go out to war, and as they used to be put in array by their muster-masters and centurions; these were followed by five hundred of his domestics carrying spices. So they went eight furlongs to Herodium; for there by his own command he was to be buried. And thus did Herod end his life.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num200" xml:id="english-book17-num200" id="english-book17-num200" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[200]</tei-num> Now Archelaus paid him so much respect, as to continue his mourning till the seventh day; for so many days are appointed for it by the law of our fathers. And when he had given a treat to the multitude, and left off his motoring, he went up into the temple; he had also acclamations and praises given him, which way soever he went, every one striving with the rest who should appear to use the loudest acclamations. So he ascended a high elevation made for him, and took his seat, in a throne made of gold, and spake kindly to the multitude, and declared with what joy he received their acclamations, and the marks of the good-will they showed to him; and returned them thanks that they did not remember the injuries his father had done them to his disadvantage; and promised them he would endeavor not to be behindhand with them in rewarding their alacrity in his service, after a suitable manner; but that he should abstain at present from the name of king, and that he should have the honor of that dignity, if Caesar should confirm and settle that testament which his father had made; and that it was on this account, that when the army would have put the diadem on him at Jericho, he would not accept of that honor, which is usually so much desired, because it was not yet evident that he who was to be principally concerned in bestowing it would give it him; although, by his acceptance of the government, he should not want the ability of rewarding their kindness to him and that it should be his endeavor, as to all things wherein they were concerned, to prove in every respect better than his father. Whereupon the multitude, as it is usual with them, supposed that the first days of those that enter upon such governments declare the intentions of those that accept them; and so by how much Archelaus spake the more gently and civilly to them, by so much did they more highly commend him, and made application to him for the grant of what they desired. Some made a clamor that he would ease them of some of their annual payments; but others desired him to release those that were put into prison by Herod, who were many, and had been put there at several times; others of them required that he would take away those taxes which had been severely laid upon what was publicly sold and bought. So Archelaus contradicted them in nothing, since he pretended to do all things so as to get the good-will of the multitude to him, as looking upon that good-will to be a great step towards his preservation of the government. Hereupon he went and offered sacrifice to God, and then betook himself to feast with his friends.</tei-p>

latin.html:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-9-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="206"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num206" id="latin-book17-num206" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="16" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>XVI Cum haec interim aguntur congregantur iudaeorum iuuenes plurimi nouarum rerum cupidine concitati et ceperunt de morte mathiae aliorumque cum eo ab herode interemptorum tumultuosa uoce causari dicentes, quod iniuste perempti etiam exequiarum honore herodis timore caruerant. Erant autem isti pro quibus turba loquebatur qui fuerant pro euultione aureae aquile perempti. Magnum ergo illa turba pro clamante et damitationibus utente, quasdam etiam iniurias quasi ex hoc posset ad illos mortuos aliqua leuigatio peruenire. Proterue procaciterque iactante, congregabatur magis magisque numerosa multitudo et ultionem mortuorum ab archelao fieri debere poscebant suppliciis eorum qui sub herode fungebantur honoribus. Et primum quidem omnium sacerdotio remoueri pontificem quem herodes fecerat proclamabant uirum numdum et secundum leges suas dignum ad pontificatum promouendum esse dicebant. Archelaus autem licet iste grauiter ferret annuebat tamen impetum eorum initigare festinans donec iter adromam quod propositum habebat sine tumultu perageret, et tum cum de sese uoluntatem caesaris agnouisset respicere quid agendum foret, et de cunctis repetitionibus eorum legitime dispositarum, neque tunc tempus esse discensionis aut contumelia ingerendi magis autem unitatis atque concordiae, donec ex precepto caesaris ad eos cum firmitate regni recureret, tunc quippe in comune consulere de quibus cumque tractandum esse uideretur. Cum autem sustinendum esset ne forte seditiones quoque crimen incurrerent,</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num210" id="latin-book17-num210" data-origname="p" data-processed="">et ille quidem haec dicens ducemque suum e docens mittit ad eos haec ipsa locuturus. Illi porro proclamantes ducem loqui penitus non sinebant periculum quoque minabantur siquis eos ab assumptione sua reuocare uoluisset, et instabant sua<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00428.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="212v" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>libidine magis explere quam imperantium subiacere consiliis. Graue namque illis uidebatur si cum herode uiuente amicis priuati fuissent eodemque mortuo nullam ultionem fieri mortuorum. 					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num213" id="latin-book17-num213" data-origname="p" data-processed="">quod illa tempestate iudaeis dies factus imminebat quando azima secundum obseruationem paterni moris exercent. Sed iuuenes qui seditionem excitauere, iudam mathiamque lamentantur ueluti doctoris expo sitoresque legis antique et persistebant in templo Suffragatione quoque uictualium ab unde subsistente nam seditiosis hominibus turpe non ducebatur ab aliis cibos expetere. Anxius autem archelaus ne indeterius eorum processisset audatia, cohortes destinat armatorum cum quibus etiam tribu nium militarem mittit, ut eorum coherceat impetum, et primum quidem ut illos seditiosos repellerent et ab alia multitudine separarent, sed uenientibus militibus illi seditiosi cum ingenti alacritate excitata secum etiam turba super tribunum actota praesidia cum uoce magna inuicem hortantes impetum faciunt, ex quibus plurimi fusi pauci autem cum tribunos auciati diffugiunt, archelaus autem cuncta pessumire censebat nisi multitudinis illius impetum<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>frangeret tumultumque illum refecatum extingueret. Cunctam igitur mittit militiam, ut alii eos qui sibi in templo habitacula construxerant exinde reppellerent. Ceduntur itaque ab equitibus circiter tria milia hominum, reliqua uero in montes proximos refugit multitudo. Ceterum ex edictos cunctos ad suas regiones discedere iubet archelaus. Quique continuo discesserunt festiuitatem deserentes minime caelebratam maioris timore periculi propulsati, licet essent in morte temeritate praecipites. Philippe fratri omnia gubernanda derelinquit, domum ei regnumque commendans. Salome soror quoque herodis cum eo simul egreditur omnem secum ducens prosapiam, ad haec etiam plurimi cognatorum uerbo quidem ueluti cum archelao, conlaboraturi ut ei regum a cesare firmaretur,. Re autem uera ut aduersus eum niterentur maxime illa quae ab eo in templo gesta sunt accusando proponerent. Obuiam fit archelao sabinus caesaris curator earum rerum quae in syria possidebat in iudaeam pergens pro conseruatione thesaurorum herodis, quem uarus ab hac intentione reuocauit pertholomeum enim transibat ab archelao conuocatus. Sabinus ergo uari gratia neque arces optinuit quae cumque fuerant in iudaeorum ciuitatibus constitutae, neque thesauros consignauit sed omnia sub iure dimisit archelai. Proinde caesarea sustinuit sic enim promiserat esse facturum. <tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="17" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>XVII Sed cum roman nauigasset archelaus, uarus autem perrexit antiochiam sabinus ascendit in hierosolimam et aulas regias optinet, euo cansque omnes oppidorum praefectos, et quotquot rerum disponsatores fuerant ratiocinari coepit, et arces ut sibi traderentur expetere ex hoc iam illi quos praefecerat custodes arche<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00429.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="213r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>laus mandata eius implere non poterant sed custodiebant omnia secundum interdicta sabini usque ad caesaris praeceptum.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num224" id="latin-book17-num224" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Nauigat etiam romam in illis diebus antipater herodis filius regnum etiam ipse petiturus hortatu salomae et promissionibus incitatus dicentis iustiores causas illum habere archelao ad regnum percipiendum. Quod primum in quo is successor regni fuerat constitutus firmius quam illud sana mente fecisset herodes, hoc autem iam sensu praeualitudine de minuto conscripserat. Ducebat secum etiam matrem et fratrem nicolai ptolomeum amicum herodis satis honorabilem sed etiam sibi ualde gratissimum atque fauentes. Maxime autem eum incitabat ad regnum petendum irae neus re thor, uir oppinione clarus et addicendum acerrimus, id circo etiam freti, eos qui per suadebant cedendum archelao, siue quod regi testamento successor fuerit institutus. Siue quod maior natu esset, aduertere contempnabant, sed cum romam uenissent omnes cognati ab archelao discedentes ad istum conueniunt, non beniuolentia circa eum aliqua constricti, sed odio quod aduersus archelaum inritabantur. Maxime autem libertatem desiderabant, et romanorum iudices magis quam reges proprios habere cupiebant. Quod si hoc minus procederet antipatrum magis quam archelaum sibi regem conducibilius aestimantes impetrare laborabant. Sabinus quoque accusationem archelai apud caesarem deposuit.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num228" id="latin-book17-num228" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Inter haec caesar suscipiens ab archelao litteras in quibus iura a patre sibi relicta proposuit, testamentum quoque cognoscens et ratiocinia thesaurorum herodis cum nullo consignatorio quod ptolomeus apportauerat, coepit conspicari quid ordinandum ratio postularet, legens quoque litteras uariet episutulas sabini summam quoque thesaurorum uel quid pecuniae per singulos annos ingrederetur aduertens, litteras quoque quas antipater pregno per merendo transmiserat recenscens<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>congregabat ad consultandum omnes senatorii ordinis et amicos in quibus etiam gaium filium agrippe et iuliae suae filiae adoptiuum. Deinde illis omnibus inconsessu in ductis copiam facit ut quisque de quibus moueretur ediceret, ibi primum salomae filius antipater dicendi potentissimus et archelao infestus, huius scemodi uerba locutus est dicens. Archelao uerbo quidem pro regni petitione se fingere laborare, opere uero omnem regni potentiam possidere, antequam ei acefare in quo cuncta potestas sita esset indulgeretur. Huius testimonium esse dicebat eius audatiam qua presumpserat in die festo interimere. Quisi et iustum aliquid gessissent aliis inter eos deberet ulcisci qui eos possit legitima et ordinata potestate conpessere, et non ab illo tantam cedam fieri oportere. Qui si ut rex illud fecisset contumeliam grandem caesari intulisse firmabat. Quod ignorans quid de eo adhuc dispositurus esset regia iam uti potestate praesumeret Si autem uti priuatus illa gessisset, amplius eum deliquisse narrabat, quod regnum non possidens supplicia quibus libet intulerit de quibus decretum caesaris debuit expectari. Opponebat illi etiam iudicum militarium mutationes et ordinationes, ad haec etiam sedisse illum in solio regali et causam plurimas iudicasse ac determinasse proclamabat tam quam a rege legitimo eius potestatis integrum possidente. Petitionum quoque plurimorum pro misse publice facta memorabat, quid eum amplius iuris ac potestatis habiturum dum in regno caesare firmaretur. Opponebat illi etiam quod ex ypodromo uinctos sponte dimiserit ex plurima alia siue quae facta fuerant seu quae facta quidem non erant sed credibilia uidebantur. Propter naturam sui quod fieri posse iudicabantur a iuuene tum etiam abacenso regnandi cupidine dicebat etiam luctum eum patris penitus ne glegisse prohibitos quoque omnes a rege cummoreretur<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00430.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="123v" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>uiuendo unde initium quoque seditionis affirmabat exortum, quod eum uidebant circa patrem suum mortuum qui ei multa et magna bona praestiterat tam nequiter conseruari, ut uelut in se lacrimas per diem publice confin gentem oculto autem uoluptate regni percepti perfrui et noctes in deliciis agitare, erga caesarem quoque huius modi praebiturum archelaum cum ei regnandi iura tribueret, qualem se circa patrem exibuisse cognoscitur, tripudiare namque et cantus exercere in morte patris tamquam si hostis aliquis interiret, et quod nunc aduenisset ad caesarem caliditate usum dicebat, ut se regni firmitatem simularet cum omnia iam usus esset antea potestate quanta illi nec amplior a caesare rerum domino posset adtribui. Maxime uero caedem quae in templo facta fuerat uerbis exaggerabat, et impietatem abiectabat, quod in die festo sacrificiis diuinis instantibus multa milia hominum caesa fuissent in quibus multi peregrini plurimi insontes indigene miserabiliter occubuerint templum quoque plenun cadaueribus mortuorum non alienigena forte perimente sed eo qui se regni iura legitine percepisse iactabat. Unde apparet illud opus crudelitatis libidine peregisse ut integre se plenum tynannidis negotium persecutum esse testetur per iniquitatem amis sam qua cunctis hominibus constaret odibilis. Festinabat enim quoque modo regnum accipere sciens quod pro sui merito numquam posset uel insomnis regiam potestatem legitimo iure promereri nam et patri suo certos esse suos mores agnouerat, unde se regnum ab eo successorem disponi procul dubio desperabat, nisi pegritudinem ac morbos quibus non solum corpore confecto defecerat uerum etiam animo parum ualido erat ceterum quando mens eius sospes fuisset et sana et corpore forti, digne ac merite negotia cuncta disponeret in antipatrum potestatem regnandi contulerat testamento iure legitimoque confecto. Vnam qualis porro<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>rex iste possit exitere qui aut contempto caesare, ius sibi totius potestatis arripuit, aut sia caesare sed ominum fieri et ab eo regnum sperabat accipere, cur ciues suos sine illius praecepto priuatus ad huc et in templo die festo instante tam crudeliter interemit,</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num240" id="latin-book17-num240" data-origname="p" data-processed="">et antipatrus quidem huius modi uerba locutus testes etiam introduxit et plurimos excog natis per quos suas dicta firmaret. Cumque his loquendi finem faceret surgit nicolaus pro archelao uerba facturus. Dicebat itaque illa quidem quae in templo contigerant potius eorum qui passi sunt quam archelai potestate contigisse. Siquidem tantum eos facinus aggressos fuisse, ut non solum iniurias contumeliasque iactarent, sed etiam eos qui deuoti humiliter que uiuere disponebant ulcisci pertenderent. Cumque hostia multa operarentur, uerbo quidem aduersus archelaum rei autem acerbitate aduersus caesarem, necessarium archelaus iudicauit, ut eos ab insolentia et inprobitate reuocaret. Sed illi eos quos archelaus ad sedandas turbas miserat interimere festinabant, sine ulla dei uelloci festiuitatis reuerentia. Mittigare sesane dicebat non confundi antipatrum quod talium defensor existeret, dum modo in imicitiae suae quam contra archelaum gerebat libitum faceret et odio magis quam natura iustitiae iudicaret illos purgare gestiendo qui cunctos scelere aduersus suos principes arma corriperint. Cetera uero de quibus archelaum accusauerant in eos ipsos accusatores referebat dicens nihil sine ipsorum consulatione uel consensu factum gestumue fuisse, sed amino ledendi nunc intrans uersum ab aequitate discedere. Nam neque scirent taliter res esse dispositas qualiter accusabant, sed ab inuidiam archelai cuncta deprauare, et tantam illos cupidinem inuasisse obsistendi archelao uiro quidem consanguinitate propinquo conuersatione autem eis familiari per omnem tempus adiuncto. Testamentum etiam patrem<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00431.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="214r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>sana mentae conscripsisse narrabat firmiusque illud esset quod posterius fuisset scriptum quod in hoc posteriore dominum cuncte ordina dinationis caesarem constitueret, quem minime illorum improbitatem imitaturum dicebat qui iniuriam herodi facerent in cuius uita omnibus essent bonis omnique potestate perfuncti. Nunc autem ad contumelias uoluntatis quidem eius intellectus in omnibus festinarent sed nequaquam caesarem iniurias illius uiri permittere quia et amicus fuerit et auxiliator et omnia in sua potestate dimiserit. Neque pati ut testamentum eius soluetetur quod de sua fide fretus scripserit, neque uirtutem caesarir imitaturum esse illorum accusatorum criminatorumque nequitiam, fidem eius in omni mundo ad exemplar propositam et indubitatam cunctis gentis esse referebat. Vnde nequaquam possit herodi alienationem et furiam mentis scribere, quem per multum tempus optime regnu gessisse cognouerit. Successionemque optimo filio dedicasse, sed neque iudicium regis circa electionem successoris pecasse firmabat immo magis prudenter et optime iudicasse quod omnia ad uoluntatem potestatemque caesaris redigisset.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num248" id="latin-book17-num248" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Post quam haec nicolaus enarrauit et finem loquendi fecit, caesar archelaum sibi ad genua prodicentem cum honorificentia subleuauit, pronuntians eum dignum regni perceptione magnumque suae mentis momentum gratiamque declarauit non aliter esse fuisse facturum nisi quae cumque testamento continerentur. Interea archelao cuncti fauere, non tamen certum aliquid fuerat definitum. Igitur facta solutione consessus apud se ipsum caesar considerabat utrumne archelao regnum confirmari deberet, an omni herodis generi dispertiri.</tei-p>

Petitionum quoque plurimorum pro misse publice facta memorabat, quid eum amplius iuris ac potestatis habiturum dum in regno caesare firmaretur. Opponebat illi etiam quod ex ypodromo uinctos sponte dimiserit ex plurima alia siue quae facta fuerant seu quae facta quidem non erant sed credibilia uidebantur. Propter naturam sui quod fieri posse iudicabantur a iuuene tum etiam abacenso regnandi cupidine dicebat etiam luctum eum patris penitus ne glegisse prohibitos quoque omnes a rege cummorereturuiuendo unde initium quoque seditionis affirmabat exortum, quod eum uidebant circa patrem suum mortuum qui ei multa et magna bona praestiterat tam nequiter conseruari, ut uelut in se lacrimas per diem publice confin gentem oculto autem uoluptate regni percepti perfrui et noctes in deliciis agitare, erga caesarem quoque huius modi praebiturum archelaum cum ei regnandi iura tribueret, qualem se circa patrem exibuisse cognoscitur, tripudiare namque et cantus exercere in morte patris tamquam si hostis aliquis interiret, et quod nunc aduenisset ad caesarem caliditate usum dicebat, ut se regni firmitatem simularet cum omnia iam usus esset antea potestate quanta illi nec amplior a caesare rerum domino posset adtribui. Maxime uero caedem quae in templo facta fuerat uerbis exaggerabat, et impietatem abiectabat, quod in die festo sacrificiis diuinis instantibus multa milia hominum caesa fuissent in quibus multi peregrini plurimi insontes indigene miserabiliter occubuerint templum quoque plenun cadaueribus mortuorum non alienigena forte perimente sed eo qui se regni iura legitine percepisse iactabat. Unde apparet illud opus crudelitatis libidine peregisse ut integre se plenum tynannidis negotium persecutum esse testetur per iniquitatem amis sam qua cunctis hominibus constaret odibilis. Festinabat enim quoque modo regnum accipere sciens quod pro sui merito numquam posset uel insomnis regiam potestatem legitimo iure promereri nam et patri suo certos esse suos mores agnouerat, unde se regnum ab eo successorem disponi procul dubio desperabat, nisi pegritudinem ac morbos quibus non solum corpore confecto defecerat uerum etiam animo parum ualido erat ceterum quando mens eius sospes fuisset et sana et corpore forti, digne ac merite negotia cuncta disponeret in antipatrum potestatem regnandi contulerat testamento iure legitimoque confecto. Vnam qualis porrorex iste possit exitere qui aut contempto caesare, ius sibi totius potestatis arripuit, aut sia caesare sed ominum fieri et ab eo regnum sperabat accipere, cur ciues suos sine illius praecepto priuatus ad huc et in templo die festo instante tam crudeliter interemit, et antipatrus quidem huius modi uerba locutus testes etiam introduxit et plurimos excog natis per quos suas dicta firmaret. Cumque his loquendi finem faceret surgit nicolaus pro archelao uerba facturus. Dicebat itaque illa quidem quae in templo contigerant potius eorum qui passi sunt quam archelai potestate contigisse. Siquidem tantum eos facinus aggressos fuisse, ut non solum iniurias contumeliasque iactarent, sed etiam eos qui deuoti humiliter que uiuere disponebant ulcisci pertenderent. Cumque hostia multa operarentur, uerbo quidem aduersus archelaum rei autem acerbitate aduersus caesarem, necessarium archelaus iudicauit, ut eos ab insolentia et inprobitate reuocaret. Sed illi eos quos archelaus ad sedandas turbas miserat interimere festinabant, sine ulla dei uelloci festiuitatis reuerentia. Mittigare sesane dicebat non confundi antipatrum quod talium defensor existeret, dum modo in imicitiae suae quam contra archelaum gerebat libitum faceret et odio magis quam natura iustitiae iudicaret illos purgare gestiendo qui cunctos scelere aduersus suos principes arma corriperint. Cetera uero de quibus archelaum accusauerant in eos ipsos accusatores referebat dicens nihil sine ipsorum consulatione uel consensu factum gestumue fuisse, sed amino ledendi nunc intrans uersum ab aequitate discedere. Nam neque scirent taliter res esse dispositas qualiter accusabant, sed ab inuidiam archelai cuncta deprauare, et tantam illos cupidinem inuasisse obsistendi archelao uiro quidem consanguinitate propinquo conuersatione autem eis familiari per omnem tempus adiuncto. Testamentum etiam patremsana mentae conscripsisse narrabat firmiusque illud esset quod posterius fuisset scriptum quod in hoc posteriore dominum cuncte ordina dinationis caesarem constitueret, quem minime illorum improbitatem imitaturum dicebat qui iniuriam herodi facerent in cuius uita omnibus essent bonis omnique potestate perfuncti. Nunc autem ad contumelias uoluntatis quidem eius intellectus in omnibus festinarent sed nequaquam caesarem iniurias illius uiri permittere quia et amicus fuerit et auxiliator et omnia in sua potestate dimiserit. Neque pati ut testamentum eius soluetetur quod de sua fide fretus scripserit, neque uirtutem caesarir imitaturum esse illorum accusatorum criminatorumque nequitiam, fidem eius in omni mundo ad exemplar propositam et indubitatam cunctis gentis esse referebat. Vnde nequaquam possit herodi alienationem et furiam mentis scribere, quem per multum tempus optime regnu gessisse cognouerit. Successionemque optimo filio dedicasse, sed neque iudicium regis circa electionem successoris pecasse firmabat immo magis prudenter et optime iudicasse quod omnia ad uoluntatem potestatemque caesaris redigisset. Post quam haec nicolaus enarrauit et finem loquendi fecit, caesar archelaum sibi ad genua prodicentem cum honorificentia subleuauit, pronuntians eum dignum regni perceptione magnumque suae mentis momentum gratiamque declarauit non aliter esse fuisse facturum nisi quae cumque testamento continerentur. Interea archelao cuncti fauere, non tamen certum aliquid fuerat definitum. Igitur facta solutione consessus apud se ipsum caesar considerabat utrumne archelao regnum confirmari deberet, an omni herodis generi dispertiri.

greek.html:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-9-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="206"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num206" xml:id="greek-book17-num206" id="greek-book17-num206" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="16" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[206]</tei-num> Ἐν τούτῳ δέ τινες τῶν Ἰουδαίων συνελθόντες νεωτέρων ἐπιθυμίᾳ πραγμάτων Ματθίαν καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ὑφ᾽ Ἡρώδου ἀποθανόντας, οἳ παραχρῆμα τῆς εἰς τὸ πενθεῖσθαι τιμῆς φόβῳ τῷ ἐκείνου ἀπεστέρηντο, ἦσαν δὲ οἱ τῶν ἐπὶ καθαιρέσει τοῦ χρυσοῦ ἀετοῦ δεδικαιωμένων, ἐπὶ μέγα τε τῇ βοῇ καὶ οἰμωγῇ χρώμενοι καί τινα ὡς κούφισιν φέροντα τοῖς τεθνεῶσιν ἀπερρίπτουν εἰς τὸν βασιλέα. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[207]</tei-num> συνόδου τε αὐτοῖς γενομένης ἠξίουν τιμωρίαν αὐτοῖς ὑπ᾽ Ἀρχελάου γενέσθαι κολάσεσιν τῶν ὑπὸ Ἡρώδου τιμωμένων, καὶ πάντων γε καὶ πρῶτον καὶ ἐκδηλότατα τὸν ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἀρχιερέα καθεστῶτα παύσαντα νομιμώτερόν τε ἅμα καὶ καθαρὸν ἀρχιερᾶσθαι ἄνδρα αἱρεῖσθαι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[208]</tei-num> τούτοις Ἀρχέλαος καίπερ δεινῶς φέρων ἐπένευεν τὴν ὁρμὴν αὐτῶν διὰ τὴν ἐπὶ Ῥώμης ὁδὸν ἀνύεσθαι προκείμενον αὐτῷ τάχος ἐπὶ περισκοπήσει τῶν δοξάντων Καίσαρι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[209]</tei-num> πέμψας δὲ τὸν στρατηγὸν πειθοῖ χρῆσθαι, καὶ τῆς ἐπὶ τοιούτοις μωρίας ἀποστάντας σκοπεῖν, θάνατόν τε, ὃς τοῖς φίλοις αὐτῶν συνέλθοι, μετὰ νόμων γεγονότα, καὶ τὰς αἰτήσεις ὡς ἐπὶ μέγα τοῦ ὑβρίζειν προΐοιεν, τούς τε καιροὺς οὐκ ἐν τοιοῖσδε εἶναι, μᾶλλον δὲ τοῦ ὁμονοεῖν ἕως καταστησάμενος τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐπινεύσει τῇ Καίσαρος ἀφίκοιτο ὡς αὐτούς: τότε γὰρ κοινῇ βουλεύσειν περὶ ὧν ἀξιοῖεν σὺν αὐτοῖς: ἄρτι δὲ ἀνέχειν, μὴ καὶ στασιάζειν δοκοῖεν.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num210" xml:id="greek-book17-num210" id="greek-book17-num210" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[210]</tei-num> Καὶ ὁ μὲν ταῦτα ὑπειπὼν καὶ διδάξας τὸν στρατηγὸν ἐκπέμπει πρὸς αὐτούς. οἱ δὲ βοῶντες λέγειν τε οὐκ εἴων καὶ εἰς κίνδυνον τοῦ ἀπολουμένου ἐκεῖνόν τε καθίστασαν καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ὅστις γε ἐπὶ σωφρονισμῷ καὶ ἀποτροπῇ τοῦ μὴ τοιῶνδε ὀριγνᾶσθαι τολμήσειν φθέγξασθαι φανερὸς ἦν διὰ τὸ πάντα βουλήσει τῇ αὐτῶν μᾶλλον ἢ ἐξουσίᾳ τῶν ἐφεστηκότων συγχωρεῖν, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[211]</tei-num> δεινὸν ἡγούμενοι, εἰ ζῶντός τε Ἡρώδου στερηθεῖεν τῶν φιλτάτων καὶ τελευτῆς αὐτῷ γενομένης τιμωριῶν τῶν ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῖς, ὠργηκότες ταῖς γνώμαις καὶ νόμιμόν τε καὶ δίκαιον ἡγούμενοι ὅ τι μελλήσοι ἡδονὴν αὐτοῖς φέρειν, κίνδυνον δὲ τὸν ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ προϊδέσθαι τε ἀμαθεῖς καὶ εἴ τῳ ὑποπτευθείη, ὑπερβολῆς αὐτῷ γενομένης τῆς παραχρῆμα ἡδονῆς ἐκ τοῦ τιμωρήσασθαι τοὺς ἐχθίστους δοκοῦντας αὐτοῖς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[212]</tei-num> πολλῶν δὲ ὑπὸ Ἀρχελάου πεμπομένων, οἳ διαλέξοιντο αὐτοῖς, τῶν τε ἐνεστώτων μὲν ὑπ᾽ ἐκείνου γνώμῃ δὲ τῇ αὐτῶν δοκεῖν παριόντων, ὅπως εἰς τὸ πραΰτερον καταστήσονται αὐτούς, οὐδενὸς ἠνείχοντο εἰπεῖν ἀνάστασίς τε ἦν δεύειν ὀργῇ χρωμένων, φανεροί τε ἦσαν ἐπὶ μέγα αὐξήσοντες τὴν στάσιν πλήθους ἐπισυρρυέντος αὐτοῖς.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num213" xml:id="greek-book17-num213" id="greek-book17-num213" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[213]</tei-num> Ἐνστάσης δὲ κατὰ τόνδε τὸν καιρὸν ἑορτῆς, ἐν ᾗ Ἰουδαίοις ἄζυμα προτίθεσθαι πάτριον: φάσκα δ᾽ ἡ ἑορτὴ καλεῖται ὑπόμνημα οὖσα τῆς ἐξ Αἰγύπτου ἀπάρσεως αὐτῶν γενομένης, καὶ θύουσιν αὐτὴν προθύμως πλῆθός τε ἱερείων ὡς οὐκ ἐν ἄλλῃ κατακόπτειν ἐστὶν αὐτοῖς νόμιμον: <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[214]</tei-num> κάτεισιν δὲ πληθὺς ἀναρίθμητος ἐκ τῆς χώρας ἤδη δὲ καὶ ἐκ τῆς ὑπερορίας ἐπὶ θρησκείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ οἱ νεωτερισταὶ τοὺς περὶ τὸν Ἰούδαν τε καὶ Ματθίαν ἐξηγητὰς τῶν νόμων ὀδυρόμενοι συστάντες ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τροφῆς ηὐποροῦντο τοῖς στασιασταῖς οὐκ ὂν ἐν αἰσχύνῃ μεταιτεῖν αὐτούς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[215]</tei-num> καὶ δείσας Ἀρχέλαος, μὴ καί τι δεινὸν βλαστήσειεν αὐτῶν τῇ ἀπονοίᾳ, πέμπει σπεῖράν τε ὁπλιτῶν χιλίαρχόν τε τὴν ὁρμὴν τῶν ἐνεστηκότων πρότερον τὸν πάντα ὅμιλον τοῦ μανιώδους αὐτῶν πλέω καταστῆναι, καὶ εἴ τινες διάδηλοι πολὺ τῶν ἄλλων καθίσταιντο προθυμίᾳ τοῦ στασιάζειν ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸν ἀγαγεῖν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[216]</tei-num> ἐπὶ τούτῳ οἱ στασιῶται τῶν ἐξηγητῶν καὶ τὸ πλῆθος ἐξηγρίωσε βοῇ καὶ διακελευσμῷ χρώμενοι ὥρμησάν τε ἐπὶ τοὺς στρατιώτας καὶ περιστάντες λεύουσιν τοὺς πλείστους αὐτῶν. ὀλίγοι δέ τινες καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος τραυματίαι διέφυγον. καὶ τοῖς μὲν ταῦτα πράξασιν διὰ χειρῶν αὖθις ἡ θυσία ἦν: <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[217]</tei-num> Ἀρχελάῳ δὲ ἄπορον ἐδόκει σώζεσθαι τὰ πάντα μὴ οὐκ ἀνακόψειν τὴν ἐπὶ τοιοῖσδε ὁρμὴν τῆς πληθύος, ἐκπέμπει δὲ πᾶν τὸ στρατόπεδον * οἳ τούς τε αὐτόθι ἐσκηνωκότας κωλύοιεν τοῖς κατὰ τὸ ἱερὸν βοηθεῖν καὶ τοὺς ἐκπίπτοντας ὑπὸ τῶν πεζῶν δέχοιντο ἀντειλῆφθαι τἀσφαλοῦς ἤδη πεπιστευκότας. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[218]</tei-num> καὶ εἰς μὲν τρισχιλίους ἄνδρας ἔκτειναν οἱ ἱππεῖς: τὸ δὲ λοιπὸν ᾤχετο ἐπὶ ὄρη τὰ πλησίον ἰόντες. ἐκήρυσσε δ᾽ Ἀρχέλαος ἀναχωρεῖν ἐπὶ τὰ αὑτῶν πᾶσιν. οἱ δὲ ἀπῄεσαν τὴν ἑορτὴν καταλιπόντες φόβῳ κακοῦ μείζονος καίπερ θρασεῖς ὄντες διὰ τὸ ἀπαίδευτον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[219]</tei-num> Ἀρχέλαος δ᾽ ἐπὶ θαλάσσης κατῄει μετὰ τῆς μητρὸς Νικόλαον καὶ Πτολεμαῖον καὶ Πτόλλαν τῶν φίλων ἐπαγόμενος, Φιλίππῳ τἀδελφῷ τὰ πάντα ἐφεὶς καθίστασθαι τοῦ οἴκου καὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[220]</tei-num> συνεξῄει δ᾽ αὐτῷ καὶ Σαλώμη ἡ Ἡρώδου ἀδελφὴ γενεὰν ἀγομένη τὴν αὐτῆς, πολλοί τε τῶν συγγενῶν, λόγῳ μὲν ὡς συναγωνιούμενοι τῷ Ἀρχελάῳ ἐπὶ κτήσει τῆς βασιλείας, ἔργῳ δὲ ἀντιπράξοντες καὶ μάλιστα περὶ τῶν πεπραγμένων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ποιησόμενοι καταβοάς. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[221]</tei-num> ὑπαντιάζει δ᾽ ἐν Καισαρείᾳ τὸν Ἀρχέλαον Σαβῖνος Καίσαρος ἐπίτροπος τῶν ἐν Συρίᾳ πραγμάτων εἰς Ἰουδαίαν ὡρμημένος ἐπὶ φυλακῇ τῶν Ἡρώδου χρημάτων. καὶ αὐτὸν τῆς ἐπὶ τοῖσδε ὁρμῆς ἔσχεν ὁ Οὔαρος παρελθών: διὰ γὰρ Πτολεμαίου μετάπεμπτος ὑπ᾽ Ἀρχελάου παρῆν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[222]</tei-num> καὶ Οὐάρῳ Σαβῖνος χαριζόμενος οὔτε τὰς ἄκρας, ὅσαι ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἦσαν, παρέλαβεν οὔτε τοὺς θησαυροὺς κατεσημήνατο, εἴα δ᾽ ἔχειν Ἀρχέλαον μέχρι Καίσαρι δόξειέν τι περὶ αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔμενεν ἐν τῇ Καισαρείᾳ τοῦθ᾽ ὑποσχόμενος. <tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="17" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>ἐπεὶ δ᾽ ἐκπλεῖ μὲν ἐπὶ τῆς Ῥώμης Ἀρχέλαος, Οὐάρῳ δ᾽ ἐπ᾽ Ἀντιοχείας ἐγένοντο κομιδαί, Σαβῖνος ἐπὶ Ἱεροσολύμων χωρήσας παραλαμβάνει τὰ βασίλεια. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[223]</tei-num> μεταπέμψας δὲ τοὺς φρουράρχους καὶ ὁπόσοι διοικηταὶ τῶν πραγμάτων ἦσαν λόγους τε ἀπαιτεῖν πρόδηλος ἦν καὶ τὰς ἄκρας καθίστατο ᾗ αὐτῷ δοκοῖ. οὐ μὴν οἱ φύλακες ἐν ὀλίγῳ τὰς Ἀρχελάου ἐπιστολὰς ἐποιοῦντο, ἀλλ᾽ ἔμενον σώζοντες τὰ πάντα ᾗ προσετέτακτο αὐτοῖς. Καίσαρι δὲ φυλάσσειν ἕκαστ᾽ ἦν προσποίησις αὐτοῖς.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num224" xml:id="greek-book17-num224" id="greek-book17-num224" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[224]</tei-num> Πλεῖ δὲ κατὰ τοῦτον τὸν καιρὸν ἐπὶ Ῥώμης καὶ Ἀντίπας Ἡρώδου μὲν παῖς, ἐπὶ δ᾽ ἀντιποιήσει τῆς ἀρχῆς ὑποσχέσεσι Σαλώμης ἠρμένος ἐπὶ τῷ ἄρχειν καὶ πολὺ δικαιότερον Ἀρχελάου παραλήψεσθαι τὰ πράγματα ἠξιωκὼς τῷ κατὰ τὰς προτέρας διαθήκας βασιλεὺς ἀποπεφάνθαι, ἃς ἀσφαλεστέρας εἶναι τῶν ἐπιγραφεισῶν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[225]</tei-num> ἐπήγετο δὲ οὗτος τήν τε μητέρα καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν τὸν Νικολάου Πτολεμαῖον φίλον τε Ἡρώδῃ τιμιώτατον γεγενημένον καὶ αὐτῷ προσκείμενον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[226]</tei-num> μάλιστα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐνῆγεν ἐπ᾽ ἀντιποιήσει τῆς βασιλείας φρονεῖν Εἰρηναῖος ῥήτωρ ἀνὴρ καὶ δόξῃ δεινότητος τῆς περὶ αὐτῷ τὴν βασιλείαν πεπιστευμένος. διὸ δὴ καὶ τῶν κελευόντων εἴκειν Ἀρχελάῳ πρεσβυτέρῳ τε ὄντι κἀν ταῖς ἐπιδιαθήκαις ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐγγεγραμμένῳ βασιλεῖ οὐκ ἠνείχετο. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[227]</tei-num> ἐπεὶ δ᾽ εἰς τὴν Ῥώμην ἀφίκετο, καὶ πάντων τῶν συγγενῶν ἀπόστασις ἦν πρὸς αὐτόν, οὐκ εὐνοίᾳ τῇ ἐκείνου, μίσει δὲ τῷ πρὸς Ἀρχέλαον, μάλιστα μὲν ἐπιθυμοῦντες ἐλευθερίας καὶ ὑπὸ Ῥωμαίων στρατηγῷ τετάχθαι, εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα τι ἀντισταίη, λυσιτελέστερον Ἀρχελάου τὸν Ἀντίπαν λογιζόμενοι, συνέπραττον Ἀντίπᾳ τὴν βασιλείαν. καὶ Σαβῖνος κατηγόρει παρὰ Καίσαρι τοῦ Ἀρχελάου διὰ γραμμάτων.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num228" xml:id="greek-book17-num228" id="greek-book17-num228" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[228]</tei-num> Καῖσαρ δὲ Ἀρχελάου τε εἰσπέμψαντος ὡς αὐτὸν γράμματα, ἐν οἷς τὰ δικαιώματα προετίθει τε αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν διαθήκην τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοὺς λογισμοὺς τῶν Ἡρώδου χρημάτων σὺν τῷ σημαντῆρι κομίζοντα Πτολεμαῖον, ἐκαραδόκει τὸ μέλλον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[229]</tei-num> ὁ δὲ ταῦτά τε ἀναγνοὺς τὰ γράμματα καὶ τὰς Οὐάρου καὶ Σαβίνου ἐπιστολὰς ὁπόσα τε χρήματα ἦν καὶ τί ἐπ᾽ ἔτος ἐφοίτα καὶ ὅσα Ἀντίπας ἐπ᾽ οἰκειώσει τῆς βασιλείας ἐπεπόμφει γράμματα συνῆγεν ἐπὶ παροκωχῇ γνωμῶν τοὺς φίλους, σὺν οἷς καὶ Γάιον τὸν Ἀγρίππου μὲν καὶ Ἰουλίας τῆς αὐτοῦ θυγατρὸς υἱὸν ποιητὸν δὲ αὐτῷ γεγονότα πρῶτόν τε καθεδούμενον παρέλαβε, καὶ κελεύει λέγειν τοῖς βουλομένοις περὶ τῶν ἐνεστηκότων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[230]</tei-num> καὶ πρῶτος ὁ Σαλώμης υἱὸς Ἀντίπατρος δεινότατός τε ὢν εἰπεῖν καὶ τῷ Ἀρχελάῳ ἐναντιώτατος ἔλεγεν Ἀρχελάῳ παιδιὰν τὸν περὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς εἶναι λόγον ἔργῳ τὴν δύναμιν αὐτῆς πρότερον ἢ Καίσαρα συγχωρῆσαι παρειληφότι, ἐπικαλῶν τὰ τετολμημένα ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀπολωλόσι κατὰ τὴν ἑορτήν: <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[231]</tei-num> ὧν καὶ ἀδικούντων ἄλλως ἔσχεν τὴν τιμωρίαν εἰς τοὺς ἔξω χρῆσθαι δυναμένους ἀνακειμένην εἶναι, καὶ μὴ ὑπ᾽ ἀνδρὸς πεπρᾶχθαι, εἰ μὲν βασιλέως, ἀδικοῦντος τὸ Καίσαρος διαγνοίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἔτι χρώμενον, εἰ δὲ ἰδιώτου, πολὺ χειρόνως, διὰ τὸ μὴ βασιλείας ἀντιποιουμένῳ καλῶς ἂν συγκεχωρῆσθαι, διὰ τὸ Καίσαρα τῆς ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίας ἀφαιρεῖσθαι. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[232]</tei-num> καθήπτετο δὲ αὐτοῦ ἡγεμόνων τινῶν ἐν τῷ στρατιωτικῷ μετάστασιν ἐπικαλῶν καὶ προκάθισιν ἐπὶ θρόνου βασιλείου καὶ δικῶν διάλυσιν ὡς ὑπὸ βασιλέως γενομένην κατανεύσεις τε αἰτήσεων τοῖς δημοσίᾳ αἰτουμένοις καὶ πάντων διάπραξιν, ὧν οὐδὲν ἂν μειζόνως ἐπινοῆσαι καθεσταμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ Καίσαρος εἰς τὴν ἀρχήν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[233]</tei-num> ἀνετίθει δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τῶν ἐκ τοῦ ἱπποδρόμου δεσμωτῶν τὴν ἄφεσιν καὶ πολλὰ τὰ μὲν γεγονότα τὰ δὲ καὶ πιστεύεσθαι δυνάμενα διὰ τὸ φύσιν ἔχειν γίνεσθαι ὑπό τε νεωτέρων καὶ φιλοτιμίᾳ τοῦ ἄρχειν προλαμβανόντων τὴν ἐξουσίαν, πένθους τε τοῦ ἐπὶ τῷ πατρὶ ἀμελείας καὶ κωμασμοὺς αὐτονυκτὶ τῇ ἐκείνου τελευτῇ γεγονότας, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[234]</tei-num> ἐφ᾽ οἷς δὴ καὶ τὴν πληθὺν ἀρχὴν τοῦ στασιάζειν λαβεῖν, εἰ τοιαῦτα εὐεργετήσαντος αὐτὸ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ οὕτως μεγάλων ἠξιωκότος τοιοῖσδε ἀμείβεσθαι τὸν νέκυν, ὥσπερ ἐπὶ σκηνῆς δακρύειν μὲν προσποιούμενον τὰς ἡμέρας, ἀπολαύοντα δὲ ἡδονῇ τῇ ἐπὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς ὅσαι νύκτες. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[235]</tei-num> φανεῖσθαί τε καὶ περὶ τὸν Καίσαρα τοιόνδε ὄντα Ἀρχέλαον συγχωροῦντα τὴν βασιλείαν, ὁποῖος γένοιτο καὶ περὶ τὸν πατέρα: χορεύειν γὰρ καὶ ᾁδειν ὥσπερ ἐχθροῦ πεσόντος, ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἀνδρὸς οὕτως μὲν συγγενοῦς, τηλικαῦτα δ᾽ εὐεργετεῖν ἐξηγμένου. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[236]</tei-num> δεινότατόν τε πάντων ἀπέφηνε τὸ νῦν ἥκειν ἐπὶ Καίσαρος κατανεύσει τῇ ἐκείνου χρησόμενον τῇ βασιλείᾳ πάντων αὐτῷ προπεποιημένων, ὁπόσα γένοιτο ἂν ὑπὸ σοῦ βεβαίως ἤδη τοῦ αὐτοκράτορος παρεσχηκότος πρασσόμενα. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[237]</tei-num> μάλιστα δὲ τὴν σφαγὴν τῶν περὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐδείνου τῷ λόγῳ καὶ τὴν δυσσέβειαν, ὡς ἑορτῆς τε ἐνεστηκυίας καὶ ἱερείων ἐν τρόπῳ σφαχθεῖεν ἔνιοι μὲν ξένοι οἱ δὲ ἐγχώριοι, πλησθείη δὲ τὸ ἱερὸν νεκρῶν οὐχ ὑπ᾽ ἀλλοφύλου, ἀλλὰ τοῦ καὶ μετὰ νομίμων ὀνομάτων τῆς βασιλείας ἐφιεμένου τῆς πράξεως, ὅπως δυνηθείη πληρῶσαι τῆς φύσει τυραννίδος τὴν πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις μεμισημένην ἀδικίαν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[238]</tei-num> δι᾽ ἣν μηδὲ ὄναρ ποτὲ ἑωρᾶσθαι βασιλείας αὐτῷ τὴν διαδοχὴν ἀρετῇ τοῦ πατρός: ἐπίστασθαι γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὸν τρόπον καί τοι ἐχθρὸν αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν διαθηκῶν ἰσχυρότερον Ἀντιπάτρῳ καθίστασθαι: κληθῆναι γὰρ ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐπὶ τὴν βασιλείαν οὐχὶ νοσοῦντος πρὸς τῷ σώματι καὶ τὴν ψυχήν, ἀλλὰ ἀκραιφνεῖ μὲν τῷ λογισμῷ χρωμένου, ἀλκῇ δὲ σώματος τοῖς πράγμασιν ἐφεστηκότος. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[239]</tei-num> εἰ δὲ καὶ πρότερον εἰς αὐτὸν ἐπίσης τοῖς νῦν διατεθεῖσθαι τὸν πατέρα, ἀποπεφάνθαι ποταπὸς ἂν γένοιτο βασιλεὺς τὸν μὲν κύριον παρασχεῖν τὴν βασιλείαν Καίσαρα ἀφῃρημένον τοῦ δοῦναι τὴν ἐξουσίαν, τοὺς δὲ πολίτας ἰδιώτην ὄντα ἀκμὴν σφάζειν ἐν ἱερῷ μὴ ἀποτετραμμένον.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num240" xml:id="greek-book17-num240" id="greek-book17-num240" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[240]</tei-num> Καὶ Ἀντίπατρος μὲν τοιάδε εἰπὼν καὶ μαρτύρων παραστάσεσιν τὰ εἰρημένα κρατυνάμενος πολλοῖς τῶν συγγενῶν παύεται τοῦ λέγειν. ἀνίσταται δὲ Νικόλαος ὑπὲρ Ἀρχελάου καὶ ἔλεγεν τὰ μὲν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γνώμῃ τῶν πεπονθότων ἀναθεὶς μᾶλλον ἢ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ Ἀρχελάου: τοὺς γὰρ ἐπὶ τοιοῖσδε ἄρχοντας οὐ μόνον τῷ καθ᾽ αὑτοὺς ὑβρίζοντι εἶναι πονηρούς, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἀναγκάζοντι εἰς τὴν ἄμυναν τῶν εὐγνωμονεῖν προαιρουμένων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[241]</tei-num> ὡς δὲ πολέμια ἔδρων λόγῳ μὲν κατ᾽ Ἀρχελάου τὸ δὲ ἀληθὲς εἰς Καίσαρα φανερὸν εἶναι: τοὺς γὰρ ὑβριοῦντας κωλυτὰς παραγενομένους ἢ ὑπ᾽ Ἀρχελάου πεπομφότος κτεῖναι ἐπιθεμένους οὔτε τοῦ θεοῦ οὔτε τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἑορτῆς ἐν φροντίδι γενομένους, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[242]</tei-num> ὧν Ἀντίπατρον οὐκ αἰσχύνεσθαι ἐκδικητὴν καθιστάμενον ἐπὶ θεραπείᾳ ἔχθρας τῆς αὐτοῦ πρὸς Ἀρχέλαον ἢ φύσει τοῦ ἀρετῇ δικαίου. οἱ παρελθόντες καὶ μὴ πρὸς διανοουμένους ἄρχοντες ἀδίκων ἔργων, οἵδε εἰσὶν οἱ βιαζόμενοι καὶ μὴ θέλοντας τοὺς ἀμυνομένους ἐφ᾽ ὅπλα χωρεῖν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[243]</tei-num> ἀνετίθει δὲ καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ πᾶσι τοῖς ἐν βουλῇ τῶν κατηγόρων: οὐδὲν γὰρ ὅ τι μὴ οὐ μετὰ γνώμης τῆς αὐτῶν γεγενημένον αἰτίᾳ τοῦ ἀδικεῖν ὑπάγεσθαι, οὐ τῇ φύσει τῇ οὕτως αὐτὰ γεγονότα πονηρὰ εἶναι, ἀλλὰ τῷ βλάψειν ἂν δοκεῖν Ἀρχέλαον. τοσήνδε αὐτοῖς εἶναι βουλὴν τοῦ ὑβριοῦντος εἰς ἄνδρα συγγενῆ, καὶ πατρὸς μὲν εὐεργέτου, συνήθη δὲ αὐτοῖς καὶ διὰ παντὸς οἰκείως πεπολιτευμένον. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[244]</tei-num> τάς γε μὴν διαθήκας ὑπό τε σωφρονοῦντος γεγράφθαι τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ κυριωτέρας τῶν γεγραμμένων πρότερον διὰ τὸ Καίσαρι δεσπότῃ τῶν ὅλων καταλελεῖφθαι τὴν κρίσιν τῶν ἐν αὐταῖς γεγραμμένων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[245]</tei-num> μιμήσεσθαί τε οὐδαμῶς Καίσαρα τὴν ὕβριν αὐτῶν, οἳ τῆς Ἡρώδου παντοίως ἀπολαύσαντες παρ᾽ ὃν ἔζη καιρὸν δυνάμεως τὰ πάντα ἐπὶ ὕβρει γνώμης ἐπείγοιντο αὐτοῦ, οὐδ᾽ αὐτῶν περὶ τὸν συγγενῆ τοιούτων γεγονότων. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[246]</tei-num> οὔκουν Καίσαρά γε ἀνδρὸς ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ πεποιημένου τὰ πάντα καὶ φίλου καὶ συμμάχου καταλύσειν τὰς διαθήκας ἐπὶ πίστει τῇ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένας, οὐδὲ μιμήσεσθαι κακίαν τὴν ἐκείνων τὴν Καίσαρος ἀρετὴν καὶ πίστιν πρὸς ἅπασαν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀνενδοίαστον γενομένην, <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[247]</tei-num> καὶ μανίαν καὶ λογισμῶν ἔκστασιν κατακρίνειν ἀνδρὸς βασιλέως, υἱεῖ μὲν ἀγαθῷ τὴν διαδοχὴν καταλελοιπότος, πίστει δὲ τῇ αὐτοῦ προσπεφευγότος: οὔτ᾽ ἁμαρτάνειν Ἡρώδην ποτὲ περὶ κρίσιν τοῦ διαδόχου σωφροσύνῃ κεχρημένον ἐπὶ τῇ Καίσαρος γνώμῃ τὰ πάντα ποιεῖσθαι.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num248" xml:id="greek-book17-num248" id="greek-book17-num248" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[248]</tei-num> Καὶ Νικόλαος μὲν τοιάδε διελθὼν καταπαύει τὸν λόγον: Καῖσαρ δὲ Ἀρχέλαον προσπεσόντα αὐτῷ πρὸς τὰ γόνατα φιλοφρόνως τε ἀνίστη φάμενος ἀξιώτατον εἶναι τῆς βασιλείας πολλήν τε ἀπέφαινε τροπὴν γνώμης τῆς αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἄλλα πράξειν, ἀλλ᾽ ὁπόσα αἵ τε διαθῆκαι ὑπηγόρευον καὶ Ἀρχελάῳ συνέφερεν. <tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[249]</tei-num> οὐ μέντοι γε ἐκεκύρωτο οὐδέν, ὡς ἂν ἐχεγγύῳ παραδείγματι χρώμενον ἐπ᾽ ἀδείας Ἀρχέλαον εἶναι. καὶ διαλύσεως τῶν ἀνδρῶν γενομένης ἐσκοπεῖτο καθ᾽ αὑτόν, εἴτε Ἀρχελάῳ τὴν βασιλείαν ἐπικυρωτέον, εἴτε νομὴν αὐτῆς ποιεῖσθαι παντὶ τῷ Ἡρώδου γένει καὶ ταῦτα πάντων πολλῆς ἐπικουρίας δεομένων.</tei-p>

greek.text: [206] Ἐν τούτῳ δέ τινες τῶν Ἰουδαίων συνελθόντες νεωτέρων ἐπιθυμίᾳ πραγμάτων Ματθίαν καὶ τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ὑφ᾽ Ἡρώδου ἀποθανόντας, οἳ παραχρῆμα τῆς εἰς τὸ πενθεῖσθαι τιμῆς φόβῳ τῷ ἐκείνου ἀπεστέρηντο, ἦσαν δὲ οἱ τῶν ἐπὶ καθαιρέσει τοῦ χρυσοῦ ἀετοῦ δεδικαιωμένων, ἐπὶ μέγα τε τῇ βοῇ καὶ οἰμωγῇ χρώμενοι καί τινα ὡς κούφισιν φέροντα τοῖς τεθνεῶσιν ἀπερρίπτουν εἰς τὸν βασιλέα. [207] συνόδου τε αὐτοῖς γενομένης ἠξίουν τιμωρίαν αὐτοῖς ὑπ᾽ Ἀρχελάου γενέσθαι κολάσεσιν τῶν ὑπὸ Ἡρώδου τιμωμένων, καὶ πάντων γε καὶ πρῶτον καὶ ἐκδηλότατα τὸν ὑπ᾽ αὐτοῦ ἀρχιερέα καθεστῶτα παύσαντα νομιμώτερόν τε ἅμα καὶ καθαρὸν ἀρχιερᾶσθαι ἄνδρα αἱρεῖσθαι. [208] τούτοις Ἀρχέλαος καίπερ δεινῶς φέρων ἐπένευεν τὴν ὁρμὴν αὐτῶν διὰ τὴν ἐπὶ Ῥώμης ὁδὸν ἀνύεσθαι προκείμενον αὐτῷ τάχος ἐπὶ περισκοπήσει τῶν δοξάντων Καίσαρι. [209] πέμψας δὲ τὸν στρατηγὸν πειθοῖ χρῆσθαι, καὶ τῆς ἐπὶ τοιούτοις μωρίας ἀποστάντας σκοπεῖν, θάνατόν τε, ὃς τοῖς φίλοις αὐτῶν συνέλθοι, μετὰ νόμων γεγονότα, καὶ τὰς αἰτήσεις ὡς ἐπὶ μέγα τοῦ ὑβρίζειν προΐοιεν, τούς τε καιροὺς οὐκ ἐν τοιοῖσδε εἶναι, μᾶλλον δὲ τοῦ ὁμονοεῖν ἕως καταστησάμενος τὴν ἀρχὴν ἐπινεύσει τῇ Καίσαρος ἀφίκοιτο ὡς αὐτούς: τότε γὰρ κοινῇ βουλεύσειν περὶ ὧν ἀξιοῖεν σὺν αὐτοῖς: ἄρτι δὲ ἀνέχειν, μὴ καὶ στασιάζειν δοκοῖεν. [210] Καὶ ὁ μὲν ταῦτα ὑπειπὼν καὶ διδάξας τὸν στρατηγὸν ἐκπέμπει πρὸς αὐτούς. οἱ δὲ βοῶντες λέγειν τε οὐκ εἴων καὶ εἰς κίνδυνον τοῦ ἀπολουμένου ἐκεῖνόν τε καθίστασαν καὶ τῶν ἄλλων ὅστις γε ἐπὶ σωφρονισμῷ καὶ ἀποτροπῇ τοῦ μὴ τοιῶνδε ὀριγνᾶσθαι τολμήσειν φθέγξασθαι φανερὸς ἦν διὰ τὸ πάντα βουλήσει τῇ αὐτῶν μᾶλλον ἢ ἐξουσίᾳ τῶν ἐφεστηκότων συγχωρεῖν, [211] δεινὸν ἡγούμενοι, εἰ ζῶντός τε Ἡρώδου στερηθεῖεν τῶν φιλτάτων καὶ τελευτῆς αὐτῷ γενομένης τιμωριῶν τῶν ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῖς, ὠργηκότες ταῖς γνώμαις καὶ νόμιμόν τε καὶ δίκαιον ἡγούμενοι ὅ τι μελλήσοι ἡδονὴν αὐτοῖς φέρειν, κίνδυνον δὲ τὸν ἀπ᾽ αὐτοῦ προϊδέσθαι τε ἀμαθεῖς καὶ εἴ τῳ ὑποπτευθείη, ὑπερβολῆς αὐτῷ γενομένης τῆς παραχρῆμα ἡδονῆς ἐκ τοῦ τιμωρήσασθαι τοὺς ἐχθίστους δοκοῦντας αὐτοῖς. [212] πολλῶν δὲ ὑπὸ Ἀρχελάου πεμπομένων, οἳ διαλέξοιντο αὐτοῖς, τῶν τε ἐνεστώτων μὲν ὑπ᾽ ἐκείνου γνώμῃ δὲ τῇ αὐτῶν δοκεῖν παριόντων, ὅπως εἰς τὸ πραΰτερον καταστήσονται αὐτούς, οὐδενὸς ἠνείχοντο εἰπεῖν ἀνάστασίς τε ἦν δεύειν ὀργῇ χρωμένων, φανεροί τε ἦσαν ἐπὶ μέγα αὐξήσοντες τὴν στάσιν πλήθους ἐπισυρρυέντος αὐτοῖς. [213] Ἐνστάσης δὲ κατὰ τόνδε τὸν καιρὸν ἑορτῆς, ἐν ᾗ Ἰουδαίοις ἄζυμα προτίθεσθαι πάτριον: φάσκα δ᾽ ἡ ἑορτὴ καλεῖται ὑπόμνημα οὖσα τῆς ἐξ Αἰγύπτου ἀπάρσεως αὐτῶν γενομένης, καὶ θύουσιν αὐτὴν προθύμως πλῆθός τε ἱερείων ὡς οὐκ ἐν ἄλλῃ κατακόπτειν ἐστὶν αὐτοῖς νόμιμον: [214] κάτεισιν δὲ πληθὺς ἀναρίθμητος ἐκ τῆς χώρας ἤδη δὲ καὶ ἐκ τῆς ὑπερορίας ἐπὶ θρησκείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ, καὶ οἱ νεωτερισταὶ τοὺς περὶ τὸν Ἰούδαν τε καὶ Ματθίαν ἐξηγητὰς τῶν νόμων ὀδυρόμενοι συστάντες ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ τροφῆς ηὐποροῦντο τοῖς στασιασταῖς οὐκ ὂν ἐν αἰσχύνῃ μεταιτεῖν αὐτούς. [215] καὶ δείσας Ἀρχέλαος, μὴ καί τι δεινὸν βλαστήσειεν αὐτῶν τῇ ἀπονοίᾳ, πέμπει σπεῖράν τε ὁπλιτῶν χιλίαρχόν τε τὴν ὁρμὴν τῶν ἐνεστηκότων πρότερον τὸν πάντα ὅμιλον τοῦ μανιώδους αὐτῶν πλέω καταστῆναι, καὶ εἴ τινες διάδηλοι πολὺ τῶν ἄλλων καθίσταιντο προθυμίᾳ τοῦ στασιάζειν ἐπ᾽ αὐτὸν ἀγαγεῖν. [216] ἐπὶ τούτῳ οἱ στασιῶται τῶν ἐξηγητῶν καὶ τὸ πλῆθος ἐξηγρίωσε βοῇ καὶ διακελευσμῷ χρώμενοι ὥρμησάν τε ἐπὶ τοὺς στρατιώτας καὶ περιστάντες λεύουσιν τοὺς πλείστους αὐτῶν. ὀλίγοι δέ τινες καὶ ὁ χιλίαρχος τραυματίαι διέφυγον. καὶ τοῖς μὲν ταῦτα πράξασιν διὰ χειρῶν αὖθις ἡ θυσία ἦν: [217] Ἀρχελάῳ δὲ ἄπορον ἐδόκει σώζεσθαι τὰ πάντα μὴ οὐκ ἀνακόψειν τὴν ἐπὶ τοιοῖσδε ὁρμὴν τῆς πληθύος, ἐκπέμπει δὲ πᾶν τὸ στρατόπεδον * οἳ τούς τε αὐτόθι ἐσκηνωκότας κωλύοιεν τοῖς κατὰ τὸ ἱερὸν βοηθεῖν καὶ τοὺς ἐκπίπτοντας ὑπὸ τῶν πεζῶν δέχοιντο ἀντειλῆφθαι τἀσφαλοῦς ἤδη πεπιστευκότας. [218] καὶ εἰς μὲν τρισχιλίους ἄνδρας ἔκτειναν οἱ ἱππεῖς: τὸ δὲ λοιπὸν ᾤχετο ἐπὶ ὄρη τὰ πλησίον ἰόντες. ἐκήρυσσε δ᾽ Ἀρχέλαος ἀναχωρεῖν ἐπὶ τὰ αὑτῶν πᾶσιν. οἱ δὲ ἀπῄεσαν τὴν ἑορτὴν καταλιπόντες φόβῳ κακοῦ μείζονος καίπερ θρασεῖς ὄντες διὰ τὸ ἀπαίδευτον. [219] Ἀρχέλαος δ᾽ ἐπὶ θαλάσσης κατῄει μετὰ τῆς μητρὸς Νικόλαον καὶ Πτολεμαῖον καὶ Πτόλλαν τῶν φίλων ἐπαγόμενος, Φιλίππῳ τἀδελφῷ τὰ πάντα ἐφεὶς καθίστασθαι τοῦ οἴκου καὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς. [220] συνεξῄει δ᾽ αὐτῷ καὶ Σαλώμη ἡ Ἡρώδου ἀδελφὴ γενεὰν ἀγομένη τὴν αὐτῆς, πολλοί τε τῶν συγγενῶν, λόγῳ μὲν ὡς συναγωνιούμενοι τῷ Ἀρχελάῳ ἐπὶ κτήσει τῆς βασιλείας, ἔργῳ δὲ ἀντιπράξοντες καὶ μάλιστα περὶ τῶν πεπραγμένων ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ ποιησόμενοι καταβοάς. [221] ὑπαντιάζει δ᾽ ἐν Καισαρείᾳ τὸν Ἀρχέλαον Σαβῖνος Καίσαρος ἐπίτροπος τῶν ἐν Συρίᾳ πραγμάτων εἰς Ἰουδαίαν ὡρμημένος ἐπὶ φυλακῇ τῶν Ἡρώδου χρημάτων. καὶ αὐτὸν τῆς ἐπὶ τοῖσδε ὁρμῆς ἔσχεν ὁ Οὔαρος παρελθών: διὰ γὰρ Πτολεμαίου μετάπεμπτος ὑπ᾽ Ἀρχελάου παρῆν. [222] καὶ Οὐάρῳ Σαβῖνος χαριζόμενος οὔτε τὰς ἄκρας, ὅσαι ἐν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις ἦσαν, παρέλαβεν οὔτε τοὺς θησαυροὺς κατεσημήνατο, εἴα δ᾽ ἔχειν Ἀρχέλαον μέχρι Καίσαρι δόξειέν τι περὶ αὐτῶν, καὶ ἔμενεν ἐν τῇ Καισαρείᾳ τοῦθ᾽ ὑποσχόμενος. ἐπεὶ δ᾽ ἐκπλεῖ μὲν ἐπὶ τῆς Ῥώμης Ἀρχέλαος, Οὐάρῳ δ᾽ ἐπ᾽ Ἀντιοχείας ἐγένοντο κομιδαί, Σαβῖνος ἐπὶ Ἱεροσολύμων χωρήσας παραλαμβάνει τὰ βασίλεια. [223] μεταπέμψας δὲ τοὺς φρουράρχους καὶ ὁπόσοι διοικηταὶ τῶν πραγμάτων ἦσαν λόγους τε ἀπαιτεῖν πρόδηλος ἦν καὶ τὰς ἄκρας καθίστατο ᾗ αὐτῷ δοκοῖ. οὐ μὴν οἱ φύλακες ἐν ὀλίγῳ τὰς Ἀρχελάου ἐπιστολὰς ἐποιοῦντο, ἀλλ᾽ ἔμενον σώζοντες τὰ πάντα ᾗ προσετέτακτο αὐτοῖς. Καίσαρι δὲ φυλάσσειν ἕκαστ᾽ ἦν προσποίησις αὐτοῖς. [224] Πλεῖ δὲ κατὰ τοῦτον τὸν καιρὸν ἐπὶ Ῥώμης καὶ Ἀντίπας Ἡρώδου μὲν παῖς, ἐπὶ δ᾽ ἀντιποιήσει τῆς ἀρχῆς ὑποσχέσεσι Σαλώμης ἠρμένος ἐπὶ τῷ ἄρχειν καὶ πολὺ δικαιότερον Ἀρχελάου παραλήψεσθαι τὰ πράγματα ἠξιωκὼς τῷ κατὰ τὰς προτέρας διαθήκας βασιλεὺς ἀποπεφάνθαι, ἃς ἀσφαλεστέρας εἶναι τῶν ἐπιγραφεισῶν. [225] ἐπήγετο δὲ οὗτος τήν τε μητέρα καὶ τὸν ἀδελφὸν τὸν Νικολάου Πτολεμαῖον φίλον τε Ἡρώδῃ τιμιώτατον γεγενημένον καὶ αὐτῷ προσκείμενον. [226] μάλιστα δὲ αὐτὸν ἐνῆγεν ἐπ᾽ ἀντιποιήσει τῆς βασιλείας φρονεῖν Εἰρηναῖος ῥήτωρ ἀνὴρ καὶ δόξῃ δεινότητος τῆς περὶ αὐτῷ τὴν βασιλείαν πεπιστευμένος. διὸ δὴ καὶ τῶν κελευόντων εἴκειν Ἀρχελάῳ πρεσβυτέρῳ τε ὄντι κἀν ταῖς ἐπιδιαθήκαις ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐγγεγραμμένῳ βασιλεῖ οὐκ ἠνείχετο. [227] ἐπεὶ δ᾽ εἰς τὴν Ῥώμην ἀφίκετο, καὶ πάντων τῶν συγγενῶν ἀπόστασις ἦν πρὸς αὐτόν, οὐκ εὐνοίᾳ τῇ ἐκείνου, μίσει δὲ τῷ πρὸς Ἀρχέλαον, μάλιστα μὲν ἐπιθυμοῦντες ἐλευθερίας καὶ ὑπὸ Ῥωμαίων στρατηγῷ τετάχθαι, εἰ δ᾽ ἄρα τι ἀντισταίη, λυσιτελέστερον Ἀρχελάου τὸν Ἀντίπαν λογιζόμενοι, συνέπραττον Ἀντίπᾳ τὴν βασιλείαν. καὶ Σαβῖνος κατηγόρει παρὰ Καίσαρι τοῦ Ἀρχελάου διὰ γραμμάτων. [228] Καῖσαρ δὲ Ἀρχελάου τε εἰσπέμψαντος ὡς αὐτὸν γράμματα, ἐν οἷς τὰ δικαιώματα προετίθει τε αὐτοῦ καὶ τὴν διαθήκην τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοὺς λογισμοὺς τῶν Ἡρώδου χρημάτων σὺν τῷ σημαντῆρι κομίζοντα Πτολεμαῖον, ἐκαραδόκει τὸ μέλλον. [229] ὁ δὲ ταῦτά τε ἀναγνοὺς τὰ γράμματα καὶ τὰς Οὐάρου καὶ Σαβίνου ἐπιστολὰς ὁπόσα τε χρήματα ἦν καὶ τί ἐπ᾽ ἔτος ἐφοίτα καὶ ὅσα Ἀντίπας ἐπ᾽ οἰκειώσει τῆς βασιλείας ἐπεπόμφει γράμματα συνῆγεν ἐπὶ παροκωχῇ γνωμῶν τοὺς φίλους, σὺν οἷς καὶ Γάιον τὸν Ἀγρίππου μὲν καὶ Ἰουλίας τῆς αὐτοῦ θυγατρὸς υἱὸν ποιητὸν δὲ αὐτῷ γεγονότα πρῶτόν τε καθεδούμενον παρέλαβε, καὶ κελεύει λέγειν τοῖς βουλομένοις περὶ τῶν ἐνεστηκότων. [230] καὶ πρῶτος ὁ Σαλώμης υἱὸς Ἀντίπατρος δεινότατός τε ὢν εἰπεῖν καὶ τῷ Ἀρχελάῳ ἐναντιώτατος ἔλεγεν Ἀρχελάῳ παιδιὰν τὸν περὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς εἶναι λόγον ἔργῳ τὴν δύναμιν αὐτῆς πρότερον ἢ Καίσαρα συγχωρῆσαι παρειληφότι, ἐπικαλῶν τὰ τετολμημένα ἐπὶ τοῖς ἀπολωλόσι κατὰ τὴν ἑορτήν: [231] ὧν καὶ ἀδικούντων ἄλλως ἔσχεν τὴν τιμωρίαν εἰς τοὺς ἔξω χρῆσθαι δυναμένους ἀνακειμένην εἶναι, καὶ μὴ ὑπ᾽ ἀνδρὸς πεπρᾶχθαι, εἰ μὲν βασιλέως, ἀδικοῦντος τὸ Καίσαρος διαγνοίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ ἔτι χρώμενον, εἰ δὲ ἰδιώτου, πολὺ χειρόνως, διὰ τὸ μὴ βασιλείας ἀντιποιουμένῳ καλῶς ἂν συγκεχωρῆσθαι, διὰ τὸ Καίσαρα τῆς ἐπ᾽ αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίας ἀφαιρεῖσθαι. [232] καθήπτετο δὲ αὐτοῦ ἡγεμόνων τινῶν ἐν τῷ στρατιωτικῷ μετάστασιν ἐπικαλῶν καὶ προκάθισιν ἐπὶ θρόνου βασιλείου καὶ δικῶν διάλυσιν ὡς ὑπὸ βασιλέως γενομένην κατανεύσεις τε αἰτήσεων τοῖς δημοσίᾳ αἰτουμένοις καὶ πάντων διάπραξιν, ὧν οὐδὲν ἂν μειζόνως ἐπινοῆσαι καθεσταμένον ὑπὸ τοῦ Καίσαρος εἰς τὴν ἀρχήν. [233] ἀνετίθει δὲ αὐτῷ καὶ τῶν ἐκ τοῦ ἱπποδρόμου δεσμωτῶν τὴν ἄφεσιν καὶ πολλὰ τὰ μὲν γεγονότα τὰ δὲ καὶ πιστεύεσθαι δυνάμενα διὰ τὸ φύσιν ἔχειν γίνεσθαι ὑπό τε νεωτέρων καὶ φιλοτιμίᾳ τοῦ ἄρχειν προλαμβανόντων τὴν ἐξουσίαν, πένθους τε τοῦ ἐπὶ τῷ πατρὶ ἀμελείας καὶ κωμασμοὺς αὐτονυκτὶ τῇ ἐκείνου τελευτῇ γεγονότας, [234] ἐφ᾽ οἷς δὴ καὶ τὴν πληθὺν ἀρχὴν τοῦ στασιάζειν λαβεῖν, εἰ τοιαῦτα εὐεργετήσαντος αὐτὸ τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ οὕτως μεγάλων ἠξιωκότος τοιοῖσδε ἀμείβεσθαι τὸν νέκυν, ὥσπερ ἐπὶ σκηνῆς δακρύειν μὲν προσποιούμενον τὰς ἡμέρας, ἀπολαύοντα δὲ ἡδονῇ τῇ ἐπὶ τῆς ἀρχῆς ὅσαι νύκτες. [235] φανεῖσθαί τε καὶ περὶ τὸν Καίσαρα τοιόνδε ὄντα Ἀρχέλαον συγχωροῦντα τὴν βασιλείαν, ὁποῖος γένοιτο καὶ περὶ τὸν πατέρα: χορεύειν γὰρ καὶ ᾁδειν ὥσπερ ἐχθροῦ πεσόντος, ἀλλ᾽ οὐκ ἀνδρὸς οὕτως μὲν συγγενοῦς, τηλικαῦτα δ᾽ εὐεργετεῖν ἐξηγμένου. [236] δεινότατόν τε πάντων ἀπέφηνε τὸ νῦν ἥκειν ἐπὶ Καίσαρος κατανεύσει τῇ ἐκείνου χρησόμενον τῇ βασιλείᾳ πάντων αὐτῷ προπεποιημένων, ὁπόσα γένοιτο ἂν ὑπὸ σοῦ βεβαίως ἤδη τοῦ αὐτοκράτορος παρεσχηκότος πρασσόμενα. [237] μάλιστα δὲ τὴν σφαγὴν τῶν περὶ τὸ ἱερὸν ἐδείνου τῷ λόγῳ καὶ τὴν δυσσέβειαν, ὡς ἑορτῆς τε ἐνεστηκυίας καὶ ἱερείων ἐν τρόπῳ σφαχθεῖεν ἔνιοι μὲν ξένοι οἱ δὲ ἐγχώριοι, πλησθείη δὲ τὸ ἱερὸν νεκρῶν οὐχ ὑπ᾽ ἀλλοφύλου, ἀλλὰ τοῦ καὶ μετὰ νομίμων ὀνομάτων τῆς βασιλείας ἐφιεμένου τῆς πράξεως, ὅπως δυνηθείη πληρῶσαι τῆς φύσει τυραννίδος τὴν πᾶσιν ἀνθρώποις μεμισημένην ἀδικίαν. [238] δι᾽ ἣν μηδὲ ὄναρ ποτὲ ἑωρᾶσθαι βασιλείας αὐτῷ τὴν διαδοχὴν ἀρετῇ τοῦ πατρός: ἐπίστασθαι γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὸν τρόπον καί τοι ἐχθρὸν αὐτῷ ἐκ τῶν διαθηκῶν ἰσχυρότερον Ἀντιπάτρῳ καθίστασθαι: κληθῆναι γὰρ ὑπὸ τοῦ πατρὸς ἐπὶ τὴν βασιλείαν οὐχὶ νοσοῦντος πρὸς τῷ σώματι καὶ τὴν ψυχήν, ἀλλὰ ἀκραιφνεῖ μὲν τῷ λογισμῷ χρωμένου, ἀλκῇ δὲ σώματος τοῖς πράγμασιν ἐφεστηκότος. [239] εἰ δὲ καὶ πρότερον εἰς αὐτὸν ἐπίσης τοῖς νῦν διατεθεῖσθαι τὸν πατέρα, ἀποπεφάνθαι ποταπὸς ἂν γένοιτο βασιλεὺς τὸν μὲν κύριον παρασχεῖν τὴν βασιλείαν Καίσαρα ἀφῃρημένον τοῦ δοῦναι τὴν ἐξουσίαν, τοὺς δὲ πολίτας ἰδιώτην ὄντα ἀκμὴν σφάζειν ἐν ἱερῷ μὴ ἀποτετραμμένον. [240] Καὶ Ἀντίπατρος μὲν τοιάδε εἰπὼν καὶ μαρτύρων παραστάσεσιν τὰ εἰρημένα κρατυνάμενος πολλοῖς τῶν συγγενῶν παύεται τοῦ λέγειν. ἀνίσταται δὲ Νικόλαος ὑπὲρ Ἀρχελάου καὶ ἔλεγεν τὰ μὲν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ γνώμῃ τῶν πεπονθότων ἀναθεὶς μᾶλλον ἢ ἐξουσίᾳ τῇ Ἀρχελάου: τοὺς γὰρ ἐπὶ τοιοῖσδε ἄρχοντας οὐ μόνον τῷ καθ᾽ αὑτοὺς ὑβρίζοντι εἶναι πονηρούς, ἀλλὰ καὶ τῷ ἀναγκάζοντι εἰς τὴν ἄμυναν τῶν εὐγνωμονεῖν προαιρουμένων. [241] ὡς δὲ πολέμια ἔδρων λόγῳ μὲν κατ᾽ Ἀρχελάου τὸ δὲ ἀληθὲς εἰς Καίσαρα φανερὸν εἶναι: τοὺς γὰρ ὑβριοῦντας κωλυτὰς παραγενομένους ἢ ὑπ᾽ Ἀρχελάου πεπομφότος κτεῖναι ἐπιθεμένους οὔτε τοῦ θεοῦ οὔτε τοῦ νόμου τῆς ἑορτῆς ἐν φροντίδι γενομένους, [242] ὧν Ἀντίπατρον οὐκ αἰσχύνεσθαι ἐκδικητὴν καθιστάμενον ἐπὶ θεραπείᾳ ἔχθρας τῆς αὐτοῦ πρὸς Ἀρχέλαον ἢ φύσει τοῦ ἀρετῇ δικαίου. οἱ παρελθόντες καὶ μὴ πρὸς διανοουμένους ἄρχοντες ἀδίκων ἔργων, οἵδε εἰσὶν οἱ βιαζόμενοι καὶ μὴ θέλοντας τοὺς ἀμυνομένους ἐφ᾽ ὅπλα χωρεῖν. [243] ἀνετίθει δὲ καὶ τὰ λοιπὰ πᾶσι τοῖς ἐν βουλῇ τῶν κατηγόρων: οὐδὲν γὰρ ὅ τι μὴ οὐ μετὰ γνώμης τῆς αὐτῶν γεγενημένον αἰτίᾳ τοῦ ἀδικεῖν ὑπάγεσθαι, οὐ τῇ φύσει τῇ οὕτως αὐτὰ γεγονότα πονηρὰ εἶναι, ἀλλὰ τῷ βλάψειν ἂν δοκεῖν Ἀρχέλαον. τοσήνδε αὐτοῖς εἶναι βουλὴν τοῦ ὑβριοῦντος εἰς ἄνδρα συγγενῆ, καὶ πατρὸς μὲν εὐεργέτου, συνήθη δὲ αὐτοῖς καὶ διὰ παντὸς οἰκείως πεπολιτευμένον. [244] τάς γε μὴν διαθήκας ὑπό τε σωφρονοῦντος γεγράφθαι τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ κυριωτέρας τῶν γεγραμμένων πρότερον διὰ τὸ Καίσαρι δεσπότῃ τῶν ὅλων καταλελεῖφθαι τὴν κρίσιν τῶν ἐν αὐταῖς γεγραμμένων. [245] μιμήσεσθαί τε οὐδαμῶς Καίσαρα τὴν ὕβριν αὐτῶν, οἳ τῆς Ἡρώδου παντοίως ἀπολαύσαντες παρ᾽ ὃν ἔζη καιρὸν δυνάμεως τὰ πάντα ἐπὶ ὕβρει γνώμης ἐπείγοιντο αὐτοῦ, οὐδ᾽ αὐτῶν περὶ τὸν συγγενῆ τοιούτων γεγονότων. [246] οὔκουν Καίσαρά γε ἀνδρὸς ἐπ᾽ αὐτῷ πεποιημένου τὰ πάντα καὶ φίλου καὶ συμμάχου καταλύσειν τὰς διαθήκας ἐπὶ πίστει τῇ αὐτοῦ γεγραμμένας, οὐδὲ μιμήσεσθαι κακίαν τὴν ἐκείνων τὴν Καίσαρος ἀρετὴν καὶ πίστιν πρὸς ἅπασαν τὴν οἰκουμένην ἀνενδοίαστον γενομένην, [247] καὶ μανίαν καὶ λογισμῶν ἔκστασιν κατακρίνειν ἀνδρὸς βασιλέως, υἱεῖ μὲν ἀγαθῷ τὴν διαδοχὴν καταλελοιπότος, πίστει δὲ τῇ αὐτοῦ προσπεφευγότος: οὔτ᾽ ἁμαρτάνειν Ἡρώδην ποτὲ περὶ κρίσιν τοῦ διαδόχου σωφροσύνῃ κεχρημένον ἐπὶ τῇ Καίσαρος γνώμῃ τὰ πάντα ποιεῖσθαι. [248] Καὶ Νικόλαος μὲν τοιάδε διελθὼν καταπαύει τὸν λόγον: Καῖσαρ δὲ Ἀρχέλαον προσπεσόντα αὐτῷ πρὸς τὰ γόνατα φιλοφρόνως τε ἀνίστη φάμενος ἀξιώτατον εἶναι τῆς βασιλείας πολλήν τε ἀπέφαινε τροπὴν γνώμης τῆς αὐτοῦ οὐκ ἄλλα πράξειν, ἀλλ᾽ ὁπόσα αἵ τε διαθῆκαι ὑπηγόρευον καὶ Ἀρχελάῳ συνέφερεν. [249] οὐ μέντοι γε ἐκεκύρωτο οὐδέν, ὡς ἂν ἐχεγγύῳ παραδείγματι χρώμενον ἐπ᾽ ἀδείας Ἀρχέλαον εἶναι. καὶ διαλύσεως τῶν ἀνδρῶν γενομένης ἐσκοπεῖτο καθ᾽ αὑτόν, εἴτε Ἀρχελάῳ τὴν βασιλείαν ἐπικυρωτέον, εἴτε νομὴν αὐτῆς ποιεῖσθαι παντὶ τῷ Ἡρώδου γένει καὶ ταῦτα πάντων πολλῆς ἐπικουρίας δεομένων.

english.html:
<tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-9-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="206"><tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num206" xml:id="english-book17-num206" id="english-book17-num206" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="16" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[206]</tei-num> AT this time also it was that some of the Jews got together out of a desire of innovation. They lamented Matthias, and those that were slain with him by Herod, who had not any respect paid them by a funeral mourning, out of the fear men were in of that man; they were those who had been condemned for pulling down the golden eagle. The people made a great clamor and lamentation hereupon, and cast out some reproaches against the king also, as if that tended to alleviate the miseries of the deceased. The people assembled together, and desired of Archelaus, that, in way of revenge on their account, he would inflict punishment on those who had been honored by Herod; and that, in the first and principal place, he would deprive that high priest whom Herod had made, and would choose one more agreeable to the law, and of greater purity, to officiate as high priest. This was granted by Archelaus, although he was mightily offended at their importunity, because he proposed to himself to go to Rome immediately to look after Caesar's determination about him. However, he sent the general of his forces to use persuasions, and to tell them that the death which was inflicted on their friends was according to the law; and to represent to them that their petitions about these things were carried to a great height of injury to him; that the time was not now proper for such petitions, but required their unanimity until such time as he should be established in the government by the consent of Caesar, and should then be come back to them; for that he would then consult with them in common concerning the purport of their petitions; but that they ought at present to be quiet, lest they should seem seditious persons.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num210" xml:id="english-book17-num210" id="english-book17-num210" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[210]</tei-num> So when the king had suggested these things, and instructed his general in what he was to say, be sent him away to the people; but they made a clamor, and would not give him leave to speak, and put him in danger of his life, and as many more as were desirous to venture upon saying openly any thing which might reduce them to a sober mind, and prevent their going on in their present courses, because they had more concern to have all their own wills performed than to yield obedience to their governors; thinking it to be a thing insufferable, that, while Herod was alive, they should lose those that were most dear to them, and that when he was dead, they could not get the actors to be punished. So they went on with their designs after a violent manner, and thought all to be lawful and right which tended to please them, and being unskillful in foreseeing what dangers they incurred; and when they had suspicion of such a thing, yet did the present pleasure they took in the punishment of those they deemed their enemies overweigh all such considerations; and although Archelaus sent many to speak to them, yet they treated them not as messengers sent by him, but as persons that came of their own accord to mitigate their anger, and would not let one of them speak. The sedition also was made by such as were in a great passion; and it was evident that they were proceeding further in seditious practices, by the multitude running so fast upon them.</tei-p>
					<tei-p sameas="#latin-book17-num213" xml:id="english-book17-num213" id="english-book17-num213" data-origname="p" data-processed=""><tei-num data-origname="num" data-processed="">[213]</tei-num> Now, upon the approach of that feast of unleavened bread, which the law of their fathers had appointed for the Jews at this time, which feast is called the Passover and is a memorial of their deliverance out of Egypt, when they offer sacrifices with great alacrity; and when they are required to slay more sacrifices in number than at any other festival; and when an innumerable multitude came thither out of the country, nay, from beyond its limits also, in order to worship God, the seditious lamented Judas and Matthias, those teachers of the laws, and kept together in the temple, and had plenty of food, because these seditious persons were not ashamed to beg it. And as Archelaus was afraid lest some terrible thing should spring up by means of these men's madness, he sent a regiment of armed men, and with them a captain of a thousand, to suppress the violent efforts of the seditious before the whole multitude should be infected with the like madness; and gave them this charge, that if they found any much more openly seditious than others, and more busy in tumultuous practices, they should bring them to him. But those that were seditious on account of those teachers of the law, irritated the people by the noise and clamors they used to encourage the people in their designs; so they made an assault upon the soldiers, and came up to them, and stoned the greatest part of them, although some of them ran away wounded, and their captain among them; and when they had thus done, they returned to the sacrifices which were already in their hands. Now Archelaus thought there was no way to preserve the entire government but by cutting off those who made this attempt upon it; so he sent out the whole army upon them, and sent the horsemen to prevent those that had their tents without the temple from assisting those that were within the temple, and to kill such as ran away from the footmen when they thought themselves out of danger; which horsemen slew three thousand men, while the rest went to the neighboring mountains. Then did Archelaus order proclamation to be made to them all, that they should retire to their own homes; so they went away, and left the festival, out of fear of somewhat worse which would follow, although they had been so bold by reason of their want of instruction. So Archelaus went down to the sea with his mother, and took with him Nicolaus and Ptolemy, and many others of his friends, and left Philip his brother as governor of all things belonging both to his own family and to the public. There went out also with him Salome, Herod's sister who took with her, her children, and many of her kindred were with her; which kindred of hers went, as they pretended, to assist Archelaus in gaining the kingdom, but in reality to oppose him, and chiefly to make loud complaints of what he had done in the temple. But Sabinus, Caesar's steward for Syrian affairs, as he was making haste into Judea to preserve Herod's effects, met with Archclaus at Caesarea; but Varus (president of Syria) came at that time, and restrained him from meddling with them, for he was there as sent for by Archceaus, by the means of Ptolemy. They lamented Matthias, and those that were slain with him by Herod, who had not any respect paid them by a funeral mourning, out of the fear men were in of that man; they were those who had been condemned for pulling down the golden eagle. The people made a great clamor and lamentation hereupon, and cast out some reproaches against the king also, as if that tended to alleviate the miseries of the deceased. The people assembled together, and desired of Archelaus, that, in way of revenge on their account, he would inflict punishment on those who had been honored by Herod; and that, in the first and principal place, he would deprive that high priest whom Herod had made, and would choose one more agreeable to the law, and of greater purity, to officiate as high priest. This was granted by Archelaus, although he was mightily offended at their importunity, because he proposed to himself to go to Rome immediately to look after Caesar's determination about him. However, he sent the general of his forces to use persuasions, and to tell them that the death which was inflicted on their friends was according to the law; and to represent to them that their petitions about these things were carried to a great height of injury to him; that the time was not now proper for such petitions, but required their unanimity until such time as he should be established in the government by the consent of Caesar, and should then be come back to them; for that he would then consult with them in common concerning the purport of their petitions; but that they ought at present to be quiet, lest they should seem seditious persons. So they went on with their designs after a violent manner, and thought all to be lawful and right which tended to please them, and being unskillful in foreseeing what dangers they incurred; and when they had suspicion of such a thing, yet did the present pleasure they took in the punishment of those they deemed their enemies overweigh all such considerations; and although Archelaus sent many to speak to them, yet they treated them not as messengers sent by him, but as persons that came of their own accord to mitigate their anger, and would not let one of them speak. <tei-div type="chapter" data-structural-identity="LOEB-17-Chapter-10-0" data-verification-status="CONFIRMED_NIESE_START" data-canonical-niese="250"><tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num250" id="latin-book17-num250" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Interae mater archelai morbo pregrauata defungitur. Sed etiam auaro qui in syria militiae magister erat litterae ueniunt significantes seditiones decessionesque iudaeorum. Postquam enim archelaus nauigauerat cuncta gens uariis motibus fuerat tumultuacionibusque uariis motibus fuerat tumultuacionibusque<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>turbata, sed uarus adueniens eos qui causa, adegit. Rebusque conpositis, in antiochiam repedabat, unum ordinem militum in hierosolimis derelinquens qui iudaeis si forte aliquid seditionis molirentur obuiamirent, sed nec sic tamen seditio terminatur. Nam post quam uarus abscessit, sabinus curator caesaris illic remanens iudaeos coepit opprimere ex militia sibi multos armigeros faciens quorum satel licio aduersus iudeos affligendos utebatur unde illi pertubati ad seditiones exitatas neces sesitate cogebantur. <tei-milestone unit="chapter" n="18" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed="" hidden=""></tei-milestone>XVIII Sed etiam arces uiolenter obtinuerat et thesauros regios scrutatus sumpserat lucrorum et rapinarum cupidine concitatus</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num254" id="latin-book17-num254" data-origname="p" data-processed="">inminente igitur pentecosten, festiuitas namque apud nos paternaliter apellatur non tantum ergo religionis gratia quantum indignatione succensi propter inprobitatem et inpressionem sabini, multa milia congregata sunt hominum galileorum et hierichuntinorum in mensa multitudo, et quotquot transiordanem fluuium habitabant, sed etiam incolarum magna manus ad unata qui plus aliis incensi in ultionem sabini conspirauerant. In tres itaque partes diuisi diuersa loca occupant. Et una quidem pars ypodromo tenuerat, ceterarum uero duarum altera pars ab aquilone ad austrum uersa circa templum erat altera uero adorientum loca posita detinebat. Tertia uero uero pars in ipodromum sicut diximus ad occidentem occupauerat, quo loco etiam aula regalis extabat. Erat autem illis tota festinatio ut romanos inclusos obsessosque constringerent, sed sabinus timens tam etiam multitudinem eorum quam nobilitatem ingenii quippe quibus mors contemptui erat dum modo cepta perficerent, confestim scribit ad uarum postulans ut quam citissime subueniret, in magno periculo esse cunctam ase ibi militiam derelictam. Nam sequoque copiam illis exeundi si id eligerent daturos sabino quoque si etiam ipse uellet exeundi tribuere facultatem. Dum ista ageruntur non nulli ex regiis militibus ad iudaeos transeunt. Rufus autem et gratus tria milia pugnatotum ex militia herodis sub se habebant, uiros corporis exercitatos et strenuos. Cum his igitur omnibus sese romanis adiciunt. Rufus etiam equites aliquantos habebat ipsos quoque secum romanis auxilio duxerat. At iudaei obsidionem minime neglegebant. Sed etiam moenia cuncta circuibant ortabantur omnes ut illam oportunitatem de se saluandi et in libertatem paternam respirandi non perderent. Sabino uero optabile fuit ut egrediens abscederet. Sed committere semet ipsum non audebat suorum consideratione factorum et quod hostes ammodum in fideli mente cognouerat, simul etiam uari presto labatur aduentum eumque si adesset obsidionem illam esse soluturum.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num269" id="latin-book17-num269" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Ea tempestate etiam alia plurima turbis tumultisque plenissima prouenerunt, quae totam iudeae regionem grauiter desola bant. In quibus namque locis alii lucri<tei-milestone n="sbb00000114_00433.jpg" data-origname="milestone" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-milestone><tei-pb n="215r" data-origname="pb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-pb><tei-cb n="1/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>cupidine concitati pars inimicitia iudaeorum ad excitanda bella fere militauerat quondam herodis duo milia hominum hinc inde congregatorum hii ergo in unum colecti et seorsum aceteris decedentes aduersus regios milites pugna congrediuntur. Vtebantur autem alicibia deduce herodis nepotem quem sibi praefecerant, qui tam in campis ad pugnam strenue ferebatur quam in locis asperis arte praeualebat propter experientiam quam ex usu belli perceperat.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num271" id="latin-book17-num271" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Iudas quidam erat filius ezechiae praepositi latronum qui multum quondam praeualuerat, sed temporibus herodis cum magno fuerat labore deprehensus. Iste igitur iudas circa se forim galileae congregans multitudinem uiuorum perditorum atque disperatorum, cum eis ad aulam regiam pugnabundus inuadit Ex qua copiam armorum quantum cumque ille locus habebat abripuit, ex inde suos omnes armat, fumit etiam cunctas opes quae ibidem pro custodia fuerant derelicte, hic terribilis uniuersis effectus est nam huc atque illuc agebat et ducebat et ductabat exercitum libine rei maioris accensus et emulatione regnandi sine ulla uirtute ullaque prudentia, sed ad uim in ferendam tantum et ledendus pronior et prodiuus extabat. Sperans ex hoc sibi dignitatem gloriamque uenturam.</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num273" id="latin-book17-num273" data-origname="p" data-processed="">Extiterat quoque symon seruus quidam herodis regis uerum decorus uir magnitudine corporis ac fortitudine prestans cui magna fuerant credita commissaque negotia. Is igitur rerum in temperantia sub leuatus, dia dema suo capiti presumpsit in ponere et aliquanta multitudine congregata rex pronuntiatur, insania simul furiaque populorum, sed etiam ipse dignum semet ipsum existimans super omnes qui regnum ante gessissent aulam regiam in hierichunte succendit et omnia quae ibi habebantur adripuit. Multa quoque indiuersis locis per uniuersam prouintiam ubi regia consistebant taberna<tei-cb n="2/2" data-origname="cb" data-empty="" data-processed=""></tei-cb>cula conburebat, cunctaque exterminio dabat ignibus concremando. Ampliora quoque iste generet et amplius ab eo illa regio deleretur ni caeleriter mutatio contigisset, nam exercitus militum regionum qui se romanis addiderant tota manu totaque uirtute congredi ent occurrit, simon ibi multa VI die long certatur, sed plures qui ex locis transiordanem cum symone fuerant congregati neque ordinis neque dispositionis bellicae gnari. Siquidem temeritate magis quam disciplina pugnabant a regiis occubuere militibus sed etiam semet ipsum symonem fugase et permon tis fauces saluare cupientem gratus occurens capud ei abscidit. Incensus est etiam illis diebus super iordanem locus nomine e machoes a quibusdam hominibus simoni consimilibus. Sic igitur in illa gente multa dementia uagabatur propter quod regem proprium non habebat qui populum uirtute ac moderatione disponeret et propter alienigene inruperant per quos seditiose mentes occasione accipientes ad bella concitanda succensesunt Intentione sola deuastandi et aliena rapiendi ceterum</tei-p>
					<tei-p xml:id="latin-book17-num278" id="latin-book17-num278" data-origname="p" data-processed="">et athonges uir neque generis dignitate conspicuus neque uirtute decoratus, sed opum tantum confisus abundantia pastor enim erat iste et cunctis in omnibus rebus obscurus. Verum magnitudine corporis et robore preualens ausus est etiam ipse in regni conspirare potentiam erant quippe illi fratres quattuor etiam ipsi corpore et magnum de fortitudine gloriantes, et ex hoc credebant sese regnum modis omnibus optinere. Nam unus quisque eorum turmam propiram ductabat congregatur itaque ad eos plurima multitudo. Et illi quidem ductorum fungebantur officio et sicubi opus erat discurrebant bellicos exercendo conflictus. Ille uero diadema suo capiti circumponens ad consultandum concilium conuocabat, ut quid facto opus esset decerneret.
